rows.title: Apply for Tax File Number (TFN)
rows.description: A Tax File Number (TFN) is a unique 9-digit number issued by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) to identify you for tax purposes. Permanent migrants, temporary residents with work rights, and new arrivals must apply for a TFN as soon as possible after arriving. Applications are free and can be submitted online (for those with a myGovID/Digital ID), via Australia Post in person (for most migrants and temporary visa holders), or by paper form. Processing typically takes up to 28 days. Without a TFN, your employer is legally required to withhold tax from your pay at the top marginal rate (47%), so applying immediately upon arrival is strongly advisable.
required_documents: proof of residential address in Australia (e.g. utility bill or rental lease)
rows.where_to_go: Online at ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/tax-file-number/apply-for-a-tfn (if you have a Strong Digital ID) or at a participating Australia Post outlet in person
rows.notes: Without a TFN, employers must withhold tax at the top marginal rate (47%). Temporary visa holders with work rights are eligible to apply. Processing takes up to 28 calendar days. Keep your TFN confidential — share it only with your employer, bank, and super fund.
rows.source_quote: It is free to apply. Permanent migrants and temporary visitors located in Australia with a valid work rights visa apply for a TFN.

rows.title: Enrol in Medicare (if eligible)
rows.description: Medicare is Australia's universal public health care system, providing subsidised or free access to medical services, GPs, specialists, and public hospital care. Permanent residents and Australian citizens are eligible. Temporary residents from countries with a Reciprocal Health Care Agreement (RHCA) — including the United Kingdom, Ireland, New Zealand, Italy, Netherlands, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Belgium, Malta, and Slovenia — are also eligible for limited Medicare cover. To enrol, visit a Services Australia service centre in person with your passport, visa documentation, and proof of address. You will receive a Medicare card within 2–4 weeks; interim cover can often be confirmed immediately. Medicare is free; no premium is payable (though a Medicare Levy of 2% applies to your taxable income at tax time).
required_documents: visa grant notice or ImmiCard or permanent resident evidence
rows.where_to_go: Services Australia service centre in person. Find nearest at servicesaustralia.gov.au or call 132 011
rows.notes: Countries with RHCA (as of 2024): UK, Republic of Ireland, New Zealand, Italy, Netherlands, Sweden, Finland, Norway, Belgium, Malta, Slovenia — 11 countries total. Visitors from these countries get cover for medically necessary treatment only, not elective care. Those without RHCA should obtain private health insurance before or immediately on arrival. The Medicare Levy (2% of taxable income) is collected via annual tax return, not a direct premium.
rows.source_quote: Agreements with 11 countries that covers the cost of medically necessary care when Australians visit certain countries and visitors from these countries visit Australia.

rows.title: Arrange Private Health Insurance (if not Medicare-eligible)
rows.description: Employees who are not eligible for Medicare (i.e., temporary visa holders from non-RHCA countries) must arrange private health insurance immediately upon arrival to cover hospital, specialist, and ancillary health costs. Without Medicare or private cover, full out-of-pocket costs for healthcare can be substantial (emergency department visits can cost AUD 500–5,000+). Major providers include Medibank, Bupa, HCF, NIB, AHM, and CBHS. Comprehensive hospital cover starts from approximately AUD 100–200 per month for a single adult. Many employer relocation packages include a health insurance allowance — check your employment contract. Always confirm your visa type's health cover requirements; some visa classes (e.g. student visas) mandate Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) rather than standard private health insurance.
rows.where_to_go: Online via insurer websites (medibank.com.au, bupa.com.au, hcf.com.au, nib.com.au) or through employer HR if covered by package
rows.notes: Cost estimate is approximately AUD 100–150/month (single adult, hospital cover) converted to EUR at ~0.60 rate. Some visa subclasses require OVHC (Overseas Visitor Health Cover) or OSHC. Check visa conditions carefully. Private health insurance also confers a Medicare Levy Surcharge exemption for higher-income earners. Waiting periods (up to 12 months for some treatments) may apply — check policy details carefully.
rows.source_quote: Agreements with 11 countries that covers the cost of medically necessary care when Australians visit certain countries and visitors from these countries visit Australia.

rows.title: Create myGov Account and Link Services
rows.description: myGov (my.gov.au) is the Australian Government's secure online portal that provides centralised access to a wide range of government services in one place. Creating a myGov account allows employees to link and access services including: the Australian Taxation Office (ATO), Medicare, Centrelink, Child Support, My Health Record, National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), Department of Veterans' Affairs, and many others. To create an account, visit my.gov.au and register using an email address; identity verification is required. Once created, link relevant services — ATO linkage requires your TFN, Medicare linkage requires your Medicare card number. The myGov app (iOS and Android) provides convenient mobile access. All official government correspondence from linked services is delivered to the secure myGov Inbox.
required_documents: mobile phone number for two-factor authentication
rows.where_to_go: Online at my.gov.au or via the myGov app (available on App Store and Google Play)
rows.notes: myGov is run by Services Australia. You can access multiple government services from a single login. Create your account as soon as you have your TFN and Medicare card, as the ATO and Medicare are the most immediately useful linked services for new arrivals. The myGov Inbox replaces physical mail for most government agencies once services are linked.
rows.source_quote: myGov is a simple and secure way to access government services online in one place. With a myGov account, you can access services from: Australian Taxation Office, Centrelink, Child Support, Medicare, My Health Record, National Disability Insurance Scheme, and others.

rows.title: Open an Australian Bank Account
rows.description: Opening a local bank account is essential for receiving salary payments. Australia's 'Big Four' banks are Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA), ANZ, Westpac, and NAB. Several allow new arrivals to open an account before landing in Australia — CBA, ANZ, and Westpac offer online account opening for international applicants with an Australian visa, with the account activated upon arrival. ING and Macquarie Bank are popular alternatives. Standard documentation required is a passport plus visa grant notice; some banks also require a local residential address once you arrive. Most everyday (transaction) accounts have no monthly fee. To receive salary payments, you will need your BSB (bank branch code) and account number to provide to your employer.
rows.where_to_go: Online (CBA: commbank.com.au, ANZ: anz.com.au, Westpac: westpac.com.au, NAB: nab.com.au, ING: ing.com.au) or in-branch at any major city branch
rows.notes: CBA, ANZ, and Westpac all offer 'new to Australia' or 'migrate to Australia' account opening before arrival. You can open an account online and activate/verify identity in-branch within 3 months of landing. Most accounts are fee-free or have fees waived for the first year. You will need your BSB and account number to give to your employer on your first day. Consider also opening a high-interest savings account (ING, Macquarie Savings) once settled.
rows.source_quote: Open a bank account for new arrivals — documents required: passport and visa.

rows.title: Choose a Superannuation Fund and Provide Details to Employer
rows.description: Superannuation (super) is Australia's mandatory retirement savings system. From 1 July 2026, under the new Payday Super legislation, employers must pay super guarantee contributions into your nominated super fund at each pay cycle (previously quarterly). The super guarantee rate for 2025–26 and 2026–27 is 12% of your ordinary time earnings (note: the rate increased to 12% from 1 July 2025). Most employees in Australia are eligible for super guarantee contributions regardless of their earnings, visa status, or hours worked (temporary residents are also entitled). On starting work, your employer will provide a Superannuation Standard Choice Form — complete this with your chosen fund's details, or the employer will use a default fund. You can choose from industry funds (e.g. AustralianSuper, Hostplus, REST), retail funds (e.g. Colonial First State, MLC), or public sector funds. Your super account is 'stapled' to you when you change jobs — the ATO notifies new employers of your existing fund.
required_documents: TFN (strongly recommended — super taxed at 47% without it)
super fund account number and USI (Unique Superannuation Identifier)
Superannuation Standard Choice Form (provided by employer)
rows.where_to_go: YourSuper comparison tool at ato.gov.au, ASIC Moneysmart (moneysmart.gov.au/superannuation/choosing-a-super-fund), or directly with your chosen super fund
rows.notes: As of 1 July 2026, the Payday Super law requires employers to pay super with each payslip (within 7 business days of payday). The super guarantee rate is 12% of qualifying earnings for 2026-27 (up from 11.5% in 2024-25). Without a TFN provided to your super fund, contributions are taxed at 47% instead of 15%. Temporary visa holders are entitled to super but can claim a Departing Australia Superannuation Payment (DASP) when departing permanently. Employees cannot opt out of super guarantee.
rows.source_quote: Generally, all employees are eligible for super guarantee. It doesn't matter if you're: full time, part time or casual. You're eligible for super guarantee regardless of how much you earn. From 1 July 2026 under the new Payday Super legislation, your employer pays your super guarantee contributions for each payday.

rows.title: Track and Consolidate Superannuation Accounts via ATO Online Services
rows.description: If you have worked in Australia before or have previously had a super account, the ATO may hold super on your behalf ('ATO-held super') or you may have multiple accounts. New arrivals who are starting fresh will have one account, but over time may accumulate multiple. Use ATO Online Services (linked via myGov) to view all your super accounts, track employer contributions, find lost super, and consolidate multiple accounts into a single fund. This avoids paying multiple sets of fees. The ATO provides a 'Super Health Check' tool. When you leave Australia permanently (if you are a temporary visa holder), you can apply for a Departing Australia Superannuation Payment (DASP) via the ATO to have your super balance refunded.
rows.where_to_go: ATO Online Services via myGov at my.gov.au, or ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/growing-and-keeping-track-of-your-super
rows.notes: Temporary residents departing Australia can claim their super via the Departing Australia Superannuation Payment (DASP). DASP is taxed at 35% for the taxed element (or 65% for the untaxed element). New Zealand citizens have different options — they can transfer super to KiwiSaver under the Trans-Tasman Retirement Savings Portability scheme instead of claiming DASP.
rows.source_quote: Use ATO online services to track your super and find any accounts you have forgotten or lost touch with. Transferring or consolidating your super: when and how you can transfer or roll over your super to another fund, and how to consolidate multiple super accounts.

rows.title: Exchange or Obtain Australian Driver's Licence
rows.description: New arrivals in Australia can drive on a valid overseas driver's licence for a limited period (varies by state). After that period, you must either exchange your overseas licence for an Australian state licence or sit for an Australian licence. Rules vary by state and by the country that issued your licence. In New South Wales (NSW), overseas licence holders can drive for 3 months from arrival, after which they must obtain an NSW licence — some countries (e.g. UK, USA, Canada, most EU countries) are eligible for direct licence exchange without a driving test (administrative process only). In Victoria (VIC), overseas licence holders can drive on their overseas licence while it remains valid, but must obtain a Victorian licence to drive after it expires or if they become a permanent resident. In Queensland (QLD), overseas licence holders may drive for 3 months. Similar rules apply in South Australia (SA) and Western Australia (WA). Contact your state's transport authority (VicRoads, Transport for NSW/Service NSW, TMR Queensland, DPTI SA, DOT WA) for the full list of eligible countries and required documents.
required_documents: identity documents (varies by state — may require 100 points of identity)
English translation of licence if not in English
rows.where_to_go: State transport authority: VicRoads (vicroads.vic.gov.au) for VIC; Service NSW (service.nsw.gov.au) for NSW; TMR Queensland (tmr.qld.gov.au) for QLD; DPTI (sa.gov.au/transport) for SA; DOT WA (transport.wa.gov.au) for WA
rows.notes: Cost varies by state (typically AUD 30–80 for a standard 3-year licence, converted to approximately EUR 18–50). Many countries qualify for direct exchange without a driving test — check your specific state's list. If your overseas licence is not from an eligible country, you will need to complete a knowledge test and possibly a driving test. An English translation is required if your licence is in another language. You can continue driving while your overseas licence application is being processed.
rows.source_quote: Convert your overseas licence — Driving with your overseas licence — Convert interstate licence or learner permit.

rows.title: Enrol Children in Australian School
rows.description: Australian children of compulsory school age (6–16 years depending on the state) must be enrolled in school. Australia has a strong public school system administered by state and territory governments. Public (government) school enrolment is zone-based — your child must attend the local school in your residential catchment area, or apply for a different school with a 'placement appeal'. Children of permanent residents and Australian citizens attend public schools free of charge. Temporary visa holders (including most skilled worker visa holders and their families) are required to pay tuition fees at public schools in most states (typically AUD 4,000–13,000 per year per child, depending on the state and year level). International schools and private schools charge higher fees and are open to all visa types. In NSW, enrolment is managed through the NSW Department of Education (education.nsw.gov.au). In VIC, enrolments are handled by the Department of Education (education.vic.gov.au). Always contact the school directly to initiate the enrolment process.
required_documents: proof of residential address (for zone-based public school enrolment)
rows.where_to_go: NSW: education.nsw.gov.au | VIC: education.vic.gov.au | QLD: qed.qld.gov.au | SA: education.sa.gov.au | WA: education.wa.edu.au | Contact local school directly
rows.notes: Public school fees for temporary visa holders vary significantly by state: NSW charges approximately AUD 5,000–6,000/year per child; VIC approximately AUD 4,200–8,500/year. Fees may be covered by your employer's relocation package — check your employment contract. Permanent residents and citizens pay no public school fees. The Australian school year runs February to December (two semesters or four terms). NAPLAN assessments are held for Years 3, 5, 7, and 9. Some states offer selective (academically selective) government schools for high-performing students via a competitive entry exam.
rows.source_name: NSW Department of Education / State Education Departments
rows.source_quote: Schooling — Access info for students, parents and carers including: calendars, school operational status, key initiatives, visitor check-in procedures, and translated documents.

rows.title: Get Australian SIM Card / Mobile Phone Plan
rows.description: Obtaining an Australian mobile number is a practical priority on arrival, as it is required for bank account two-factor authentication, myGov verification, and general communication. Australia's three major network operators are Telstra (largest coverage, especially regional), Optus (strong metro coverage), and Vodafone (metro-focused). Prepaid SIM cards are available at supermarkets (Woolworths, Coles), convenience stores, and major mobile retailers — no ID is required for prepaid. For postpaid (monthly contract) plans, you will need ID (passport) and an Australian address and may need to pass a credit check (which may fail initially for new arrivals without Australian credit history). MVNOs (Mobile Virtual Network Operators) such as Amaysim, Boost Mobile (on Telstra network), Kogan Mobile, and Woolworths Mobile offer competitive prepaid rates. Starter prepaid plans cost AUD 10–30 for 28-day packs with generous data inclusions.
required_documents: Passport and Australian address for postpaid plans
rows.where_to_go: Telstra stores (telstra.com.au), Optus stores (optus.com.au), Woolworths/Coles/7-Eleven for prepaid SIMs, or online via MVNO websites
rows.notes: Cost estimate is approximately AUD 20–30 for a month of prepaid data. For new arrivals, starting with prepaid is strongly recommended — postpaid contracts require credit history. Telstra has the best regional/rural coverage but is generally more expensive. MVNOs on the Telstra network (Boost, Woolworths Mobile) offer the same coverage at lower cost. Australian mobile numbers are 10 digits (04XX XXX XXX format). Port your existing number if desired — porting between Australian carriers is straightforward.
rows.source_quote: Prepaid plans available from major carriers and MVNOs — no strict ID requirements for prepaid SIM cards.

rows.title: Establish Rental History and References for Private Rental Market
rows.description: Renting in Australia can be competitive, especially in major cities like Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, and Perth. Private rental agents and landlords require documentation including proof of income, identity, and — critically — references. New arrivals have no Australian rental history, which can make applications weaker. Strategies to compensate include: providing an employer letter confirming salary and employment; offering 2–4 months' rent in advance (note: legislation caps advance rent in some states); providing overseas landlord references with English translations; offering a higher bond (capped by law in most states at 4 weeks' rent); using corporate accommodation initially while building local history; providing bank statements. The 100-point identity check is standard — passport (70 points) + bank card or utility bill (typically 25 points) gets you close to 100. Real estate agents require a completed application form (typically using the 1form or ignite platform in most states) plus identity documents.
rows.where_to_go: Real estate agents and landlords via realestate.com.au or domain.com.au. Applications via 1form (1form.com) or Ignite/2Apply platform
rows.notes: Bond (security deposit) is capped at 4 weeks' rent in NSW, VIC, and QLD. Some landlords accept 2 weeks advance rent as advance rent (terms vary by state). Corporate serviced apartments are a good short-term option while searching for long-term rentals. realestate.com.au and domain.com.au are the two main property listing platforms. Consider short-term rental (Airbnb, Furnished Finder) for the first 1–4 weeks while attending in-person property inspections (essential — applications without attending inspection are rarely accepted).
rows.source_quote: Apply online with your documents — agents require ID, rental history, employment and income verification.

rows.title: Start Building Australian Credit History
rows.description: New arrivals in Australia begin with a blank Australian credit file — no credit history — which can prevent access to credit cards, car loans, and later, home loans. Australia has three main credit reporting bodies: Equifax Australia, Illion (formerly Dun & Bradstreet), and Experian Australia. Positive credit history is built by responsibly using credit products over time. Strategies for new arrivals include: (1) Open a basic bank transaction account immediately (no credit check required). (2) Apply for a low-limit or secured credit card — CommBank Neo (CBA), Latitude GO Mastercard, or a basic Visa/Mastercard from your bank with a low credit limit. (3) Ensure all bills (phone, internet, utilities) are paid on time — late payments are recorded. (4) After 6–12 months of responsible use, apply for a standard credit card. (5) Avoid applying for multiple credit products simultaneously. You can access your free credit report from Equifax at equifax.com.au, Illion at getcreditscore.com.au, and Experian at experian.com.au.
rows.where_to_go: Your chosen bank branch/website for a secured or low-limit credit card. Free credit reports: equifax.com.au, getcreditscore.com.au, experian.com.au
rows.notes: Australia uses a 'comprehensive credit reporting' (CCR) system since 2018, meaning both positive and negative information is reported. Positive payment history helps build your score quickly. The CBA Neo card and Latitude credit cards are known to be more accessible for recent arrivals. Avoid payday lenders or high-fee products. Comprehensive credit reporting means responsible account management (never missing a payment) builds history faster than under old negative-only systems.
rows.source_quote: Credit scores and credit reports — understand your credit score and how to improve it.

rows.title: Complete Tax File Number (TFN) Declaration for Employer
rows.description: On commencing employment in Australia, your employer will ask you to complete a Tax File Number Declaration form (NAT 3092). This form is separate from applying for a TFN — it informs your employer of your TFN (or that you have applied for one) so they can set up correct tax withholding at the appropriate marginal rate. You also declare on this form whether you have a tax-free threshold entitlement (Australian residents generally claim the tax-free threshold — AUD 18,200 for 2024–25 — from their main employer only). If you have not yet received your TFN after applying, you have 28 days to provide it to your employer; during that time your employer should withhold tax at the 'no TFN' rate (47%). Always check the form details with your employer's payroll team.
required_documents: TFN (or confirmation of TFN application in progress)
rows.where_to_go: Completed and given to your employer's payroll or HR team on or before your first day of work. Form available at ato.gov.au (NAT 3092)
rows.notes: The tax-free threshold (AUD 18,200 in 2024-25) should only be claimed from your main/primary employer. Claiming it from multiple employers may result in a tax debt at year-end. Temporary residents are generally not entitled to the tax-free threshold — check your visa category. The TFN Declaration is not the same as the TFN application — it is completed for each new employer.
rows.source_quote: What is a tax file number? Find out why you need a TFN, where to find it and how to keep your TFN and personal details safe.

rows.title: Understand Departing Australia Superannuation Payment (DASP) — Temporary Visa Holders
rows.description: Temporary visa holders (e.g., skilled worker visa holders who are not permanent residents) who accumulate superannuation in Australia can claim a Departing Australia Superannuation Payment (DASP) when they permanently leave Australia and their visa has expired or been cancelled. DASP allows temporary visa holders to access their super balance after departure. The payment is taxed at 35% on the taxed element (the portion that had concessional contributions tax applied). New Zealand citizens have an alternative — they can transfer their Australian super balance to a KiwiSaver account in New Zealand under the Trans-Tasman Retirement Savings Portability scheme, avoiding DASP tax rates. Permanent residents do not need DASP — they retain their super until Australian preservation age (60–65). To claim DASP, submit an application via the ATO website after departing Australia.
required_documents: evidence of visa expiry or cancellation
rows.where_to_go: ATO Online Services or ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/super-for-individuals-and-families/super/temporary-residents-and-superannuation
rows.notes: DASP is relevant on departure, not arrival — but employees should be aware of this entitlement from day one of planning. DASP tax rate is 35% (taxed element) or 65% (untaxed element, uncommon). NZ citizens should consider the Trans-Tasman portability option (lower tax treatment) rather than DASP. Super cannot be accessed while still in Australia on a temporary visa (with very limited exceptions). The ATO holds unclaimed DASP if not claimed within 6 months of departure — this can be reclaimed later.
rows.source_quote: Temporary residents and superannuation — How superannuation applies to temporary residents. If you're a temporary resident of Australia, how to claim your superannuation when you leave. Departing Australia superannuation payment DASP.

rows.title: Obtain a myGovID / Digital ID (for ATO Online Services access)
rows.description: myGovID is the Australian Government's digital identity credential (the app-based version of a Digital ID), distinct from the myGov portal. It allows individuals to verify their identity to a high standard and access government services without needing to attend a service centre in person. myGovID works in conjunction with the Relationship Authorisation Manager (RAM) for business, and is required for some ATO online services (including direct TFN application online for eligible individuals). To set up myGovID, download the myGovID app (iOS or Android), verify your identity using one of: passport, Australian driver's licence, Medicare card, or ImmiCard. There are three identity levels — Basic, Standard, and Strong — that unlock different government services. A Strong identity level allows new Australian citizens and some visa holders to apply for a TFN directly online.
required_documents: at least one identity document: passport, Australian driver's licence, Medicare card, or ImmiCard
rows.where_to_go: myGovID app — download from App Store or Google Play. Information at mygovid.gov.au
rows.notes: myGovID (digital identity app) is different from myGov (the portal at my.gov.au). myGovID is used to log in to myGov securely and to access certain ATO services. The Australian Government's Digital ID system (previously myGovID) was rebranded as part of the broader Australian Government Digital ID System (AGDIS) framework. All services remain accessible via the myGovID app. Setting up myGovID early enables faster and more secure access to ATO, myGov, and other government portals.
rows.source_quote: myGovID is Australia's digital identity app, helping you prove who you are online — quickly, safely and securely.

rows.title: Choose a Super Fund Using the YourSuper Comparison Tool
rows.description: The ATO's YourSuper comparison tool allows employees to compare MySuper-authorised superannuation products side by side across key metrics including investment returns, fees, and insurance options. This is the recommended starting point for choosing a default super fund if you have no existing Australian super. Industry funds (e.g. AustralianSuper, Hostplus, REST, HESTA, Cbus) have historically shown strong long-term net returns and lower fees compared to many retail funds. Retail funds (run by banks and financial institutions) offer broader investment choices. Public sector funds are restricted to government employees. If you are employed under an award or enterprise agreement that specifies a particular fund, you may have limited choice — your employer will advise. Complete the Superannuation Standard Choice Form and return it to your employer within 28 days of starting employment.
required_documents: Superannuation Standard Choice Form (provided by employer)
your member number (once account opened with chosen fund)
rows.where_to_go: YourSuper comparison tool at ato.gov.au/yoursuper | ASIC Moneysmart: moneysmart.gov.au/superannuation/choosing-a-super-fund
rows.notes: Industry funds consistently outperform retail funds on net returns over 5–10 year periods according to APRA data. All MySuper products must pass the APRA annual performance test — funds that fail two years in a row cannot accept new members. When you start a new job, your employer must give you 28 days to choose a fund. If you already have an Australian super account, it is automatically 'stapled' to you and the ATO will notify new employers to use it.
rows.source_quote: Whether you're an employee, contractor or self-employed, you can usually choose which fund you want your superannuation contributions (including your super guarantee contributions) to be paid into. To help compare options and choose a super fund that meets your needs you can: visit Choosing a super fund on ASIC's Moneysmart website; use the YourSuper comparison tool.

rows.title: Understand Australian Income Tax Rates and File First Tax Return
rows.description: Australia has a progressive income tax system. For Australian residents (including most permanent migrants and temporary residents who are tax residents), the 2024–25 income tax rates are: AUD 0–18,200 = 0% (tax-free threshold); AUD 18,201–45,000 = 19 cents per dollar over AUD 18,200; AUD 45,001–135,000 = AUD 5,092 + 32.5 cents per dollar; AUD 135,001–190,000 = AUD 31,288 + 37 cents; over AUD 190,000 = AUD 51,638 + 45 cents. A Medicare Levy of 2% applies to most Australian residents (on top of income tax). Non-residents are taxed at 32.5% from the first dollar and are not entitled to the tax-free threshold. The Australian financial year runs 1 July to 30 June. The deadline to lodge a tax return for most individuals is 31 October each year (or later if using a registered tax agent). New arrivals often receive a tax refund in their first year due to pro-rata withholding. Use the ATO's myTax system (via myGov) or a registered tax agent to lodge.
required_documents: payment summaries / income statements from employer (available via myGov/ATO from 1 July)
records of deductions (work-related expenses, charitable donations)
rows.where_to_go: ATO myTax via myGov at my.gov.au | ATO: ato.gov.au/individuals-and-families/lodging-income-tax-returns | Registered tax agent
rows.notes: The deadline for lodging your own tax return is 31 October each year (for the year ending 30 June). Using a registered tax agent extends this deadline. Income statements from your employer are automatically pre-populated in myTax from late July. Non-residents for tax purposes cannot claim the tax-free threshold and are taxed at higher rates — residency status for tax purposes is complex and may differ from immigration residency. Consider seeking advice from a registered tax agent for your first Australian tax return.
rows.source_quote: Tax file number — How to apply for a tax file number (TFN), update your TFN details, where to find your TFN and what to do if it's stolen.

rows.title: Provide Bank Account BSB and Account Number to Employer for Payroll
rows.description: Once your Australian bank account is opened, you must provide your BSB (Bank State Branch — a 6-digit code identifying your bank and branch) and account number to your employer's payroll team so they can process your salary payments via the Australian banking system. Australian payroll is processed via EFT (Electronic Funds Transfer). Wages are typically paid weekly, fortnightly, or monthly depending on your employment contract. If you have not yet opened an Australian account when starting work, your employer cannot pay you via EFT and may need to pay by cheque or delay payment — open your account before your first day wherever possible. You should also notify your employer of any changes to your bank details in writing.
rows.where_to_go: Employer's HR or payroll team — usually via an onboarding form or HR system
rows.notes: Your BSB can be found on your bank card, in your bank's app, or by searching your bank's name at bsb.com.au. Wages in Australia are typically paid in arrears — your first pay may be delayed by 1–2 weeks. The Fair Work Act sets minimum pay rates and payment frequency requirements. Ensure your employer is paying you at or above the applicable award rate or National Minimum Wage.
rows.source_quote: Employers must pay employees their minimum pay rate and entitlements by the due date, using EFT or another agreed method.

rows.title: Resident address registration (Anmeldung)
rows.description: Within 14 days of moving in, register your address at the local Bürgeramt (citizens' office). Book an appointment online in advance. Bring your passport or national ID and the Wohnungsgeberbestätigung (landlord confirmation form, required under §19 BMG). The Anmeldung confirmation (Meldebescheinigung) you receive is a gate-keeping document needed for bank accounts, tax ID delivery, and most official processes.
required_documents: completed Anmeldeformular (registration form, often available online)
rows.where_to_go: Local Bürgeramt — book via berlin.de/buergeramt, muenchen.de, hamburg.de or equivalent city portal
rows.notes: Late registration is an administrative offence under §54(3) BMG, fine up to €1,000. Landlord must issue Wohnungsgeberbestätigung within 14 days of move-in (§19 BMG). EU/EEA citizens and non-EU nationals alike must register.
rows.source_quote: You can be fined up to €1,000 under §54 of the Federal Registration Act (BMG). According to § 17 of the Bundesmeldegesetz (BMG), you must register your flat within two weeks of moving in.

rows.title: Steueridentifikationsnummer (Tax ID) receipt
rows.description: The Bundeszentralamt für Steuern (BZSt) automatically issues an 11-digit Steuer-Identifikationsnummer (IdNo) to every person registered in Germany. It is sent by post to your registered address within a few weeks of Anmeldung. You do not need to apply — registration triggers it. If not received after 3 months, submit your personal details to BZSt via the online form or in writing to request it. The IdNo is permanent and does not change if you move, marry, or change your name.
required_documents: for manual request: full name, address, date and place of birth
rows.where_to_go: Bundeszentralamt für Steuern — online form at bzst.de or by post to BZSt, Referat St II 7, 11055 Berlin
rows.notes: BZSt FAQ states: 'If you have not received a notification of your IdNo after three months, you can provide the Federal Central Tax Office with your personal data.' For data-protection reasons the IdNo can only be communicated by mail. Employer needs it for payroll (ELStAM electronic wage-tax system).
rows.source_quote: The Federal Central Tax Office will send you your IdNo as soon as the registration office has sent it the necessary data. If you have not received a notification of your IdNo after three months, you can provide the Federal Central Tax Office with your personal data.

rows.title: Statutory health insurance (GKV) enrollment
rows.description: All employees earning up to €77,400 gross per year (2026 threshold) are legally required to enrol in a statutory health insurance fund (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung, GKV). Enrolment must happen before or on the first day of employment — the employer notifies the chosen Krankenkasse. The total GKV contribution rate is approximately 17.5% of gross salary (14.6% base + avg. 2.9% additional contribution in 2026), split equally between employer and employee. Choose any of the major GKV providers (TK, AOK, Barmer, DAK, KKH, etc.) and notify your employer of your choice. Employees earning above €77,400 may opt out and choose private health insurance (PKV).
rows.where_to_go: Chosen GKV provider — apply online at tk.de, aok.de, barmer.de, or equivalent before employment start
rows.notes: PKV threshold 2026: €77,400 gross/year (source: GTAI investment guide citing Federal Ministry of Health data). Employer pays half of contributions. Family members can be co-insured at no extra cost under GKV. PKV may offer lower premiums initially but costs can rise significantly with age.
rows.source_name: Germany Trade & Invest (GTAI) — Social Insurance System Investment Guide
rows.source_quote: Employees earning a gross wage of up to EUR 77,400 (2026) per year are compulsorily insured by one of the public health insurance providers (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung - GKV). The average rate of additional contributions for 2026 has been set at 2.9 percent by the Federal Ministry of Health.

rows.title: Open a German bank account
rows.description: A German IBAN is essential for salary payments, SIM-card contracts, and most subscription services. Digital banks (N26, bunq) require only a passport and can be opened fully online within days of arrival, before Anmeldung. Traditional banks (Deutsche Bank, Commerzbank, Sparkasse, ING) typically require passport, Anmeldung confirmation (Meldebescheinigung), and sometimes a residence permit. N26 is not available to US or UK citizens; US citizens should look at Deutsche Bank or Commerzbank. Bunq and Wise are widely available.
required_documents: valid passport (and residence permit if non-EU)
German phone number (usually required for online onboarding)
rows.where_to_go: N26: n26.com (app-based) | Bunq: bunq.com | Deutsche Bank: deutsche-bank.de | Commerzbank: commerzbank.de | ING: ing.de | Sparkasse: local branch
rows.notes: N26 not available for US or UK passport holders. Bunq and Wise accept non-EU residents without Anmeldung. Traditional banks may require Anmeldung proof. Some employers will advance salary by wire transfer before account is open if notified early.
rows.source_name: Migaku / findenglish.de — Bank Accounts in Germany for Foreigners
rows.source_quote: What you need to open any German bank account: Valid passport (and residence permit if non-EU), Anmeldebestätigung (city registration confirmation), German phone number.

rows.title: Sozialversicherungsausweis (Social Security card) receipt
rows.description: The Sozialversicherungsausweis is a card showing your Sozialversicherungsnummer (SVNR), a permanent 12-digit social security number issued by Deutsche Rentenversicherung (DRV). For employees it is issued automatically once the employer registers them with the chosen GKV, which then notifies DRV. The card arrives by post within 2–6 weeks. You must provide it to your employer. If it has not arrived after 6 weeks, contact your Krankenkasse or DRV directly (0800 1000 4800, free).
required_documents: no application required for employees — employer triggers issuance via GKV enrollment
rows.where_to_go: Deutsche Rentenversicherung — drv.de | via your Krankenkasse | or call 0800 1000 4800
rows.notes: The number is permanent and does not change. Self-employed individuals must apply directly to Deutsche Rentenversicherung Bund. You can submit a tax return without the SVNR but cannot work without it long-term.
rows.source_quote: Service telephone 0800 1000 4800 — Monday to Thursday 8.00 a.m. till 7.00 p.m. and on Fridays to 3.30 p.m.

rows.title: Rentennummer (pension insurance number) — self-employed action
rows.description: For employees, the Rentennummer (pension insurance number) is contained within the Sozialversicherungsnummer and assigned automatically via the employer-GKV process. Self-employed individuals (Freiberufler/Selbstständige) are not automatically enrolled and must apply directly to Deutsche Rentenversicherung Bund (DRV Bund) in writing or online. Pension insurance contributions (18.6% of gross, split employer/employee for employees; full rate for relevant self-employed) are mandatory for many self-employed professions.
required_documents: proof of self-employment status (trade registration / Gewerbeschein or freelance contracts)
rows.where_to_go: Deutsche Rentenversicherung Bund — deutsche-rentenversicherung.de | postal address: DRV Bund, 10704 Berlin
rows.notes: Employees need no action — employer handles registration. Self-employed in certain professions (artists, teachers, journalists via Künstlersozialkasse) have specific mandatory pension obligations. Check with DRV or a Steuerberater.
rows.source_quote: Service telephone 0800 1000 4800 — available Monday to Thursday 8.00 a.m. till 7.00 p.m. and Fridays to 3.30 p.m.

rows.title: Driver's license conversion (non-EU nationals)
rows.description: EU/EEA licence holders: no conversion required; licence is fully valid in Germany indefinitely. Non-EU nationals (US, UK, Australia, Canada, etc.): foreign licence is valid for 6 months from the date of Anmeldung registration. After 6 months, a German licence is required to drive legally. Apply at the local Führerscheinstelle. Holders from US states with reciprocal agreements (e.g. Texas, New York has partial, etc.) may be exempt from practical or written tests. UK licence holders must convert within 6 months of moving. Australian and Canadian requirements vary by province/state agreement.
rows.where_to_go: Local Führerscheinstelle (driver's licence office) at the Stadtverwaltung or Landratsamt
rows.notes: US Embassy confirms: 'As of January 1, 1999, U.S. driver's license holders must be in possession of a German license six months after entering the country.' Holders from US states with full reciprocity skip practical test; partial reciprocity states skip road test but take written test (~€40). Processing 4–6 weeks. Start early — Führerscheinstelle appointment waits can be long.
rows.source_name: U.S. Embassy & Consulates in Germany — Driving in Germany
rows.source_quote: As of January 1, 1999, U.S. driver's license holders must be in possession of a German license six months after entering the country, if they wish to continue driving.

rows.title: Rundfunkbeitrag (broadcast fee) registration
rows.description: Every household in Germany is legally required to pay the Rundfunkbeitrag (public broadcasting fee), regardless of whether they own a TV, radio, or use public broadcasting services. The current fee is €18.36 per month per household. When you register your Anmeldung, the registration office notifies the Beitragsservice, which will write to you. You must then register your household online at rundfunkbeitrag.de or by post. One fee covers all occupants of a household. Exemptions are available for recipients of Bürgergeld, BAföG, and certain disability codes.
required_documents: bank account IBAN for direct debit setup
rows.where_to_go: rundfunkbeitrag.de — online registration form
rows.notes: Fee is €18.36/month as of 2025–2026 per the official Rundfunkbeitrag website. If several persons share a flat, only one pays. Secondary residences can apply for exemption. Beitragsservice runs regular data matching against all registration offices.
rows.source_quote: For private households, the current fee is 18.36 euros per month. The contribution serves to finance public broadcasting service based on a contributory model.

rows.title: German SIM card acquisition
rows.description: German federal law requires mandatory identity verification for all SIM cards (prepaid and contract). You must present a valid passport or national ID. A German address is required for registration — a hotel address is acceptable for short-term stays, but your Anmeldung address is needed for contracts. Major providers include Telekom (best coverage), Vodafone, O2/Telefónica, and discount MVNOs (Aldi Talk, Lidl Connect, etc.). Online-only activation requires a video ID check (VideoIdent). Contract SIMs additionally require proof of address and a German IBAN.
required_documents: German address (temporary address acceptable for prepaid)
rows.where_to_go: Telekom store: telekom.de | Vodafone: vodafone.de | O2: o2online.de | or electronics retailers (MediaMarkt, Saturn, Rewe, Aldi)
rows.notes: Prepaid SIMs can be purchased at supermarkets and activated online with video ID. Contract SIMs require Anmeldung address and IBAN. eSIM options available from major providers. Note that some MVNO SIM cards still require registration via PostIdent or VideoIdent.
rows.source_name: ESIMPass / German prepaid SIM law overview
rows.source_quote: German law requires mandatory identity verification for all prepaid SIM cards. Requirements: Valid ID: A passport or national ID card. German Address: You must provide a valid German address.

rows.title: Child school registration (Schulanmeldung)
rows.description: School attendance is compulsory (Schulpflicht) in Germany from age 6. Children who arrive mid-year can and should start school immediately — they do not have to wait for the new school year. The assigned school depends on your registered address (Wohnort); in some states you may choose. Contact the local Grundschule (primary) or Gymnasium/Realschule (secondary) directly. Bring ID, Anmeldung confirmation, child's birth certificate, vaccination record, and previous school transcripts. International schools are available in major cities but charge significant fees (€8,000–€15,000/year for 6 months enrollment) and have waiting lists.
rows.where_to_go: Local Grundschule (primary) or secondary school assigned by address | or local Schulamt (school authority) | International schools: contact directly
rows.notes: Schulpflicht applies to all children regardless of nationality or residence permit status (UN Convention on Children's Rights). School registration cutoff dates (Stichtage) vary by federal state. German-language support programmes (DaZ — Deutsch als Zweitsprache) are available in most schools for non-German-speaking children.
rows.source_quote: In Germany, every child is required to attend school once they reach the age of 6. Your child does not have to wait a whole year to start school if you have arrived in Germany or moved within the country during the school year — they can also begin to attend school during the school year.

rows.title: Kindergeld (child benefit) application
rows.description: Kindergeld is a monthly state child benefit of €259 per child per month (from 1 January 2026, up from €255 in 2025), payable regardless of income level. It is available to parents who are residents or work in Germany with a qualifying residence/work permit (min. 6 months). Apply as soon as you arrive with children — it can be claimed retroactively for up to 6 months. Submit the KG1 application form plus KG11 annex (per child) to the responsible Familienkasse (Family Benefits Office) of the Bundesagentur für Arbeit. You need both your Steuer-IdNo and your child's Steuer-IdNo.
required_documents: KG1 application form + KG11 child annex
rows.where_to_go: Familienkasse — find local office at arbeitsagentur.de by entering postal code | application also available online at familienkasse.de
rows.notes: Amount: €259/month per child from 1 Jan 2026. Only one parent applies. Retroactive claim possible for 6 months only — apply promptly. Children up to age 18 (up to 25 if in education/training). Kindergeld is paid regardless of number of children at the same rate per child.
rows.source_quote: On January 1st, 2025, child benefits were increased, i.e., €255 per month for each child. The amount will increase to €259 on 1 January 2026. You can apply for Child Benefit immediately after childbirth or entering Germany, given you meet the requirements.

rows.title: Elterngeld (parental allowance) application
rows.description: Elterngeld is a federal parental benefit replacing 65%–67% of pre-birth net income (minimum €300/month, maximum €1,800/month for Basic Elterngeld) for up to 14 months per couple (each parent takes minimum 2 months, max 12). Parents can also choose Elterngeld Plus (half the amount, twice as long) or a combination. Income ceiling for eligibility: €175,000 taxable income per year for couples or single parents (for births from 1 April 2025 onwards). Apply at the local Elterngeldstelle (parental allowance office) — ideally before or shortly after birth, as it is retrospective for up to 3 months.
required_documents: last 12 months of payslips or income tax assessment
rows.where_to_go: Local Elterngeldstelle — part of the Jugendamt or Landratsamt depending on federal state | Berlin: berlin.de/sen/jugend | Online calculator: familienportal.de
rows.notes: Income limit (births from 1 April 2025): €175,000/year for couples and single parents. Minimum benefit €300/month even with no prior income. Application retroactive for up to 3 months — do not wait. Federal portal: familienportal.de has a Elterngeld calculator. Elternzeit (unpaid parental leave of up to 3 years) is a separate but linked entitlement.
rows.source_name: Berlin Senate Department for Youth — Parental Allowance and Parental Leave (Official City Page)
rows.source_quote: The parental allowance is a minimum of 300 euros and a maximum of 1,800 euros. The amount of the parental allowance is based on the average monthly net income of the applying or caring parent in the year before the child was born. For births from 1 April 2025, the income threshold for couples and single parents will be lowered again to 175,000 euros.

rows.title: Income tax class (Steuerklasse) confirmation with employer
rows.description: Germany has six income tax classes (Steuerklassen I–VI) that determine payroll withholding. Your employer retrieves your tax class automatically via the ELStAM system using your Steuer-IdNo once you provide it. Singles default to Class I; married couples can choose Class III/V split or Class IV/IV. Verify your class appears correctly on your first payslip. If you wish to change (e.g. after marriage), submit a request to the local Finanzamt. Tax class affects monthly take-home pay — an incorrect class means over- or under-withholding that is reconciled in the annual tax return.
required_documents: marriage certificate if applicable (for Class III/V)
rows.where_to_go: Employer HR department (provides IdNo) | Local Finanzamt for class changes — find at bzst.de
rows.notes: Class I (single, no children) is default. Class III/V is typically most advantageous for couples with unequal incomes. Class II applies to single parents. Provide your IdNo to employer immediately — payroll cannot be processed correctly until ELStAM data is loaded.
rows.source_name: Bundeszentralamt für Steuern (BZSt) — Identification Number Overview
rows.source_quote: For the purpose of providing employers with automatically retrievable wage tax deduction data, the BZSt also stores additional reporting data for each taxpayer in accordance with Section 39e (2) of the Income Tax Act (EStG).

rows.title: Residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) — non-EU nationals
rows.description: Non-EU/EEA nationals relocating for employment must hold a valid work/residence permit (Aufenthaltstitel) before or immediately upon arrival. Those entering on a national D-visa must convert it to a residence permit at the local Ausländerbehörde within the visa validity period (typically 3–6 months). Book the appointment as early as possible — waiting times in cities like Berlin and Munich can be 8–12 weeks. EU Blue Card applicants with an employer with salary ≥ €48,300/year (2025) qualify for expedited processing via the fast-track procedure.
required_documents: university degree or qualification (for skilled worker permit)
rows.where_to_go: Local Ausländerbehörde (foreigners authority) — Berlin: berlin.de/labo | Munich: kreisverwaltungsreferat.de | Hamburg: hamburg.de/auslaenderbehoerde
rows.notes: EU/EEA citizens do not require a residence permit but may register at the Bürgeramt. Fee approximately €100–€150 depending on permit type. Bridging status ('Fiktionsbescheinigung') allows continued residence and employment while permit application is pending.
rows.source_name: Make it in Germany — Federal Government Employment Portal
rows.source_quote: The provisions were phased in since November 2023. Drivers must exchange their foreign driving licence for a German one within six months of registering their place of residence in Germany.

rows.title: Pension insurance enrollment confirmation (Deutsche Rentenversicherung)
rows.description: Pension insurance (Rentenversicherung) is compulsory for all employees in Germany. The premium is 18.6% of gross salary, split equally between employer (9.3%) and employee (9.3%), deducted automatically through payroll. The employer registers the employee with the DRV via the GKV health insurance company. Confirm with HR that pension contributions are appearing on your payslip. Contributions accumulate toward German state pension entitlements and are coordinated internationally under EU law and bilateral social security agreements.
required_documents: handled by employer — no employee action required if Sozialversicherungsausweis received
rows.where_to_go: Deutsche Rentenversicherung — deutsche-rentenversicherung.de | Check contributions via your DRV online account (Mein DRV-Konto)
rows.notes: Contribution rate 2026: 18.6% gross (9.3% employee, 9.3% employer). GTAI confirms these figures from the Federal Ministry of Health data. International agreements (bilateral treaties with US, UK, AU, CA etc.) may coordinate contributions to avoid double-charging.
rows.source_name: Germany Trade & Invest (GTAI) — Social Insurance System Investment Guide
rows.source_quote: 18.6% pension insurance: 9.3% employer, 9.3% employee. Pension insurance is compulsory for employees.

rows.title: Family co-insurance under GKV (Familienversicherung)
rows.description: Under GKV, non-working spouses and dependent children can be co-insured at no extra cost (Familienversicherung). This is one of the major advantages of GKV over private insurance. The co-insured family member must have no independent income above €535/month (2026, marginal income threshold) and must not be eligible for their own mandatory GKV membership. Register family members with your Krankenkasse immediately upon arrival. Children are automatically co-insured if the GKV parent is the primary earner.
required_documents: proof that co-insured person has no independent mandatory insurance obligation
completed Familienversicherung application form from your Krankenkasse
rows.where_to_go: Your chosen GKV Krankenkasse — TK, AOK, Barmer, DAK, etc.
rows.notes: Free family co-insurance does not apply to PKV members — private insurers charge separate premiums for each family member. Income threshold for co-insured spouse: €535/month (marginal part-time work limit, 2026). This is a significant cost advantage for families choosing GKV.
rows.source_name: Germany Trade & Invest (GTAI) — Social Insurance System Investment Guide
rows.source_quote: Employees earning a gross wage of up to EUR 77,400 (2026) per year are compulsorily insured by one of the public health insurance providers (Gesetzliche Krankenversicherung - GKV). Employee and employer also share the premiums for private health insurance plans.

rows.title: Utilities registration (electricity, gas, internet)
rows.description: Upon moving in, register with the local electricity and gas provider (often already contracted by your landlord). If not, the local default supplier (Grundversorger) automatically covers you until you switch to a cheaper tariff. Internet (DSL/fiber) takes 2–4 weeks to activate after ordering — order immediately on arrival or before if possible. Common providers: Telekom, Vodafone, Unitymedia/Vodafone, O2. Bring your Anmeldung address and IBAN for direct debit. Water is typically included in rent (Nebenkosten) in Germany.
required_documents: previous meter reading (Zählerstand) at move-in date
rows.where_to_go: Electricity/gas: check.24.de or verivox.de for tariff comparison | Internet: telekom.de, vodafone.de, o2online.de | inform landlord of move-in meter readings
rows.notes: Record electricity and gas meter readings on day of move-in and send to previous supplier and your new provider to avoid disputes. Internet lead time is 2–4 weeks — bridge with mobile data in the interim. Average electricity cost ~€100–200/month depending on apartment size.
rows.source_name: Make it in Germany — Federal Government Employment Portal
rows.source_quote: Practical steps for everyday life in Germany including utilities registration after Anmeldung.

rows.title: Annual income tax return (Einkommensteuererklärung) — first year
rows.description: Employees in Germany have taxes withheld automatically via payroll (Lohnsteuer). However, filing an annual Einkommensteuererklärung is often advantageous — on average, tax filers receive a refund of ~€1,100. For new arrivals who started mid-year, the partial-year income typically results in a refund. Deadline: 31 July of the following year (or 28/29 February if using a Steuerberater). File online via ELSTER (elster.de, free) or use a tax app (Taxfix, WISO, etc.). You need your Lohnsteuerbescheinigung (employer tax certificate) from the previous year.
required_documents: receipts for deductible expenses (relocation costs, home office, professional expenses)
rows.where_to_go: ELSTER online portal: elster.de (free) | Finanzamt (local tax office) | or via a registered Steuerberater (tax advisor)
rows.notes: Voluntary for most employees (mandatory if self-employed, if both spouses work and use Class III/V, or if you had income from multiple employers). Relocation expenses for international moves can often be partially deducted. Steuerberater fees are tax-deductible.
rows.source_name: Bundeszentralamt für Steuern (BZSt) — Identification Number & Tax Return
rows.source_quote: You can also submit your income tax return to your tax office without an IdNo. Your tax office is aware of this fact.

rows.title: Obtain Codice Fiscale (tax identification number)
rows.description: The Codice Fiscale is a 16-character alphanumeric tax identification number issued by the Agenzia delle Entrate. It is required for almost every interaction with Italian public authorities and private entities — including opening a bank account, signing a lease, accessing healthcare, enrolling children in school, and obtaining a SIM card. Non-EU citizens can obtain it at any Agenzia delle Entrate territorial office (booking an in-person appointment is mandatory for first-time applicants), at immigration single desks (Sportelli Unici per l'Immigrazione), at the Questura when applying for a residence permit, or at Italian consulates abroad before departure. EU citizens apply directly at any Revenue Agency office. Required documents for non-EU citizens include a valid passport with visa (if required), or a valid residence permit, or an identity certificate from Italian diplomatic/consular authorities. There is no fee for the first issuance.
required_documents: or identity certificate from Italian diplomatic/consular authorities
rows.where_to_go: Agenzia delle Entrate — any territorial office (in-person appointment required); or Italian consulate abroad before departure; or Sportello Unico per l'Immigrazione; or Questura (during residence permit application)
rows.notes: First-time applicants must attend in person for identity verification. The code can be self-calculated but only the Agenzia delle Entrate-issued card is officially valid. Obtain this before or on the day of arrival if possible via the Italian consulate abroad.
rows.source_quote: EU and non-EU foreign citizens applying for their first Italian tax identification number (codice fiscale) must book an in-person appointment. Identity verification is mandatory.

sources: agenziaentrate.gov.it (direct fetch, T1)
en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_fiscal_code (T1 legislative)

rows.title: Residenza registration (iscrizione anagrafica) at the Comune
rows.description: All persons establishing habitual residence in Italy must register their residency (iscrizione anagrafica) at the Anagrafe (registry office) of their local Comune or Municipio. For EU citizens the deadline is 20 days from establishing residence; for non-EU nationals it should be done as soon as practicable — typically once the Permesso di Soggiorno has been issued or the application receipt (ricevuta) obtained. Registration requires proof of address (rental contract or property deed), valid identity document, Codice Fiscale, and for non-EU nationals a valid Permesso di Soggiorno or application receipt. Some Comuni accept online submissions; others require an in-person appointment. Upon successful registration the municipality verifies the address (a local police visit may occur within 45 days). Once registered the employee receives a certificate of residence (certificato di residenza) and can obtain an Italian identity card (Carta d'Identità Elettronica).
required_documents: valid passport or EU identity card
proof of address (rental contract or property deed)
for non-EU: Permesso di Soggiorno or application receipt
for EU citizens: proof of sufficient economic resources or employment (if staying over 3 months)
rows.where_to_go: Ufficio Anagrafe (registry office) at the local Comune or Municipio — many cities offer online booking or online submission
rows.notes: EU citizens: 20-day deadline after establishing residence per D.Lgs. 30/2007. Non-EU citizens: register as soon as Permesso di Soggiorno (or receipt) is available. A Polizia Municipale officer may visit to verify actual residency at the stated address.
rows.source_quote: All persons residing in Italy must register their habitual residence at the Anagrafe of the municipality where they live.

sources: interno.gov.it (T1 — ministry homepage only, detail inferred from D.Lgs. 30/2007)
comune.*/anagrafe (T1 institutional knowledge)

rows.title: Apply for Permesso di Soggiorno (residence permit) — non-EU nationals only
rows.description: Non-EU nationals must apply for a Permesso di Soggiorno within eight working days of entering Italy. The application is submitted at a post office (Poste Italiane) designated 'Sportello Amico' using a pre-filled 'Kit postale' envelope available at those offices. The kit contains an application form and a pre-addressed envelope. The Post Office forwards the application to the relevant Questura (provincial police headquarters). At the Questura the applicant will be fingerprinted and photographed. Types include: work (lavoro subordinato/autonomo), family reunification, study, and others — each with its own supporting documents. A stamped receipt (ricevuta) is issued immediately and serves as a temporary residence document while the permit is processed. The permit (plastic card) is collected later at the Questura. Processing typically takes 60–180 days depending on type and region. Fee: standard government fee applies (approx. €40–€200 depending on permit type, plus €30 postal fee for the kit).
required_documents: proof of accommodation (rental contract, hotel, or host declaration)
postal money orders for government fees
rows.where_to_go: Poste Italiane — Sportello Amico offices for kit pickup and submission; then Questura (Ufficio Immigrazione) for fingerprinting and permit collection
rows.notes: Deadline is eight WORKING days (not calendar days) from entry. Keep the ricevuta (receipt) safe — it is a valid proof of legal stay during processing. Status can be checked at questure.poliziadistato.it/stranieri. Renewal must be requested at least 60 days before expiry.
rows.source_quote: Non-EU nationals must apply within eight working days of entering Italy. The process is managed by the Polizia di Stato under the Ministry of the Interior.

sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permesso_di_soggiorno (T1 legislative citations — D.Lgs. 286/1998)
poliziadistato.it (T1 — navigation confirmed)

rows.title: Register with local ASL and obtain Tessera Sanitaria (health card)
rows.description: Italy's Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN — National Health Service) provides universal healthcare. Employees with a valid Permesso di Soggiorno (or EU residents with Residenza registration) are entitled to enroll. Registration is done in person at the local ASL (Azienda Sanitaria Locale — Local Health Authority) office. Required documents include: Codice Fiscale, valid identity document, Permesso di Soggiorno or residence registration certificate, and employment contract. Upon enrollment the employee is assigned a primary care physician (Medico di Medicina Generale) and receives the Tessera Sanitaria — a plastic card issued by the Ministry of Economy and Finance in cooperation with Agenzia delle Entrate. The reverse side of the card also functions as a European Health Insurance Card (EHIC/TEAM). The card is typically mailed to the registered address within a few weeks of enrollment. Enrollment should be completed within 30 days of establishing residency or starting employment.
required_documents: Permesso di Soggiorno or application receipt (non-EU) / residence registration certificate (EU)
employment contract or proof of employment
rows.where_to_go: Local ASL (Azienda Sanitaria Locale) — Ufficio Scelta e Revoca Medico (physician registration office)
rows.notes: The Tessera Sanitaria is issued by the Ministero dell'Economia e delle Finanze and mailed automatically after ASL enrollment. The card also serves as the TEAM (Tessera Europea di Assicurazione Malattia / EHIC). Family members should also be enrolled at ASL.
rows.source_quote: The Italian health insurance card is a personal identification document for citizens entitled to benefits from Italy's National Health Service. The Italian Ministry of Economy and Finance issues the card in cooperation with the Italian Agency of Revenue.

rows.title: INPS social security registration (employer-led; employee obtains INPS number)
rows.description: INPS (Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale) is Italy's national social security institution. For employees in the private sector, the employer is legally obligated to register the employment contract with INPS and make mandatory contributions on the employee's behalf. The employer submits a mandatory hiring communication (COB — Comunicazione Obbligatoria) to the employment center and registers the employee with INPS before or on the first working day. The employee does not need to take direct action for INPS registration, but should verify that they receive a payslip (busta paga) showing the INPS contribution deductions. The employee should also note their INPS registration/worker number (which may appear on payslips). Employees can access their personal INPS position — including pension statements, contribution history, and benefit applications — online at INPS.it using their SPID digital identity or CIE (Electronic Identity Card).
required_documents: Codice Fiscale (employer uses this to register employee)
rows.where_to_go: Employer handles registration; employee accesses INPS.it online using SPID or CIE for personal position
rows.notes: Employee contribution rate is approximately 9.19% of gross salary; employer contributes approximately 23–30%. Contributions cover pension, disability, unemployment (NASPI), and maternity benefits. Employee should verify payslip shows INPS contributions from first month.
rows.source_name: INPS — Istituto Nazionale della Previdenza Sociale
rows.source_quote: The employer must register the employment and make social security contributions on behalf of the employee before or on the first working day.

rows.title: Open an Italian bank account
rows.description: An Italian bank account is needed to receive salary payments, pay rent via direct debit (RID/SDD), and handle utilities. The Codice Fiscale is the key identifier required by all banks. Most banks require an in-person visit to open a current account (conto corrente). Documents typically required: valid passport, Codice Fiscale, Permesso di Soggiorno or residence registration certificate, and Italian address. Major banks: Intesa Sanpaolo (capillary branch network, strong English support), UniCredit (major European bank), Fineco Bank (online-first, low fees). Some banks offer a basic payment account (conto di base) at capped cost for low-income residents. Online/fintech alternatives (N26, Revolut, Wise) can bridge the gap in the first weeks before a full Italian bank account is opened — they accept non-Italian residents and have lower document requirements.
required_documents: Permesso di Soggiorno or residence registration certificate
rows.where_to_go: Branch of chosen bank (Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, Fineco, or other); Fineco and some others allow online account opening with video identification
rows.notes: Fineco Bank is popular with expats for low fees and English-language online banking. The conto di base (basic account) is a legal option with capped annual fees (~€18/yr) for those with ISEE under €11,600. Salary accounts (conto corrente aziendale) may be arranged directly by the employer.
rows.source_name: Agenzia delle Entrate / Major Italian banks
rows.source_quote: The codice fiscale is required for opening bank accounts, university enrollment, signing leases, and purchasing property.

rows.title: Driver's license — validity and conversion rules
rows.description: EU/EEA driving licenses are fully valid in Italy without any conversion requirement and remain valid for their original expiry date. Holders of EU licenses who establish Italian residency may, however, be required to exchange their license for an Italian one after two years of residency in some circumstances. Non-EU driving licenses are generally valid in Italy for one year from the date of establishing Italian residency (iscrizione anagrafica). After that period, non-EU license holders must convert their license to an Italian one. Italy has bilateral agreements with some non-EU countries (including Switzerland, Norway, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, and others) allowing direct exchange (cambio) without passing a test. For countries without a bilateral agreement, the holder must pass the full Italian driving theory test (esame di teoria) and practical test (esame di guida). The conversion application is submitted to the Motorizzazione Civile (MIT) or through a licensed driving school (autoscuola).
required_documents: certified Italian translation (for non-EU, if required)
rows.where_to_go: Motorizzazione Civile (MIT — Ministero delle Infrastrutture e dei Trasporti) provincial office; or through an autoscuola (driving school) for exam-based conversion
rows.notes: EU license holders: no conversion needed. Non-EU holders from bilateral agreement countries: direct exchange possible. Check the updated list of bilateral agreements on the MIT website. International Driving Permit (IDP) is recommended for the first year.
rows.source_name: Ministero delle Infrastrutture e dei Trasporti (MIT)
rows.source_quote: Non-EU driving licences are valid in Italy for one year from the date of establishing residency; after that period, conversion to an Italian licence is required.

rows.title: Enroll children in Italian school (Istituto Comprensivo)
rows.description: School attendance is compulsory in Italy for children aged 6–16. Families must enroll children at the local Istituto Comprensivo (comprehensive school covering elementary and lower secondary) or at a secondary school (Liceo, Istituto Tecnico, etc.). Enrollment is managed through the school's secretariat (segreteria scolastica) and, for the main enrollment periods, through the national online portal (MIUR/MIM — Ministero dell'Istruzione). Enrollment for the academic year (starting September) typically opens in January–February. New arrivals can enroll mid-year at any time directly at the school secretariat. Required documents: birth certificate (translated and apostilled), vaccination records, Codice Fiscale, passport, and any previous school records (pagella/diploma). For non-Italian-speaking children, schools are required to provide Italian language support (L2 classes). Major Italian cities also have international schools (British, American, German, French) as alternatives.
required_documents: child's birth certificate (translated and apostilled if non-Italian)
rows.where_to_go: Segreteria of the local Istituto Comprensivo or secondary school; online enrollment at Portale Iscrizioni MIUR (miur.gov.it) for annual enrollment periods
rows.notes: State schools are free. A small contribution (contributo scolastico) of €20–€100/year may be requested voluntarily. For mid-year enrollments, go directly to the school. The school will assign a class based on the child's age and assessment of prior learning.
rows.source_quote: School attendance is mandatory in Italy for all children aged 6 to 16 years regardless of nationality or residency status.

rows.title: Obtain an Italian SIM card
rows.description: An Italian SIM card (scheda SIM) from a local operator is needed for a local phone number, which is required by many services including bank accounts and official communications. Under Italian law (based on EU anti-terrorism regulations), SIM card registration requires identity verification. Any adult can purchase a SIM; no proof of residency is required. Required documents: a valid identity document (passport) and Codice Fiscale. Major operators: TIM, Vodafone Italia, WindTre, ILIAD Italia, ho. Mobile, Very Mobile. Prepaid (ricaricabile) SIMs are available immediately at operator stores, tobacconists (tabaccherie), and electronics stores. Porting an existing non-Italian number to an Italian SIM is possible after the SIM is activated. ILIAD and ho. Mobile are popular budget options (plans from ~€5–10/month for unlimited calls + 50+ GB data).
required_documents: valid passport or EU identity card
rows.where_to_go: Operator stores (TIM, Vodafone, WindTre, ILIAD), tobacconists (tabaccherie), electronics stores (Euronics, MediaWorld), or online for some operators
rows.notes: ILIAD offers SIM purchase online with home delivery. The Codice Fiscale is mandatory for SIM registration under Italian law. Bring the original passport — photocopies are not always accepted. Budget operators (ILIAD, ho. Mobile) offer strong value; TIM/Vodafone have better rural coverage.

rows.title: Set up home utilities (electricity, gas, water)
rows.description: Utilities in Italy are typically set up by the tenant when moving into a rental property. Electricity and gas are liberalized markets; the tenant can choose their supplier. The main providers include ENEL Energia (electricity and gas), ENI Gas e Luce, A2A, Edison, and many others. Water is managed by local public utilities (municipalities) and is not liberalized. To activate electricity and gas: contact the supplier directly online, by phone, or in person, providing the meter POD/PDR number (found in the property or on the previous tenant's bill), your Codice Fiscale, Italian bank account IBAN for direct debit, and Italian address. The landlord must provide the meter POD (electricity) and PDR (gas) codes. Activation typically takes 2–5 working days. Water (acqua) registration is done with the local municipal water utility (e.g., ACEA in Rome, MM in Milan) — bring the rental contract and identity document. Broadband internet is provided by TIM, Fastweb, Vodafone, WINDTRE, EOLO (for rural areas); contracts typically require Codice Fiscale and Italian bank account.
required_documents: meter POD number (electricity) and PDR number (gas) — from landlord
rows.where_to_go: Online at supplier website (ENEL Energia at enel.it, ENI at eni.com, etc.); or by phone; water utility at municipal office or online
rows.notes: Italy's electricity and gas market is liberalized — compare offers at portale offerte.it (ARERA official comparison site). The 'tutela graduale' transitional tariff applies to those who don't choose a market supplier. Water is always a local municipal monopoly.
rows.source_name: ARERA — Autorità di Regolazione per Energia Reti e Ambiente
rows.source_quote: The Italian electricity and gas market is fully liberalized; consumers can freely choose their supplier and switch at any time without penalty.

rows.title: Obtain PESEL number (national identification number)
rows.description: PESEL (Powszechny Elektroniczny System Ewidencji Ludności — Universal Electronic System for Registration of the Population) is Poland's national identification number — an 11-digit permanent code that identifies each person uniquely. It is required for banking, healthcare, tax registration, and most administrative interactions. All persons residing in Poland permanently, or temporarily for more than 30 days (for EU citizens) or those legally residing and working (for non-EU citizens), are entitled to a PESEL number. EU/EEA citizens obtain PESEL automatically when registering permanent or temporary residence (zameldowanie) for more than 3 months at the local gmina (urząd gminy/miasta). Non-EU citizens with a valid Karta Pobytu (residence card) or work visa can also apply for PESEL. Application is made in person at the local urząd gminy (municipal office). Required documents: valid passport or EU identity card, address registration document (or rental contract for address proof), and for non-EU citizens a valid residence permit or work visa. There is no fee.
required_documents: valid passport or EU identity card
proof of address in Poland (rental contract or zameldowanie confirmation)
for non-EU: valid Karta Pobytu (residence card) or work visa
completed application form (available at urząd gminy)
rows.where_to_go: Urząd Gminy or Urząd Miasta (municipal office) at the place of residence — Wydział Ewidencji Ludności (Population Registry Department)
rows.notes: PESEL is automatically assigned to Polish citizens at birth. For foreigners, it is issued upon registration of residence. Once you have a PESEL, NIP (tax ID) is automatically derived/linked. The PESEL number also enables creation of a Profil Zaufany (trusted profile) for online government services.
rows.source_quote: PESEL identifies exactly one person and is mandatory for all permanent Polish residents and those living temporarily in Poland for over two months.
