COBRA is administered by the US Department of Labor.
required_documents: COBRA election notice from prior employer
COBRA election form (must be returned within 60 days)
rows.where_to_go: Contact prior employer's HR/benefits administrator; DOL COBRA resources at dol.gov/general/topic/health-plans/cobra
rows.notes: COBRA premiums are typically much higher than employer-sponsored coverage because the employer no longer contributes. Compare with ACA marketplace plans before electing COBRA. state_variation_note: Some states (NY, CA, NJ, etc.) have 'mini-COBRA' laws extending similar protections to employees of small businesses (fewer than 20 employees) not covered by federal COBRA.
rows.source_quote: COBRA insurance lets qualified workers keep their group health insurance for a limited time after a change in eligibility.

rows.title: Verify and Update I-94 Arrival/Departure Record
rows.description: Form I-94 is the official record of your arrival and authorized period of stay in the United States, issued by US Customs and Border Protection (CBP). Since 2013, I-94 records are electronic for most air and sea arrivals — you may not receive a physical I-94 stamp. Your I-94 record is the legal document that controls how long you can remain in the US. Key actions upon arrival: (1) Retrieve your electronic I-94 at i94.cbp.dhs.gov within the first few days to verify it is correct (correct visa class, correct name, correct admitted-until date). Errors on the I-94 can cause serious immigration problems. (2) Note your 'Admit Until' date — this is the authorized period of stay, not your visa expiration date (which is only the window to enter, not how long you can stay). (3) If you entered by land, a physical I-94 may have been issued. (4) If you find errors, contact CBP Deferred Inspection at the nearest airport or port of entry to correct them. (5) Your I-94 number is required for SSN applications, ITIN applications, and many other administrative processes.
required_documents: Travel information (flight number, date of entry)
rows.where_to_go: Online at i94.cbp.dhs.gov; for corrections: CBP Deferred Inspection site nearest to you — find at cbp.gov
rows.notes: Critical: Overstaying your I-94 authorized period — even by one day — can result in bars to re-entry and immigration consequences. The I-94 'admit until' date governs your lawful presence, not your visa expiration date. state_variation_note: No state variation — I-94 is a federal CBP document.
rows.source_name: US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) — I-94
rows.source_quote: CBP has automated the Form I-94 process at air and sea ports of entry. Travelers arriving at an air or sea port of entry no longer receive a paper Form I-94 as proof of admission to the U.S.

rows.title: Register Change of Address with USCIS (if applicable)
rows.description: Foreign nationals on non-immigrant visas (H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN, etc.) and green card holders are legally required to notify USCIS of any change of address within 10 days of moving. This requirement applies under Section 265 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA). Failure to comply can technically result in a fine or immigration consequences, though enforcement is rare. Notification is done online using Form AR-11 (Alien's Change of Address Card) at uscis.gov/ar-11 — it is free and takes only a few minutes. Note: Filing AR-11 updates your address with USCIS only. It does not update your address with CBP, the IRS, SSA, or the US Postal Service. Each agency must be notified separately. If you have a pending immigration application, you must also update your address on that application separately (Form AR-11 alone does not update pending case addresses — use the USCIS online account or contact the relevant service center).
required_documents: A number (alien registration number) or receipt number for pending applications
rows.where_to_go: Online at uscis.gov/ar-11 (free, online form)
rows.notes: Required by law within 10 days of moving. Filing is free and takes approximately 5 minutes online. Does not update address with IRS, SSA, or USPS — those must be updated separately. state_variation_note: No state variation — AR-11 is a federal USCIS form. However, some states have additional alien registration requirements — check with a qualified immigration attorney if unsure.
rows.source_quote: Most non-U.S. citizens who change their address must report their new address to USCIS within 10 days of moving.

rows.title: Any Country to Italy
rows.description: Relocating to Italy requires obtaining a National D Visa before departure, applying for a Permesso di Soggorno(within 8 days of arrival), and completing residency registration at your local Comune. You will also need a Codice Fiscale (tax ID), which is required for virtually every official act including opening a bank account and signing a lease. Build in at least 4-6 weeks of buffer for administrative steps due to Italy's lengthy bureaucratic processes.

extras.hr_summary: Employers must initiate the Nulla Osta (work authorization) application in Italy before the employee can obtain a visa. Non-EU nationals are subject to the annual Decreto Flussi quota system, which is released once per year (typically December/January). Missing the quota window means a 12-month delay. HR should budget for legal admin support and anticipate long wait times at the Questura for the Permesso di Soggiorno.

items.text: Decreto Flussi quota is released once a year (typically December/January). Missing the annual window means a minimum 12-month wait before the employee can begin working in Italy.
Permesso di Soggorno(aresidence permit) must be applied for within 8 days of arrival. Failure to meet this deadline results in legal violations and potential deportation risk.
Codice Fiscale (tax ID) is needed before almost every official act -- signing a lease, opening a bank account, enrolling in healthcare. Obtain this as a first priority upon arrival.
Questura (Police HQ) appointments for Permesso di Soggorno can take several months in major cities. Plan travel and work start dates accordingly.
Italy's bureaucracy is notoriously slow. Build a 4-6 weeks buffer into all administrative timelines and avoid committing the employee to a hard start date.
Spouse and family members require a separate Ricongiungimento Familiare application and may not be able to travel concurrently with the primary employee.

rows.title: Confirm Nulla Osta Decreto Flussi Eligibility
rows.description: Verify employee's nationality and job category are eligible under current Decreto Flussi quota and check whether EU Blue Card is an alternative (requires salary > 29,400/y EUR).

rows.title: Engage Italian Immigration Lawyer / Relocation Partner
rows.description: Retain a licensed Italian immigration attorney or designated relocation management company to handle Nulla Osta filing and Permesso di Soggiorno process.

rows.title: Submit Nulla Osta Application (Click Day)
rows.description: Employer submits Nulla Osta al lavoro application via the government portal on Click Day when annual Decreto Flussi window opens. Timely submission is critical as quotas fill rapidly.

rows.title: Receive Nulla Osta from Prefettura
rows.description: Await issuance of Nulla Osta from local Prefettura (typically 2-8 weeks). Once issued, the Nulla Osta is transmitted to the Italian Embassy in the employee's home country.

rows.title: Apply for National Visa Type D at Italian Consulate
rows.description: Employee applies for National Type D visa at the Italian consulate in their home country, using the Nulla Osta. Required documents: passport, Nulla Osta, employment contract, proof of accommodation, and health insurance.

rows.title: Book Temporary Housing for Arrival
rows.description: Secure temporary accommodation before arrival. Proof of address is needed for various registration steps including Comune residency registration.

rows.title: Arrive in Italy & Declare Presence
rows.description: Upon entry into Italy, ensure passport is stamped and declaration of presence is made if not staying in a hotel. The 8-day clock for Permesso di Soggorno starts from entry date.

rows.title: Obtain Codice Fiscale (Tax ID)
rows.description: Visit Agenzia delle Entrate (Italian revenue agency) or Italian consulate abroad to obtain Codice Fiscale. This tax ID is mandatory for all official activities and should be obtained as early as possible.

rows.title: Submit Permesso di Soggorno Application (within 8 days)
rows.description: Submit residence permit application kit at a designated Post Office (Sportello Amico) within 8 days of arrival. Kit includes application form (called 'kit'), passport copies, visa copy, and payment of fees.

rows.title: Register Residency at Comune (Anagrafe)
rows.description: Register residency with the local municipality (Comune) within 20 days of arrival. Requires Codice Fiscale, passport, and proof of accommodation.

rows.title: Attend Questura Appointment for Permesso di Soggiorno
rows.description: Attend appointment at local Questura (Police Headquarters) where biometrics are taken and identity is verified. Appointment must be scheduled at the Post Office step. Wait times can be 3-6 months in major cities.

rows.title: Enroll in INPS (Social Security)
rows.description: Employer enrolls employee in Italian social security system (INPS) upon start of employment. Mandatory for all workers.

rows.title: Register with Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN)
rows.description: Register with the national health service (SSN) at local ASL. Requires Codice Fiscale, residence permit/application receipt, and employment contract. Provides access to a local doctor (Medico di Base).

rows.title: Open Italian Bank Account
rows.description: Open a local bank account using Codice Fiscale, passport, and proof of address. Needed for receiving salary and paying local expenses.

rows.title: Secure Permanent Housing
rows.description: Find and sign lease for permanent residence. Italian landlords will require Codice Fiscale. For expats, a 1+4 or 4+4 year lease is standard. HR should provide a housing search budget or introduction to relocation agent.

rows.title: Collect Permesso di Soggorno Card
rows.description: Collect physical permesso di soggiorno card from Questura after approval. This card serves as the official residence permit and must be kept valid throughout stay.

rows.title: Family Reunification Application (if applicable)
rows.description: If employee has family members joining, initiate Ricongiungimento Familiare application separately. Family members cannot just travel with the primary worker under a work permit.

rows.title: Nulla Osta Submitted
rows.description: Employer has submitted Nulla Osta application on Click Day. This kicks off the formal work authorization process.

rows.title: Nulla Osta Approved
rows.description: Prefettura issues approved Nulla Osta. Employee can now proceed with visa application at the Italian consulate in their home country.

rows.title: Visa Granted
rows.description: Italian consulate grants National Type D visa. Employee can now book flight and plan travel to Italy.

rows.title: Arrival & Permesso Submitted
rows.description: Employee has arrived in Italy and submitted Permesso di Soggorno);application at Post Office within 8 days.

rows.title: Residency Registered & SSN Active
rows.description: Employee has registered residency at Comune, enrolled in SSN, and is fully set up for daily life in Italy.

rows.title: Permesso di Soggorno Card Received
rows.description: Physical residence permit card received from Questura. Employee is now fully legally resident in Italy.

rows.title: USA to Italy
rows.description: US nationals relocating to Italy are treated as non-EU extracommunitari nationals and are subject to the Decreto Flussi annual quota system. The process is lengthy: your employer must first apply for a Nulla Osta (on annual Click Day), then once approved you apply for a National D Visa at the Italian Consulate in the USA. Alternatively, if your annual salary exceeds EUR 29,400, you may qualify for the EU Blue Card, which bypasses the Decreto Flussi quota.

extras.hr_summary: The US-Italy corridor is one of the most bureaucratically demanding in Europe for non-EU nationals. HR must plan 12+ months ahead to align with the annual Decreto Flussi window (usually opens December/January). EU Blue Card is a strongly recommended alternative for higher-salary hires as it is not subject to quota. All Italian consulate appointments in the USA (New York, Chicago, Los Angeles, etc.) should be booked early as wait times can be 2-3 months.

items.text: Decreto Flussi quota window opens once per year. US nationals not covered by EU Blue Card must wait for this window -- missing it means a full 12-month delay.
Italian Consulate appointments in major US cities (NY, LA, Chicago) have 2-3 month wait times. Book immediately once Nulla Osta is approved.
Permesso di Soggiorno must be applied for within 8 days of arrival in Italy. Missing this deadline is a legal violation that can result in deportation.
Codice Fiscale must be obtained before signing any housing lease or opening a bank account. Employees can obtain it in the USA at the Italian consulate during visa application.
Questura (Police HQ) appointments for Permesso di Soggiorno can take 3-6 months in major cities such as Milan or Rome. Plan employment start date accordingly.
US credentials and documents may require Apostille certification and certified Italian translation. Allow 2-4 weeks for this process.
EU Blue Card bypasses Decreto Flussi quotas and should be evaluated for all hires with salary above EUR 29,400/year. HR should confirm eligibility before defaulting to Decreto Flussi route.

rows.title: Determine Visa Pathway: Decreto Flussi vs EU Blue Card
rows.description: Evaluate whether employee's salary exceeds EUR 29,400/y and qualifications meet EU Blue Card criteria. EU Blue Card is preferred as it bypasses the annual quota system.

rows.title: Engage Italian Immigration Counsel
rows.description: Retain an Italian-licensed immigration lawyer to manage Nulla Osta and visa application. Ensure they have experience with US nationals.

rows.title: Apostille US Documents
rows.description: Obtain Apostille certification for US-issued documents (diplomas, birth certificate, marriage certificate) and obtain certified Italian translations. The Hague Convention applies between USA and Italy.

rows.title: Submit Nulla Osta on Decreto Flussi Click Day
rows.description: Employer submits Nulla Osta application via Inlocop-Integro government portal exactly when the window opens. Quotas fill within minutes to hours on Click Day. If quota is missed, employee must wait until next year.

rows.title: Receive Nulla Osta Approval from Prefettura
rows.description: Prefettura issues Nulla Osta directly to the Italian Embassy in Washington DC or consulate handling the employee's case. Typical processing: 2-8 weeks.

rows.title: Book Visa Appointment at Italian Consulate in USA
rows.description: Sphedule appointment at the relevant Italian consulate (covering employee's US state). Appointment wait times are typically 2-3 months in NY, Chicago, or LA -- book immediately after Nulla Osta approval.

rows.title: Obtain Codice Fiscale at Italian Consulate in USA
rows.description: Request Codice Fiscale (Italian tax ID) directly at the consulate during visa appointment. This avoids needing to visit Agenzia delle Entrate on arrival.

rows.title: Attend Visa Appointment & Receive National D Visa
rows.description: Attend in-person consulate appointment. Bring: passport, Nulla Osta, employment contract, proof of accommodation in Italy, health insurance proof, and proof of means (salary letter). Apostilled documents may be required.

rows.title: Arrange Pre-Arrival Temporary Housing in Italy
rows.description: Secure temporary accommodation for at least 4 weeks after arrival. Permanent rental requires Codice Fiscale and Permesso di Soggiorno receipt in some cases.

rows.title: Arrive in Italy & Start 8-Day Clock
rows.description: Enter Italy with National D visa. The 8-calendar-day deadline for Permesso di Soggiorno application begins on entry date. Confirm passport stamp or entry stamp is recorded.

rows.title: Submit Permesso di Soggiorno Application at Post Office
rows.description: Visit a Sportello Amico Post Office within 8 days of arrival. Submit the 'complete kit' form, passport copies, visa copy, photos, and payment fee. The Post Office also books the Questura appointment.

rows.title: INPS Enrollment by Employer
rows.description: Employer registers employee with INPS (Italian Social Security) upon first day of employment. Contributions are mandatory and employee receives a contribution statement.

rows.title: Register Residency at Comune (Anagrafe) - Within 20 Days
rows.description: Register residency at local Comune. Requires passport, Codice Fiscale, proof of address, and Permesso receipt. Must be done within 20 days of arrival.

rows.title: Register with Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN)
rows.description: Register with local ASL for national healthcare access. Requires Codice Fiscale, Permesso di Soggiorno receipt, and employment contract. Provides access to a Medico di Base (GP).

rows.title: Open Italian Bank Account
rows.description: Open a local bank account using Codice Fiscale and passport. Major banks that accept non-resident new arrivals include Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, and neobanks like N.26

rows.title: Attend Questura Appointment
rows.description: Attend biometrics appointment at Questura. Bring original passport, all application receipts, and additional documents as requested. Wait times in Milan and Rome can be 4-6 months for first available appointment.

rows.title: Collect Permesso di Soggorno Card
rows.description: Collect permit card from Questura after approval. Renew annually until permanent residency eligibility (5 years).

rows.title: File US FBAR and Form 8938 if Required
rows.description: USC employees remain subject to US tax reporting obligations on worldwide income. Advise employee to consult a US-Italy cross-border tax advisor.

rows.title: Visa Pathway Confirmed
rows.description: HR has confirmed whether employee goes via Decreto Flussi or EU Blue Card route. Timeline and budget are set accordingly.

rows.title: Nulla Osta Submitted on Click Day
rows.description: Employer has submitted Nulla Osta application on Decreto Flussi Click Day. Quota position is secured.

rows.title: Nulla Osta Approved by Prefettura
rows.description: Nulla Osta issued and transmitted to Italian consulate in the USA. Employee can now book consulate visa appointment.

rows.title: National D Visa Issued
rows.description: Italian consulate in USA grants National Type D visa. Employee can now book flight to Italy.

rows.title: Arrival & Permesso Submitted
rows.description: Employee arrived in Italy and submitted Permesso di Soggorno application at Post Office within 8 days.

rows.title: Residency Registered at Comune
rows.description: Employee has completed residency registration with local Comune. Now legally resident in Italy.

rows.title: Permesso di Soggiorno Card Received
rows.description: Physical residence permit card received. Employee is fully legalized in Italy.

rows.title: Any Country to Poland
rows.description: Relocating to Poland as a non-EU national requires obtaining a National Visa Type D before arrival, then applying for a Single Permit (Zezwolenie na pobyt czasowy i pracę) once in Poland. The Single Permit combines residence and work authorization into one document. You will need a PESEL number (Polish national ID number) for accessing any public services, opening a bank account, or registering for healthcare. Allow 2-6 months for Single Permit processing depending on voivodeship.

extras.hr_summary: Employers should initiate the Work Permit Type A or Single Permit application as early as possible -- ideally 3-6 months before the planned start date. The Single Permit must be applied for IN Poland (no consulate option), so the employee must enter on a valid visa first. All foreign documents must be sworn translated into Polish by a certified translator. Processing times vary significantly by voivodeship: Warsaw can take 4-10 months.

items.text: The Single Permit must be applied for IN Poland, not at a consulate abroad. The employee must have a valid visa to enter first and then apply in-country.
Employee cannot change employer or alter their job position while Single Permit application is pending. Any change requires a new application.
All foreign documents must be sworn translated into Polish by a certified sworn translator (tłumacz przysęglony). Translation costs and times should be budgeted and scheduled early.
Single Permit processing times are highly variable: Warsaw (Mazowieckie) can take 4-10 months, while smaller voivodeships may process in 8-16 weeks. Agressive start date commitments are risky.
PESEL number is assigned automatically upon residence registration (zameldowanie). Without it, employee cannot fully access public services, open some bank accounts or access NFZ healthcare.
ZUS (social security) registration must be completed within 7 days of the employment start date or penalties may apply.

rows.title: Determine Visa Requirements for Employee Nationality
rows.description: Check whether the employee needs a Polish National Visa (EU citizens do not) or whether they are eligible under any special bilateral agreement with Poland.

rows.title: Engage Polish Immigration Lawyer
rows.description: Retain a Polish-licensed immigration attorney to manage Work Permit and Single Permit process. Experience with the relevant voivodeship office is highly recommended.

rows.title: Initiate Work Permit Type A Application
rows.description: Employer files Work Permit Type A at the voivodeship office (urżąd marszałkowski if based in Warsaw). Requires job description, proof of no EU labour market test, and company registration docs.

rows.title: Collect and Sworn-Translate Employee Documents
rows.description: Employee collects all necessary documents (diplomas, passport, birth certificate, police clearance) and has them sworn-translated into Polish by a certified translator.

rows.title: Receive Work Permit Type A
rows.description: Voivodeship office issues Work Permit Type A. Typical processing: 4-12 weeks. Work Permit Type A allows the employee to apply for the visa and enter Poland.

rows.title: Apply for Polish National Visa Type D at Consulate
rows.description: Employee applies for Polish National Visa (type D) at Polish consulate in home country. Requires Work Permit Type A, employment contract, passport, and proof of accommodation.

rows.title: Arrive in Poland and Register Address (Zameldowanie)
rows.description: Non-EU foreigners must register address (zameldowanie) within 4 days of arrival at local municipal office (Urząd Miasta/Gminy). This triggers automatic PESEL assignment.

rows.title: Obtain PESEL Number
rows.description: PESEL is automatically assigned upon address registration if staying more than 30 days. If not registered, apply separately at municipal office (Urząd Miasta/Gminy) with passport and proof of address.

rows.title: Submit Single Permit Application at Voivodeship Office
rows.description: Employee (with employer support) submits Single Permit (Zezwolenie na pobyt czasowy i pracę) application at the regional voivodeship office (Urząd Wojewódzki). Requires: passport, visa, employment contract, proof of accommodation, and sworn-translated documents.

rows.title: Register With ZUS (Social Security)
rows.description: Employer must register employee with ZUS within 7 days of employment start date. This covers pension, disability, and health insurance contributions.

rows.title: Register for NFZ Health Insurance
rows.description: Once ZUS registration is complete, employee is eligible for NFZ (Narodowy Fundusz Zdrowia) health insurance. Register with a local NFZ office to activate healthcare access.

rows.title: Open Polish Bank Account
rows.description: Open a bank account using passport and PESEL or proof of address. Major banks accepting new arrivals include PKO BP, Mbank, ING, Schoo and neobanks like Revolut.

rows.title: Attend Single Permit Appointment & Biometrics
rows.description: Attend appointment at voivodeship office where biometrics are collected. Bring all original documents and translations.

rows.title: Secure Permanent Housing
rows.description: Find and sign lease for permanent residence. PESEL and address registration may be required by some landlords. HR should provide housing allowance or introduction to relocation agent.

rows.title: Collect Karta Pobytu (Residence Card)
rows.description: Collect physical Karta Pobytu (residence card) from voivodeship office after Single Permit approval. Typical processing: 2-6 months. This is the official document proving residence and work rights.

rows.title: Enroll Children in School (if applicable)
rows.description: Poland offers free public education. Register children at local school with PESEL and proof of residence. International schools are available in major cities.

rows.title: Work Permit Type A Submitted
rows.description: Employer has filed Work Permit Type A at voivodeship office. Processing clock has started.

rows.title: Work Permit Type A Issued
rows.description: Voivodeship office has issued Work Permit Type A. Employee can now apply for National Visa D at Polish consulate.

rows.title: National Visa D Granted
rows.description: Polish consulate has granted National Visa D. Employee can now travel to Poland.

rows.title: Arrival & Residence Registered
rows.description: Employee has arrived in Poland and registered residence (zameldowanie) within 4 days. PESEL is being processed.

rows.title: Single Permit Submitted
rows.description: Single Permit application submitted at voivodeship office. ZUS registration complete. Employee can legally work on a stamp/receipt pending decision.

rows.title: Kara Pobytu (Residence Card) Received
rows.description: Employee has received Karta Pobytu (residence card). Fully legalized for residence and work in Poland.

rows.title: Ukraine to Poland
rows.description: Ukrainian citizens in Poland benefit from the EU Temporary Protection Directive, granting simplified access to residence and work rights. Instead of the standard Single Permit process, many Ukrainian nationals can work legally in Poland under Temporary Protection status. You will receive a special UKR-PESEL and a Karta Pobytu marked 'temporary protection'. However, if you wish to remain long-term or change status, a full Single Permit application may be needed.

extras.hr_summary: Hiring Ukrainian nationals in Poland under Temporary Protection is significantly faster and simpler than the standard non-EU process. Many steps (visa, Work Permit Type A) are waived. However, hr must verify the employee's current status (Temporary Protection vs normal residence permit) and ensure all ZUS and tax obligations are met from day one. Temporary Protection status may expire and must be monitored.

items.text: Temporary Protection status has an expiry date and must be actively monitored. If it expires without a status change, the employee loses the right to work. HR must track expiry dates and proactively renew.

Not all Ukrainian nationals automatically receive Temporary Protection. Only those who fled after 24 February 2022 and meet specific criteria are covered. Verify employee's status before assuming this pathway applies.
Ukrainian employees must register with ZUS from day one of employment. Penalties for late registration apply regardless of Temporary Protection status.
Ukrainian nationals receive a special UKR-PESEL number (starting with 62). This is functionally equivalent to a standard PESEL but must be obtained at a municipal office in person.
Ukrainian documents may need sworn translation into Polish for certain procedures (eg. child school registration, permanent residence applications). Plan accordingly.
Ukrainian workers on Temporary Protection who wish to move to another EU state must re-register in that state. Their Polish status does not automatically transfer.

rows.title: Verify Temporary Protection Status Eligibility
rows.description: Confirm that employee qualifies under the EU Temporary Protection Directive (fled Ukraine after 24 Feb 2022). Verify current status documentation and expiry date.

rows.title: Confirm Status Pathway: Temporary Protection vs Single Permit
rows.description: Decide with immigration counsel whether employee should remain on Temporary Protection or transition to a Single Permit for long-term stability.

rows.title: Register for Ukrainian Temporary Protection Status at Ministry of Internal Affairs
rows.description: If not yet registered, employee registers for Temporary Protection status at an Urząd do Spraw Wewnętrznych office. This provides immediate right to stay and work in Poland.

rows.title: Obtain UKR-PESEL Number
rows.description: Register at local municipal office (Urząd Miasta/Gminy) to receive Ukrainian-designated PESEL (UKR prefix, starting with 62). Requires passport and proof of address. PESEL is needed for bank account, healthcare, and tax registration.

rows.title: Register Address (Zameldowanie)
rows.description: Register residence address at local municipal office within 4 days of arrival. Ukrainian nationals under Temporary Protection use the same process as other non-EU foreigners.

rows.title: Sign Employment Contract
rows.description: Sign Polish-law employment contract (umowa o pracę or other contract type). Ukrainian nationals under Temporary Protection do not need a separate work permit -- the employment contract combined with Temporary Protection status is sufficient.

rows.title: Register With ZUS (Social Security) Within 7 Days
rows.description: Employer registers employee with ZUS within 7 days of employment start. Mandatory regardless of immigration status. Requires PESEL.

rows.title: Register for NFZ Health Insurance
rows.description: Ukrainian nationals under Temporary Protection have access to Polish NFZ healthcare on the same terms as Polish citizens. Register with local NFZ office once ZUS registration is confirmed.

rows.title: Open Polish Bank Account
rows.description: Open a Polish bank account using PESEL and passport. Many Polish banks have Ukrainian-language support and express onboarding for Ukrainian refugees/workers.

rows.title: Enroll Children in School or Kindergarten
rows.description: Ukrainian children under Temporary Protection have access to free Polish public education. Register at local school with PESEL. Some schools offer Ukrainian-language classes or support.

rows.title: Secure Permanent Housing
rows.description: Move from temporary to permanent housing. Polish rental market has high demand in major cities. HR housing allowance or relocation support is strongly recommended.

rows.title: Monitor Temporary Protection Expiry & Renew
rows.description: Track expiry date of employee's Temporary Protection document. Initiate renewal at least 4 weeks before expiry. HR should set calendar reminders for all Ukrainian employees.

rows.title: Assess Long-Term Status Pathway (Single Permit or Permanent Residence)
rows.description: For employees planning to stay long-term, assess when to transition from Temporary Protection to a full Single Permit or long-term EU residence permit (after 5 years).

rows.title: Ensure Ukrainian Credentials Recognition
rows.description: Verify that employee's Ukrainian professional degrees and certifications are recognized in Poland. Regulated professions (eg. doctors, lawyers) may require formal nostrifikacja (credentials recognition) process.

rows.title: Polish Language Support & Integration
rows.description: Arrange Polish language training if needed. Although Ukrainian and Polish are related, workplace integration and administrative processes will be in Polish.

rows.title: Submit PIT Tax Return with Polish Us Office
rows.description: Ukrainian employees are subject to Polish tax law on Polish-source income. Ensure PIT registration with local urząd skarbowy (Tax Office) and file annual return by 30 April each year.

rows.title: Temporary Protection Status Verified
rows.description: HR has confirmed employee's Temporary Protection status and expiry date. Pathway and timeline are set.

rows.title: UKR-PESEL Obtained
rows.description: Employee has received UKrainian-specific PESEL number. Address registration complete.

rows.title: Employment Started & ZUS Registered
rows.description: Employee has started work. ZUS registration complete within 7 days of start date.

rows.title: Fully Integrated: NFZ active, Bank Account Open
rows.description: Employee is fully set up in Poland: NFZ healthcare active, bank account open, and children enrolled in school if applicable.

rows.title: Temporary Protection Renewal Check
rows.description: HR has checked Temporary Protection expiry and initiated renewal or status change process if needed.

rows.title: Long-Term Status Planned
rows.description: HR and employee have agreed on long-term residency strategy: Single Permit or EU long-term residence permit process initiated.

rows.title: USA to UK
rows.description: Moving from the USA to the UK requires a Skilled Worker Visa (post-Brexit). Your employer must hold a valid sponsor licence and assign you a Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS) before you can apply. Plan for 8–12 weeks from offer acceptance to visa grant. On arrival, register with a GP for NHS access, apply for your National Insurance Number, open a UK bank account, and complete a Right-to-Work check with your employer. Your US driving licence is valid for 12 months; exchange it for a UK licence before that window closes.

extras.hr_summary: As the sponsoring employer you must hold an active Sponsor Licence (apply 8+ weeks ahead if not already licensed; fee: £536 small employer / £1,476 medium-large). Assign a Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS) via the Sponsor Management System and pay the Immigration Skills Charge (£364/year small; £1,000/year medium-large). Conduct a Right-to-Work check before the employee's start date. Ensure payroll is set up with the employee's National Insurance Number and confirm council tax and pension (auto-enrolment) obligations.

items.text: Right-to-Work check is a legal obligation. The employee cannot start work until this is completed and documented. Failure carries civil penalties up to £60,000 per illegal worker.
If your company does not yet hold a Sponsor Licence, allow a minimum of 8 weeks for UKVI to process the application before the CoS can be assigned. This adds significantly to total lead time.
The Immigration Skills Charge must be paid upfront at CoS assignment. Failure to pay will prevent issuance of the CoS and block the visa application.
US driving licence is only valid in the UK for 12 months from the date of becoming a UK resident. Missing this window requires a full UK driving test.
National Insurance Number must be obtained before the employee's first payroll run. Without it, emergency tax (higher rate) may be applied.
IHS (Immigration Health Surcharge) must be paid during visa application at £1,035/year per adult. This is a personal cost unless the employer covers it.

rows.title: Verify or obtain Sponsor Licence
rows.description: Confirm your company holds an active UKVI Sponsor Licence. If not, submit the sponsor licence application immediately (fee: £536 small / £1,476 medium-large). Allow 8+ weeks for processing.

rows.title: Assign Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS)
rows.description: Once the employee's role is confirmed, assign a CoS via the Sponsor Management System (SMS). Pay the Immigration Skills Charge at the same time (£364/year small employer; £1,000/year medium-large).

rows.title: Employee submits Skilled Worker Visa application
rows.description: Employee applies online at gov.uk/skilled-worker-visa using CoS reference number. Pays visa fee and Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS). Books biometrics appointment at a UKVCAS centre in the USA.

rows.title: Attend biometrics appointment at UKVCAS
rows.description: Employee attends in-person biometrics appointment (fingerprints, photo) at a UKVCAS centre. Bring passport, CoS number, and supporting documents (salary evidence, English language proof).

rows.title: Conduct Right-to-Work check
rows.description: HR must verify the employee's Right to Work in the UK before their start date using the UK Visas & Immigration online checking service. Retain records for the duration of employment plus 2 years.

rows.title: Apply for National Insurance Number (NIN)
rows.description: Employee applies for a NIN online or by phone (0800 141 2075) on arrival. Required for payroll, tax, and state pension contributions. Allow 4-6 weeks for the number to be issued.

rows.title: Register with NHS GP
rows.description: Employee registers with a local GP (General Practitioner) practice on arrival. Entitled to free NHS care as a Skilled Worker Visa holder who paid the IHS. Find a GP at nhs.uk/service-search/find-a-gp.

rows.title: Open UK bank account
rows.description: Employee opens a UK current account (HSBC, Barclays, Lloyds) or digital account (Monzo, Revolut) using visa, passport, and employer letter as proof of address. Required for salary payments.

rows.title: Set up UK payroll with emergency tax code
rows.description: HR sets up employee in payroll using their right-to-work BRP details. Use emergency tax code (1257L W1/M1) until NIN is received. Update payroll once NIN is confirmed.

rows.title: Enrol employee in workplace pension (auto-enrolment)
rows.description: Auto-enrol the employee in the workplace pension scheme within 6 weeks of their start date. Minimum employer contribution: 3%; employee minimum: 5%. Governed by The Pensions Regulator.

rows.title: Register for Council Tax
rows.description: Employee registers with the local council for Council Tax within 30 days of moving into accommodation. Rates vary by local authority and property band.

rows.title: Exchange US driving licence for UK licence
rows.description: Employee exchanges their US driving licence for a UK licence within 12 months of arrival. Apply via DVLA (gov.uk/exchange-foreign-driving-licence). Some US state licences require a UK driving test — check DVLA country list.

rows.title: Collect Biometric Residence Permit (BRP)
rows.description: Employee collects their BRP from the nominated UK Post Office within 10 days of arrival. The BRP is the primary document proving immigration status and right to work.

rows.title: Notify HMRC of new employee (FPS)
rows.description: HR submits Full Payment Submission (FPS) to HMRC on or before the employee's first payday via payroll software. Required under Real Time Information (RTI) rules.

rows.title: Arrange relocation support and housing
rows.description: HR/employee coordinates temporary or permanent housing. UK rental applications typically require proof of income (employment letter), right-to-work evidence, and references. Verify lease terms pre-arrival where possible.

rows.title: US tax obligations — FBAR / FATCA review
rows.description: Employee remains a US taxpayer (citizen/green card holder). Advise to engage a US expat tax advisor. May need to file FBAR if UK bank account balance exceeds $10,000. IRS Form 2555 (Foreign Earned Income Exclusion) may apply.

rows.title: Plan for ILR eligibility tracking
rows.description: HR and employee should note the 5-year continuous residence requirement for Indefinite Leave to Remain (ILR). Set a calendar milestone to review ILR eligibility and avoid excessive absences from the UK (>180 days/year).

rows.title: Sponsor Licence confirmed / applied
rows.description: Company has verified it holds an active UKVI Sponsor Licence, or has submitted an application. This is the gating dependency for all subsequent immigration steps.

rows.title: Certificate of Sponsorship assigned
rows.description: CoS has been assigned via the Sponsor Management System and the Immigration Skills Charge has been paid. Employee receives CoS reference number to begin visa application.

rows.title: Skilled Worker Visa granted
rows.description: UKVI decision issued. Employee receives visa vignette in passport, confirming right to travel to the UK and work for the sponsoring employer. BRP collection letter issued.

rows.title: Employee arrives in UK & BRP collected
rows.description: Employee enters the UK on their visa. BRP collected from nominated Post Office within 10 days. Right-to-Work check completed by HR before first day of work.

rows.title: NIN received and payroll normalised
rows.description: National Insurance Number issued by HMRC. Payroll updated from emergency tax code to correct cumulative code. Employee fully onboarded in UK payroll and pension.

rows.title: Full UK administrative setup complete
rows.description: Employee has completed NHS registration, opened a UK bank account, registered for Council Tax, and initiated driving licence exchange. Day-to-day UK life fully operational.

rows.title: ILR eligibility review scheduled
rows.description: Five-year ILR eligibility review point. HR and employee confirm continuous residence, absence records, and salary compliance to prepare ILR application.

rows.title: International to UK
rows.description: Relocating to the UK from abroad (non-USA) requires a Skilled Worker Visa if you do not hold British/Irish citizenship or EU settled status. Your employer must be a licensed UKVI sponsor and assign you a Certificate of Sponsorship. Lead time from offer to visa is typically 8–14 weeks depending on whether the sponsor licence is already in place. On arrival, collect your Biometric Residence Permit, register with a GP for NHS care, apply for a National Insurance Number, and open a UK bank account. Check whether your home country driving licence is exchangeable with DVLA or whether a UK test is required.

extras.hr_summary: Confirm your organisation holds an active UKVI Sponsor Licence before making an international offer. Assign a Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS) and pay the Immigration Skills Charge (£364/year small; £1,000/year medium-large). Conduct a Right-to-Work check before the employee's first day. Enrol the new employee in auto-enrolment pension within 6 weeks. Submit FPS to HMRC on or before first payday. Depending on origin country, the employee's driving licence exchange rules will vary — provide guidance on DVLA process.

items.text: Right-to-Work check is mandatory before the employee's first day. Civil penalties of up to £60,000 per illegal worker apply for non-compliance.
If the employer does not already hold a Sponsor Licence, the application takes 8+ weeks. Total lead time can exceed 14 weeks. Factor this into offer timelines.
Employees from non-EEA countries must check whether their driving licence is on the DVLA approved exchange list. If not, a full UK driving test is required.
The Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) must be paid upfront during visa application — currently £1,035/year. This is a significant upfront cost and employers should clarify cost-sharing policy.
National Insurance Number can take 4-6 weeks to arrive after application. Emergency tax code applies in the meantime; ensure payroll is prepared for this scenario.
Employees must not exceed 180 days outside the UK per year if they intend to qualify for Indefinite Leave to Remain after 5 years.

rows.title: Verify or obtain Sponsor Licence
rows.description: Confirm the company holds an active UKVI Sponsor Licence. If not, submit the application immediately (fee: £536 small / £1,476 medium-large). Allow 8+ weeks for UKVI processing.

rows.title: Confirm role meets Skilled Worker eligibility criteria
rows.description: Verify the role meets minimum salary threshold (£26,200 general / £10.75/hr; higher for shortage occupation list roles), is on the eligible occupation code list, and employee meets English language requirement.

rows.title: Assign Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS)
rows.description: Assign CoS via the Sponsor Management System once role and candidate are confirmed. Pay Immigration Skills Charge. Provide CoS reference number to employee for their visa application.

rows.title: Employee applies for Skilled Worker Visa
rows.description: Employee submits online application at gov.uk/skilled-worker-visa. Pays visa application fee and IHS. Books biometrics appointment at nearest UKVCAS centre in home country.

rows.title: Attend biometrics appointment
rows.description: Employee attends UKVCAS biometrics appointment. Bring passport, CoS reference, payslips or job offer letter, English language test certificate (if required), and any dependant documents.

rows.title: Conduct Right-to-Work check before start date
rows.description: HR verifies the employee's right to work in the UK using the UKVI online checking service (share code from employee) or physical document check. Retain evidence for duration of employment plus 2 years.

rows.title: Collect Biometric Residence Permit (BRP)
rows.description: Employee collects BRP from the designated UK Post Office within 10 days of arrival. BRP serves as primary proof of immigration status and right to work.

rows.title: Apply for National Insurance Number
rows.description: Employee applies for NIN online or by calling 0800 141 2075 on arrival. Required for payroll, tax, and National Insurance contributions toward state pension. Allow 4-6 weeks for number issuance.

rows.title: Register with NHS GP
rows.description: Employee registers with a local NHS GP practice. As an IHS payer, entitled to free NHS care. Use nhs.uk/service-search/find-a-gp to locate nearby practice. Bring BRP and proof of address.

rows.title: Open a UK bank account
rows.description: Employee opens a UK current account (HSBC, Barclays, Lloyds, NatWest) or digital account (Monzo, Revolut, Starling) using BRP, passport, and employer letter. Required for salary deposits.

rows.title: Set up payroll with emergency tax code
rows.description: HR sets up the employee in payroll on emergency tax code (1257L W1/M1) until NIN arrives. Update payroll and inform HMRC once NIN is confirmed to correct any over-deduction.

rows.title: Auto-enrol in workplace pension
rows.description: Enrol eligible employee in workplace pension scheme within 6 weeks of start date. Minimum employer contribution: 3%; minimum employee: 5%. Issue auto-enrolment letter within 6 weeks.

rows.title: Register for Council Tax
rows.description: Employee registers with local council for Council Tax within 30 days of moving into property. Rates depend on local authority and property valuation band. Some exemptions apply (e.g., full-time students).

rows.title: Driving licence — check exchange eligibility
rows.description: Employee checks DVLA list to see if their home country licence qualifies for direct exchange (no test). If not listed, must pass UK driving theory and practical test. Start process promptly if test required.

rows.title: Submit HMRC Full Payment Submission (FPS)
rows.description: HR submits FPS to HMRC on or before the employee's first payday via payroll software. This is a legal requirement under Real Time Information (RTI) payroll reporting.

rows.title: Coordinate relocation and temporary housing
rows.description: HR or employee arranges short-term accommodation pre-arrival. UK rental market requires employment letters, references, and right-to-work docs. Consider serviced apartments for the first 4-8 weeks.

rows.title: Track absence days for ILR eligibility
rows.description: HR sets up a system to track the employee's UK residency days. Employees must not exceed 180 days outside the UK per year to remain eligible for Indefinite Leave to Remain after 5 years.

rows.title: Sponsor Licence confirmed
rows.description: Company confirms active UKVI Sponsor Licence or submits application. All subsequent immigration steps are gated on this milestone.

rows.title: Certificate of Sponsorship assigned
rows.description: CoS assigned via SMS, Immigration Skills Charge paid. Employee receives CoS reference number and can submit visa application.

rows.title: Visa decision received
rows.description: UKVI issues visa decision. Employee receives visa vignette and BRP collection details. Travel can be planned.

rows.title: Employee arrives — Right-to-Work & BRP complete
rows.description: Employee arrives in UK, collects BRP, and HR completes Right-to-Work check. Employee legally able to commence employment.

rows.title: NIN received — payroll normalised
rows.description: NIN issued by HMRC. Payroll updated to correct cumulative tax code. Pension auto-enrolment confirmed.

rows.title: Full administrative setup complete
rows.description: Employee has NHS registration, UK bank account, Council Tax registration, and driving licence exchange in progress. Fully integrated into UK administrative systems.

rows.title: ILR eligibility milestone
rows.description: Five-year residency milestone for Indefinite Leave to Remain eligibility. Review absence records, salary compliance, and immigration status before applying.

rows.title: USA to Canada
rows.description: As a US citizen or permanent resident relocating to Canada, you may qualify for CUSMA/USMCA work permit categories (e.g., TN, intra-company transfer, investors) which are LMIA-exempt — a major advantage. TN permits are issued at the port of entry for qualifying professional occupations and are valid up to 3 years (renewable). For roles outside TN categories, an LMIA-exempt permit (ICT, IEC) or LMIA-backed permit may be required. On arrival, obtain your Social Insurance Number (SIN) at a Service Canada office, register for provincial health insurance (waiting period varies by province), and open a Canadian bank account. Apply for Express Entry if permanent residence is your goal.

extras.hr_summary: For US employees under CUSMA/USMCA TN status, no LMIA is required — confirm the role is on the TN eligible occupations list and prepare a support letter. For other categories, determine whether an LMIA exemption applies (ICT, IEC). If a standard LMIA is needed, budget 1-5 months and a filing fee of CAD $1,000 per position. Ensure payroll is compliant with Canadian federal and provincial tax rules, CPP (Canada Pension Plan) contributions, and EI (Employment Insurance) premiums. Register the employee with the appropriate provincial health plan if the employer sponsors extended benefits.

items.text: TN status applies only to specific professional occupations listed in the CUSMA/USMCA Appendix. If the role is not listed, an LMIA or other work permit category is required — do not assume TN eligibility.
If an LMIA is required, the process takes 1-5 months and costs CAD $1,000. This is a significant time and cost burden. Explore LMIA exemptions (ICT, CUSMA) first.
Provincial health insurance waiting periods vary: BC has a 3-month wait; Ontario has no wait for most applicants. Ensure the employee has private health coverage during any waiting period.
US citizens remain US taxpayers regardless of Canada residency. Employee should engage a cross-border tax specialist to manage both CRA and IRS obligations, including potential FBAR filing.

Provincial driver's licence must be obtained within 60-90 days of establishing residency in most provinces. US licences may qualify for a direct exchange (credit for driving experience) without a full test.
SIN (Social Insurance Number) is required before the first payroll run. It must be obtained at a Service Canada office in person on arrival. Temporary SINs begin with '9' and have an expiry date.

rows.title: Determine correct work permit category
rows.description: Assess whether the employee qualifies for a CUSMA/USMCA TN permit (professional roles on approved list), ICT (intra-company transfer), IEC, or standard LMIA-backed work permit. Document assessment in employee file.

rows.title: Prepare CUSMA TN support letter (if applicable)
rows.description: HR prepares a formal employer support letter for TN status including: employee's occupation, qualifications, US citizenship, duration of work, and employer details. Employee presents this at the Canadian port of entry.

rows.title: Initiate LMIA application if required
rows.description: If LMIA is required (role not exempt), file with Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC). Fee: CAD $1,000. Provide evidence of recruitment efforts, wage rates, and job duties. Allow 1-5 months for processing.

rows.title: Employee applies for work permit (if not TN at border)
rows.description: For non-TN categories, employee applies online via IRCC portal (ircc.canada.ca) or at a visa application centre. Requires employer offer letter, LMIA number (if applicable), and supporting documents.

rows.title: TN entry at Canadian port of entry
rows.description: For TN holders, present employer support letter, proof of US citizenship, educational credentials, and fee payment (CAD $230) at the Canadian border. TN is issued on the spot by CBSA officer.

rows.title: Obtain Social Insurance Number (SIN)
rows.description: Employee visits a Service Canada office in person on arrival to apply for a SIN. Bring work permit, passport, and proof of address. SIN is required for payroll, tax filing, and government benefits. Temporary SINs (starting with '9') expire with the work permit.

rows.title: Register for provincial health insurance
rows.description: Employee registers for provincial health insurance in their province of residence (e.g., OHIP in Ontario, BC Services Card in BC, RAMQ in Quebec). Waiting periods: BC 3 months, Ontario none, Quebec 3 months. Arrange private interim coverage where applicable.

rows.title: Arrange interim private health coverage
rows.description: HR or employee secures private health insurance for provinces with a waiting period (e.g., BC, Quebec, New Brunswick — 3 months). Employer extended benefits plan should activate immediately if possible.

rows.title: Open Canadian bank account
rows.description: Employee opens a Canadian bank account at RBC, TD, Scotiabank, BMO, or CIBC (or digital: Tangerine, EQ Bank). Required for salary deposits. Bring work permit, passport, and proof of address. Most banks allow new immigrants to open accounts quickly.

rows.title: Set up Canadian payroll — CPP and EI deductions
rows.description: HR sets up employee in Canadian payroll with SIN. Deduct Canada Pension Plan (CPP) contributions and Employment Insurance (EI) premiums from day one. Employer matches CPP and contributes 1.4x employee EI rate.

rows.title: Register with CRA as a Canadian tax resident
rows.description: Employee registers as a Canadian tax resident with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). File T1 income tax return for first year of Canadian residence. Engage cross-border tax advisor for US/Canada dual filing obligations.

rows.title: Exchange US driver's licence for provincial licence
rows.description: Employee exchanges US driver's licence for the provincial equivalent within 60-90 days of establishing residency. Most provinces grant reciprocal credit for driving experience, avoiding a full road test. Contact provincial licensing authority (e.g., DriveBC, ServiceOntario, SAAQ).

rows.title: Enrol employee in workplace benefits and RRSP
rows.description: HR enrols employee in company benefits plan (extended health, dental, vision) and any RRSP matching program. Confirm employee understands RRSP contribution room and tax advantages.

rows.title: Assess Express Entry eligibility
rows.description: Employee and HR assess eligibility for Permanent Residence via Express Entry (Federal Skilled Worker, CEC, or FSTP streams). Calculate Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score. Consider filing an Express Entry profile if CRS score is competitive.

rows.title: US tax obligations — cross-border filing
rows.description: Remind employee that US citizens must continue filing US tax returns (IRS) regardless of Canada residency. Engage a cross-border CPA. Consider IRS Form 2555 (FEIE), Foreign Tax Credit, and FBAR (FinCEN 114) for Canadian bank accounts over $10,000.

rows.title: Arrange relocation and temporary housing
rows.description: HR assists with temporary accommodation for first 4-8 weeks. Canadian rental market in major cities (Toronto, Vancouver) is competitive. Employer letter, pay stubs (US), and references will be needed. Consider short-term furnished rentals.

rows.title: Notify relevant Canadian authorities of provincial address
rows.description: Employee registers with province of residence for tax purposes and informs CRA of Canadian address. Update all government correspondence details. In Quebec, ensure compliance with the Quebec Pension Plan (QPP) rather than CPP.

rows.title: Work permit category confirmed
rows.description: HR and immigration counsel confirm whether TN, ICT, IEC, or LMIA-backed permit applies. This drives all subsequent timeline planning.

rows.title: LMIA approved or LMIA-exempt confirmation issued
rows.description: LMIA positive decision received from ESDC (if required), or LMIA exemption confirmed in writing. Employee can now proceed with work permit or border entry.

rows.title: Work permit / TN status obtained
rows.description: Employee receives Canadian work permit (at port of entry for TN, or online/at VAC for other categories). Employment in Canada can commence.

rows.title: SIN obtained and payroll live
rows.description: Social Insurance Number received from Service Canada. Employee added to Canadian payroll with CPP and EI deductions active.

rows.title: Provincial health insurance active
rows.description: Provincial health coverage becomes effective (accounting for waiting period where applicable). Private interim coverage can be discontinued.

rows.title: Full Canadian administrative setup complete
rows.description: Bank account opened, driver's licence exchange in progress, CRA tax residence registered, employer benefits enrolled. Employee fully integrated into Canadian administrative systems.

rows.title: PR application submitted (Express Entry / PNP)
rows.description: Employee submits Permanent Residence application via Express Entry or Provincial Nominee Program, building toward long-term Canadian status.

rows.title: International to Canada
rows.description: Relocating to Canada from most countries requires an employer-sponsored work permit. The most common pathway is a Labour Market Impact Assessment (LMIA)-backed work permit, which requires the employer to demonstrate no qualified Canadian can fill the role (process: 1-5 months, CAD $1,000 fee). LMIA-exempt categories exist for intra-company transfers (ICT/C12), significant benefit (R205), and bilateral agreements. On arrival, obtain a Social Insurance Number at Service Canada, register for provincial health insurance (waiting period varies by province), open a Canadian bank account, and exchange your driving licence within 60-90 days.

extras.hr_summary: Assess whether the role qualifies for an LMIA exemption before committing to the standard LMIA route. If LMIA is required, begin the process 4-6 months before the intended start date. Once LMIA is obtained, the employee applies for a work permit. Set up payroll with CPP and EI deductions from day one. Arrange private health coverage for provinces with waiting periods. Provide the employee with a comprehensive Canadian settlement guide including Service Canada and provincial health registration steps.

items.text: LMIA processing times vary from 1 to 5 months depending on the stream (Global Talent Stream can be as fast as 2 weeks). Begin the assessment immediately to avoid blocking the start date.

Provincial health insurance waiting periods apply in several provinces (BC, Quebec, New Brunswick — up to 3 months). Failure to arrange private interim coverage exposes the employee to uninsured medical costs.
The employee cannot legally work in Canada until the work permit is issued (and, for in-Canada applicants, received). Do not allow the employee to commence work before permit confirmation.
SIN numbers issued to temporary workers begin with '9' and expire when the work permit expires. HR must update payroll systems when the permit is renewed to ensure continued payroll compliance.

Quebec has distinct immigration rules administered by the MIFI (Ministère de l'Immigration). Employees destined for Quebec require a Quebec Selection Certificate (CSQ) in addition to the federal work permit.
Provincial driver's licence must be obtained within 60-90 days of establishing provincial residency. Requirements and reciprocity agreements vary by province and country of origin.

rows.title: Assess work permit stream (LMIA vs exempt)
rows.description: HR and immigration counsel determine the applicable work permit category: LMIA-backed, ICT (intra-company transfer, C12), significant benefit (R205), IEC, or bilateral agreement. Document the assessment.

rows.title: Initiate LMIA application (if required)
rows.description: Submit LMIA application to Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC). Fee: CAD $1,000 per position. Include recruitment evidence, job posting records, wage information, and business legitimacy documents. Consider Global Talent Stream for tech roles (2-week target).

rows.title: Obtain Quebec Selection Certificate (CSQ) if applicable
rows.description: For employees relocating to Quebec, the employer initiates the CSQ process with MIFI before the federal work permit application. CSQ is required in addition to the federal work permit for Quebec-destined workers.

rows.title: Employee applies for work permit via IRCC
rows.description: Once LMIA or exemption code is confirmed, employee applies online at ircc.canada.ca or at a Canadian Visa Application Centre (VAC) in their country. Requires offer letter, LMIA number, passport, photos, and supporting documents.

rows.title: Complete biometrics at VAC
rows.description: Most nationalities must provide biometrics (fingerprints and photo) at a Visa Application Centre. Biometrics are valid for 10 years once enrolled. Fee: CAD $85 per person (CAD $170 family).

rows.title: Work permit issued — confirm before travel
rows.description: Confirm that the work permit has been issued and the employee has received either an eTA (Electronic Travel Authorization) or entry visa before booking travel. Verify port-of-entry procedures for the specific nationality.

rows.title: Obtain Social Insurance Number (SIN)
rows.description: Employee visits a Service Canada office on arrival to obtain a SIN. Bring work permit and passport. Temporary workers receive a SIN starting with '9' that expires with the work permit. Required before first payroll run.

rows.title: Register for provincial health insurance
rows.description: Employee registers for health coverage in their province: OHIP (Ontario), BC Services Card (BC), RAMQ (Quebec), AHCIP (Alberta), MSP (Manitoba), etc. Waiting periods: BC/Quebec 3 months; Ontario/Alberta immediate for most. Arrange interim private coverage where needed.

rows.title: Arrange interim private health insurance
rows.description: HR ensures interim private health coverage is in place for employees in provinces with a waiting period. Employer group benefits should ideally start from day one; supplement with travel/visitor health insurance if needed.

rows.title: Open a Canadian bank account
rows.description: Employee opens an account at one of the Big 6 banks (RBC, TD, Scotiabank, BMO, CIBC, National Bank) or a digital bank (Tangerine, EQ Bank). Bring work permit, passport, and proof of Canadian address. Most banks offer New to Canada packages.

rows.title: Set up Canadian payroll (CPP, EI, income tax)
rows.description: HR configures payroll with the employee's SIN. Deduct Canada Pension Plan (CPP) contributions, Employment Insurance (EI) premiums, and federal/provincial income tax from first paycheque. In Quebec, QPP replaces CPP.

rows.title: Register with CRA for Canadian taxes
rows.description: Employee establishes Canadian tax residency with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). File T1 income tax return annually. Understand worldwide income reporting requirements as a Canadian tax resident.

rows.title: Exchange driving licence for provincial licence
rows.description: Employee exchanges foreign driving licence for provincial licence within 60-90 days of establishing residency. Check provincial reciprocity agreements. Some countries/provinces require a road test; others allow a direct exchange.

rows.title: Enrol in workplace benefits and pension/RRSP
rows.description: HR enrols the employee in extended health, dental, and vision benefits. Set up RRSP matching contributions if offered. Inform employee of RRSP contribution room rules and TFSA (Tax-Free Savings Account) eligibility.

rows.title: Assess Provincial Nominee Program (PNP) eligibility
rows.description: Evaluate whether the employee qualifies for a Provincial Nominee Program for permanent residence. Many PNPs have employer-nomination streams that prioritize existing employees. File a profile if eligible.

rows.title: Coordinate relocation and temporary housing
rows.description: Arrange short-term accommodation prior to arrival. Provide an employer reference letter for rental applications. Canadian landlords typically require employment letters, pay stubs, and references. Consider corporate housing or short-term furnished apartments for the first month.

rows.title: Monitor work permit expiry and renewal
rows.description: HR sets a calendar reminder 6 months before the work permit expiry date to initiate renewal. Employee must maintain valid status to continue working. Apply for renewal before expiry to maintain 'maintained status' protection.

rows.title: Work permit pathway confirmed
rows.description: HR and immigration counsel confirm LMIA or exemption stream. LMIA application submitted if required. Timeline for permit issuance established.

rows.title: LMIA positive decision received
rows.description: ESDC issues positive LMIA. Employee can now submit work permit application to IRCC. LMIA number included in all permit applications.

rows.title: Work permit issued
rows.description: IRCC issues work permit. Employee confirms travel authorization and books flights to Canada.

rows.title: Employee arrives — SIN obtained and payroll live
rows.description: Employee arrives in Canada, visits Service Canada for SIN, and is added to Canadian payroll. Employment commences legally.

rows.title: Provincial health coverage active
rows.description: Provincial health insurance effective date reached. Private interim coverage can be discontinued. Employee has access to publicly funded healthcare.

rows.title: Full Canadian administrative integration
rows.description: Bank account open, driver's licence exchanged, CRA registration complete, employer benefits enrolled. Employee fully integrated into Canadian systems.

rows.title: Work permit renewal initiated
rows.description: HR initiates work permit renewal 6 months before expiry to ensure uninterrupted legal work status. Explores pathway to permanent residence at this stage.

rows.title: UK to Australia
rows.description: Relocating from the UK to Australia most commonly requires a Subclass 482 Temporary Skill Shortage (TSS) visa, sponsored by an Australian employer who must be an approved Standard Business Sponsor. The sponsorship approval takes 4-8 weeks, followed by the visa application (further 4-8 weeks). Some occupations require a skills assessment from a relevant assessing body before the visa can be granted. On arrival, apply for a Tax File Number (TFN) with the ATO, enrol in Medicare for universal healthcare, choose a superannuation fund for your mandatory retirement savings (employer contributes 11.5%), and open an Australian bank account. UK driving licence holders can drive for up to 3 months before obtaining a state/territory licence.

extras.hr_summary: The employer must be an approved Standard Business Sponsor (or apply to become one — 4-8 weeks, AUD $420 application). Once approved, a nomination is lodged for the specific position (AUD $330 fee). The employee then applies for the Subclass 482 visa. Skills assessments may be required for some occupations (e.g., Engineers Australia for engineers). Once the employee arrives, set up payroll with TFN, register Superannuation guarantee contributions (11.5% of ordinary time earnings), and ensure the employee is enrolled in Medicare. UK citizens in Australia may also explore the Working Holiday visa (417) if under 35, or the Skilled Independent 189 visa for points-based PR.

items.text: Employer must be an approved Standard Business Sponsor before nominating the employee. If not already approved, allow 4-8 weeks for the application — this is a hard prerequisite that blocks all subsequent steps.

Some occupations on the TSMIT (Temporary Skilled Migration Income Threshold) list require a skills assessment from the relevant assessing authority before the visa can be granted. Failure to obtain the assessment will result in visa refusal.
The Temporary Skilled Migration Income Threshold (TSMIT) is AUD $73,150 (2024-25). Roles must meet or exceed this threshold. Ensure salary compliance before making the offer.
Superannuation must be paid at 11.5% of ordinary time earnings from the first pay cycle. Failure to pay Superannuation is illegal and may attract ATO penalties.
UK driving licence is valid for 3 months from the date of establishing residency in most Australian states/territories. After that, a local licence is required. Requirements vary by state.
Tax File Number must be applied for after arrival. Without a TFN, the employer is required to withhold tax at the highest marginal rate (47%).

rows.title: Verify or apply for Standard Business Sponsorship
rows.description: Confirm whether the company is an approved Australian Standard Business Sponsor via the Department of Home Affairs. If not, apply immediately (AUD $420 fee). Online application via ImmiAccount. Allow 4-8 weeks for processing.

rows.title: Check occupation against TSMIT and skills assessment requirements
rows.description: Verify the role is on the Short-term or Medium-term Skilled Occupation List (STSOL/MLTSSL) and meets the TSMIT of AUD $73,150. Determine if a skills assessment is required (e.g., Engineers Australia, VETASSESS, APEC).

rows.title: Initiate skills assessment (if required)
rows.description: Employee applies to the relevant skills assessing authority for their occupation. Assessment takes 4-12 weeks and requires educational certificates, employment history, and references. UK qualifications are generally well-regarded.

rows.title: Lodge nomination for Subclass 482 visa
rows.description: Once Standard Business Sponsorship is approved, HR lodges a nomination for the specific position via ImmiAccount (AUD $330). Provide position description, salary evidence, and business justification.

rows.title: Employee lodges Subclass 482 visa application
rows.description: Employee applies online via ImmiAccount for the Subclass 482 (TSS) visa. Attach skills assessment (if required), health examination results, police clearance, English language evidence, and sponsor nomination reference.

rows.title: Complete health examination
rows.description: Employee books and completes a health examination with a Department of Home Affairs approved panel physician. Results are sent directly to the Home Affairs. UK applicants are generally healthy — this is typically straightforward.

rows.title: Apply for Tax File Number (TFN)
rows.description: Employee applies for a TFN online at ato.gov.au after arrival. Requires passport and visa details. TFN is issued by post within 28 days. Without a TFN, employer must withhold tax at the highest rate (47%). Apply immediately on arrival.

rows.title: Enrol in Medicare
rows.description: Employee visits a Services Australia (Medicare) office to enrol. Requires passport, visa, and proof of address. Entitled as a 482 visa holder. Medicare card provides access to subsidised medical services and the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS).

rows.title: Choose and register a superannuation fund
rows.description: Employee selects a superannuation fund (industry or retail). If no choice is made within 28 days, employer defaults to the stapled fund or company default. Employee provides fund details and TFN to employer for Super Guarantee payments.

rows.title: HR sets up Superannuation contributions
rows.description: HR sets up Superannuation Guarantee contributions from the first pay cycle (11.5% of ordinary time earnings from 1 July 2024). Payments must be made quarterly (or per pay cycle for STP Phase 2 employers). Non-payment attracts Superannuation Guarantee Charge.

rows.title: Open an Australian bank account
rows.description: Employee opens an account with a major Australian bank (CBA, Westpac, ANZ, NAB). Many offer pre-arrival account opening for migrants. Required for salary payment and superannuation registration. Bring passport and visa details.

rows.title: Set up Australian payroll with TFN
rows.description: HR configures payroll in Australia once TFN is received. Deduct PAYG withholding (income tax) and report via Single Touch Payroll (STP) to ATO. Apply correct tax scale based on residency status and Medicare levy entitlement.

rows.title: Exchange UK driving licence for state/territory licence
rows.description: Employee exchanges their UK driving licence for the relevant state/territory licence within 3 months of establishing residency. UK licences are generally accepted for direct exchange without a road test. Contact state licensing authority (e.g., VicRoads, TfNSW, DTMR QLD).

rows.title: Register with ATO as an Australian tax resident
rows.description: Employee registers as an Australian tax resident. File an Australian tax return (July-October each year). As a UK expat, check whether double taxation agreement (DTA) with UK applies to any UK-source income.

rows.title: Coordinate relocation and housing
rows.description: Arrange temporary accommodation pre-arrival. Australian rental market is competitive; employer reference letter, payslips, and ID required for applications. Consider short-term furnished apartments for the first 4-8 weeks while securing permanent accommodation.

rows.title: Assess pathway to Permanent Residence (Subclass 186 / 189 / 190)
rows.description: After 2 years on Subclass 482, employee may be eligible to apply for the Employer Nomination Scheme (ENS) Subclass 186 PR visa. Alternatively, assess points for Subclass 189 (independent) or 190 (state-nominated). Plan PR pathway from day one.

rows.title: Monitor Subclass 482 visa expiry and renewal
rows.description: HR sets a reminder 6 months before Subclass 482 visa expiry. The visa can be renewed for medium-term occupation list roles. Ensure continuous sponsorship and salary compliance throughout the visa period.

rows.title: Standard Business Sponsorship approved
rows.description: Home Affairs approves the company's Standard Business Sponsorship. The employer can now lodge nominations for Subclass 482 visa holders.

rows.title: Nomination approved and visa application lodged
rows.description: Nomination for the specific role has been approved. Employee has lodged the Subclass 482 visa application online including health, police clearance, and skills assessment documents.

rows.title: Subclass 482 visa granted
rows.description: Home Affairs grants the Subclass 482 visa. Employee receives grant notification and can book travel to Australia.

rows.title: Employee arrives — bank, TFN, Medicare initiated
rows.description: Employee arrives in Australia. Bank account opened (or activated if pre-opened), TFN application submitted, Medicare enrolment completed.

rows.title: TFN received — payroll and Super fully configured
rows.description: TFN received from ATO. Payroll updated with correct tax withholding. Superannuation fund details confirmed and contributions commenced.

rows.title: Full Australian administrative setup complete
rows.description: Medicare card received, driver's licence exchanged, permanent accommodation secured, ATO registration complete. Employee fully operational in Australia.

rows.title: PR eligibility — ENS 186 / points test review
rows.description: Two-year milestone on Subclass 482. HR and employee review eligibility for Employer Nomination Scheme (Subclass 186) or points-based PR (Subclass 189/190) applications.

rows.title: International to Australia
rows.description: Moving to Australia for work from most countries requires an employer-sponsored Subclass 482 (Temporary Skill Shortage) visa. The employer must first become an approved Standard Business Sponsor (4-8 weeks), then nominate the position, and the employee applies for the visa. Some occupations also require a positive skills assessment from a relevant Australian authority before the visa is granted. On arrival, apply for a Tax File Number (TFN) with the ATO, enrol in Medicare, select a superannuation fund (employer will contribute 11.5% of your earnings), and open an Australian bank account. Obtain a local driver's licence within 3-6 months depending on your state or territory.

extras.hr_summary: Confirm the employer is an approved Standard Business Sponsor or apply immediately (AUD $420, 4-8 weeks). Lodge a nomination for the role once approved. Ensure the role meets the Temporary Skilled Migration Income Threshold (TSMIT — AUD $73,150 for 2024-25). Some roles require skills assessments — check ANZSCO code requirements. On the employee's arrival, set up payroll via Single Touch Payroll (STP), commence Superannuation Guarantee contributions (11.5%), and verify Medicare enrolment. Build a clear PR pathway plan for employee retention — Subclass 186 ENS after 2 years is the primary employer-sponsored route.

items.text: Employer must be an approved Standard Business Sponsor before submitting a nomination. This is a hard prerequisite — if not yet approved, allow 4-8 weeks minimum before any visa steps can begin.
The Temporary Skilled Migration Income Threshold (TSMIT) of AUD $73,150 (2024-25) must be met for all Subclass 482 visa holders. Offering below this amount will result in nomination rejection.

Skills assessment requirements vary significantly by occupation. Some have mandatory pre-visa assessments (e.g., Engineers Australia, VETASSESS, AHPRA for health professionals). Begin the assessment process early as it can take 4-12 weeks.
Without a TFN, the employer is legally required to withhold tax at the top rate (47%). Employee must apply for TFN immediately on arrival — allow 28 days for receipt from ATO.

Superannuation Guarantee contributions (11.5%) are a legal employer obligation from the first pay cycle. Non-payment triggers the SGC (Superannuation Guarantee Charge) which includes interest and administrative penalties.

Medicare eligibility for temporary visa holders depends on the visa subclass and home country Reciprocal Health Care Agreements (RHCA). UK, Ireland, New Zealand, Belgium, Sweden, Norway, Slovenia, Malta, and Italy citizens are covered. Others must obtain private health insurance.

rows.title: Verify or apply for Standard Business Sponsorship
rows.description: Check whether the company holds approved Standard Business Sponsorship from the Department of Home Affairs. If not, submit the application (AUD $420) via ImmiAccount. Allow 4-8 weeks for approval.

rows.title: Confirm occupation on skills occupation list
