rows.description: Verify the role's ANZSCO code appears on the Short-term Skilled Occupation List (STSOL) or Medium-term List (MLTSSL). Medium-term list positions allow 4-year visas and a pathway to PR. Short-term allows 2-year maximum.

rows.title: Determine skills assessment requirement
rows.description: Identify whether the occupation requires a skills assessment and which authority conducts it (e.g., Engineers Australia, VETASSESS, AHPRA for health, ACWA for social work, CPA/CAANZ for accounting). Begin the assessment process immediately if required.

rows.title: Employee initiates skills assessment
rows.description: Employee applies to the relevant assessing authority. Provide certified copies of qualifications, employment references, and professional registrations. Allow 4-12 weeks. Outcome is 'suitable' or 'not suitable'.

rows.title: Lodge nomination for Subclass 482 visa
rows.description: Once Standard Business Sponsorship is approved, HR lodges a nomination for the specific position via ImmiAccount (AUD $330 fee). Include ANZSCO-aligned position description, salary details, and genuine need justification.

rows.title: Employee lodges Subclass 482 visa application
rows.description: Employee applies online via ImmiAccount for the Subclass 482 visa. Attach nomination reference, skills assessment, health examination results, police clearance certificate, and English language evidence (e.g., IELTS, PTE, or passport exemption).

rows.title: Complete approved health examination
rows.description: Employee books a health examination with a panel physician approved by the Australian Department of Home Affairs (list available at immi.homeaffairs.gov.au). Results are submitted directly to Home Affairs. Chest x-ray typically required.

rows.title: Obtain police clearance certificates
rows.description: Employee obtains police clearance from each country lived in for 12+ months in the past 10 years. Processing times vary by country (1-6 weeks). Australian Federal Police check also required for some applicants.

rows.title: Apply for Tax File Number (TFN) on arrival
rows.description: Employee applies for a TFN online at ato.gov.au immediately after arriving. Requires passport and visa details. TFN is issued by post within 28 days. Without TFN, employer must withhold 47% tax.

rows.title: Enrol in Medicare (if eligible)
rows.description: Eligible employees enrol in Medicare at a Services Australia office (bring passport, visa, proof of address). Citizens of RHCA countries (UK, Ireland, NZ, Belgium, Sweden, Norway, Slovenia, Malta, Italy) are eligible. Others must obtain private health insurance.

rows.title: Arrange private health insurance (if not Medicare eligible)
rows.description: Employees from non-RHCA countries who are not Medicare eligible must obtain private health insurance. Ensure coverage includes hospital, medical, and ambulance. Confirm with insurer that the policy is valid for visa holders.

rows.title: Choose a superannuation fund
rows.description: Employee selects a superannuation fund and provides details (fund USI, member account number) to HR. If no choice is made within 28 days, employer uses the 'stapled' fund (ATO-assigned). Employee can make voluntary contributions above the mandatory 11.5%.

rows.title: Set up Superannuation Guarantee contributions
rows.description: HR configures payroll to pay Superannuation Guarantee (SG) at 11.5% of ordinary time earnings from the first pay cycle. Payments must reach the fund within 28 days of the end of each quarter (or per STP schedule). Issue SG Payment Summary annually.

rows.title: Open an Australian bank account
rows.description: Employee opens a bank account with CBA, Westpac, ANZ, or NAB. Many allow pre-arrival account opening for visa holders. Required for salary and superannuation payments. Bring passport and visa. BPay details needed for super fund.

rows.title: Obtain state/territory driving licence
rows.description: Employee obtains a local driving licence within 3-6 months of establishing residency (varies by state). Requirements depend on the country of origin licence. Some countries require a knowledge test; others allow direct exchange. Check with state authority.

rows.title: Set up payroll via Single Touch Payroll (STP)
rows.description: HR reports payroll information (salary, PAYG withholding, super) to the ATO each pay cycle via STP Phase 2 compliant payroll software. This is mandatory for all Australian employers. Apply correct residency tax scale.

rows.title: Plan PR pathway — Subclass 186 ENS
rows.description: HR and employee discuss the permanent residence pathway from day one. After 2 years (medium-term list) or 3 years on 482, the Subclass 186 ENS (Employer Nomination Scheme) is the primary employer-sponsored PR pathway. Log this as a milestone in the employee's mobility plan.

rows.title: Standard Business Sponsorship approved
rows.description: Department of Home Affairs approves the employer as a Standard Business Sponsor. Employer can now lodge nominations for Subclass 482 candidates.

rows.title: Skills assessment result received
rows.description: Relevant assessing authority issues a suitable skills assessment outcome. This is required before the visa can be granted for assessed occupations.

rows.title: Nomination approved and visa application lodged
rows.description: Nomination for the role is approved by Home Affairs. Employee has submitted the Subclass 482 visa application with all required attachments.

rows.title: Subclass 482 visa granted
rows.description: Home Affairs grants the Subclass 482 visa. Employee can book travel and prepare for relocation to Australia.

rows.title: Employee arrives — TFN applied, Medicare enrolled, bank opened
rows.description: Employee arrives in Australia. TFN applied for, Medicare enrolment initiated, and Australian bank account opened. Superannuation fund selected.

rows.title: TFN received — payroll and Super fully operational
rows.description: TFN received from ATO. PAYG withholding at correct rate applied. Superannuation Guarantee contributions commenced and Super fund confirmed.

rows.title: PR pathway review — Subclass 186 eligibility
rows.description: Two-year milestone on Subclass 482. HR and employee review eligibility and readiness to apply for Subclass 186 ENS permanent residence.

rows.title: France to USA
rows.description: Relocating from France to the USA requires obtaining a valid US work visa — most commonly the H-1B — well before your intended start date, as the lottery process alone can take six months or more. You will need to register for a Social Security Number upon arrival, set up a US bank account, and enroll in your employer's health insurance plan, as there is no universal public coverage. Tax obligations are significant: the US taxes on worldwide income and you may owe both federal and state income taxes from day one of residency.

extras.hr_summary: HR teams must initiate visa sponsorship at least 26 weeks before the target move date to accommodate the H-1B lottery (filed in April for an October 1 start) or to explore cap-exempt or alternative visa pathways (L-1, O-1). Failure to secure the visa before the employee's contract start date creates serious legal and business continuity risk. HR must also manage benefits enrollment, tax equalisation assessments, and relocation policy compliance across potentially varying state-level requirements.

items.text: H-1B visa has an annual lottery (filed April 1, starts October 1) — odds ~25-35% in recent years. Begin the process by October of the prior year; explore cap-exempt employers or L-1/O-1 alternatives early.
French employees will lose French Sécurité Sociale coverage upon leaving; US employer health insurance must be in place from day one as there is no public safety net.

US Substantial Presence Test triggers full tax residency after 183 days in a calendar year — French employee may owe US taxes within months of arrival. Engage a cross-border tax adviser before the move.

Social Security Number (SSN) can only be applied for after arrival; without it, the employee cannot open a bank account, get a driving licence, or complete payroll onboarding. Allow 2-4 weeks processing time.
French driving licence is valid for 3-6 months depending on the US state; the employee must convert to a state driving licence — some states require a road test. Advise early.
US 401(k) enrollment windows are typically 30-90 days from hire date; missing the window may mean waiting until the next open enrollment period.

rows.title: Assess visa category and pathway
rows.description: Determine whether H-1B (lottery), L-1 (intracompany), O-1 (extraordinary ability), or another visa category applies. Engage immigration counsel immediately. H-1B requires registration in March and filing April 1; plan at least 12 months ahead for lottery-dependent cases.

rows.title: Engage US immigration attorney
rows.description: Retain a qualified US immigration lawyer to manage visa petition preparation, USCIS filing, and compliance. Provide attorney with employee CV, degree certificates, and offer letter.

rows.title: File LCA (Labor Condition Application) with DOL
rows.description: For H-1B petitions, the employer must file a certified LCA with the Department of Labor before the USCIS petition. Allow 7 business days for DOL processing. This step is mandatory and must precede the I-129 petition.

rows.title: File USCIS I-129 visa petition
rows.description: Submit the H-1B or L-1 I-129 petition with supporting documentation. For H-1B, premium processing (Form I-907, fee ~$2,805 as of 2024) reduces processing to 15 business days. Standard processing is 3-5 months.

rows.title: Employee schedules US visa interview at US Embassy Paris
rows.description: Once the USCIS petition is approved, the employee must schedule a visa stamp appointment at the US Embassy in Paris (avenue Gabriel). Appointment availability varies; book as soon as the petition approval (I-797) is received.

rows.title: Attend US Embassy visa interview and obtain visa stamp
rows.description: Employee attends interview with passport, I-797 approval notice, DS-160 confirmation, SEVIS fee receipt (if applicable), and supporting documents. Visa stamp is usually affixed within 1-3 business days if approved.

rows.title: Conduct tax equalisation and pre-departure tax briefing
rows.description: Engage a cross-border tax adviser to assess French exit tax obligations, US Substantial Presence Test implications, and treaty benefits under the France-US tax treaty. Brief the employee on potential double-taxation risks and employer tax equalisation policy.

rows.title: Complete US payroll and benefits onboarding setup
rows.description: Set up employee in US payroll system with correct state withholding, federal withholding (W-4), and benefits elections. Coordinate health insurance, dental, vision, and 401(k) enrollment. Employee must complete elections within 30 days of start date.

rows.title: Apply for Social Security Number (SSN)
rows.description: Employee visits local Social Security Administration office with passport, visa, I-94 arrival record, and employment offer letter. SSN required for payroll, bank accounts, credit, and state ID. Processing takes 2-4 weeks. Cannot apply from abroad.

rows.title: Open a US bank account
rows.description: Open a checking account at a major bank (Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo). Requires SSN or ITIN, passport, visa, and proof of US address. Some banks (e.g., HSBC Premier) offer pre-arrival accounts for international employees.

rows.title: Enrol in employer health insurance plan
rows.description: US employers typically provide group health insurance; the employee must actively enrol within the election window (usually 30 days from hire). Review plan options, deductibles, and network coverage. Ensure coverage begins no later than first day of employment.

rows.title: Enrol in 401(k) retirement plan
rows.description: Employee should enrol in employer 401(k) plan within the allowable window (typically 30-90 days from hire). Confirm employer match vesting schedule and contribution limits ($23,000 employee limit in 2024, $69,000 total including employer).

rows.title: Obtain state driver's licence
rows.description: French driving licence is valid for 3-6 months depending on state (check state DMV rules). Employee should visit the state DMV to convert their French licence to a US licence. Some states require a written test and/or road test. Bring passport, visa, SSN, and proof of residence.

rows.title: Register for US federal and state tax filing
rows.description: Employee must file US federal tax return (Form 1040) and state tax return for the state of residence. If arriving mid-year, a dual-status return may be required for the first year. Coordinate with tax adviser on French-US treaty elections (e.g., Article 24 relief).

rows.title: Notify French authorities of departure
rows.description: Employee should deregister from French commune (mairie), notify CAF, terminate French social security coverage, and close or convert French bank accounts. Obtain a Certificate of Coverage from the French social security if applicable under the France-US Social Security Agreement to avoid dual contributions.

rows.title: Arrange housing and temporary accommodation
rows.description: HR or relocation provider should assist with identifying short-term housing (corporate housing or furnished apartment) for the first 30-60 days while the employee secures long-term rental. US landlords typically require SSN, credit history, and 1-2 months deposit.

rows.title: Ship household goods and personal effects
rows.description: Engage an international moving company. US Customs allows duty-free import of household goods if owned 12+ months. Shipping typically takes 4-6 weeks by sea. HR should confirm relocation allowance and whether a lump sum or managed move is offered.

rows.title: Complete I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification
rows.description: US law requires all employees to complete Form I-9 within 3 business days of their first day of work. Employee must present original identity and work authorisation documents (e.g., passport + visa + I-94). HR must retain I-9 records for compliance.

rows.title: Visa petition filed with USCIS
rows.description: I-129 petition (H-1B or L-1) submitted to USCIS with all supporting documentation and LCA certification. Premium processing requested if timeline is tight.

rows.title: USCIS petition approved (I-797 received)
rows.description: USCIS issues I-797 approval notice. Employee can now schedule visa stamp appointment at US Embassy Paris. If RFE (Request for Evidence) issued, respond within 87 days.

rows.title: US visa stamp in passport
rows.description: Employee has obtained the US visa stamp from the US Embassy in Paris. Travel to the US is now authorised. Employee should verify visa validity dates and authorised duration of stay.

rows.title: Employee arrives in the USA
rows.description: Employee crosses US border, I-94 record is created automatically. Employee should verify I-94 record online (i94.cbp.dhs.gov) within 48 hours of arrival to confirm authorised stay period.

rows.title: Social Security Number received
rows.description: SSN card received in the mail. Employee can now complete payroll, open a bank account, and apply for a state driving licence. HR should update payroll records.

rows.title: Benefits enrollment complete
rows.description: Health insurance, dental, vision, and 401(k) elections completed. Coverage confirmed active. Employee has copies of insurance cards and plan documents.

rows.title: Fully settled and operationally ready
rows.description: Employee has SSN, bank account, state driving licence, health insurance, and permanent housing in place. Tax adviser engaged. Employee is fully operational and integrated.

rows.title: India to USA
rows.description: Relocating from India to the USA is one of the most common and most competitive international tech corridors. The H-1B visa remains the primary pathway but carries significant lottery risk and long per-country green card backlogs that can stretch decades for Indian nationals. Premium processing ($2,805) can reduce USCIS review time to 15 business days but does not guarantee selection in the lottery. You should plan finances carefully, as the US has no universal healthcare and you will need to establish credit history from scratch.

extras.hr_summary: HR teams sponsoring Indian nationals must plan the H-1B lottery at least 12 months ahead and maintain a contingency plan (L-1 for intracompany transfers, O-1 for exceptional talent). The Indian per-country EB-2/EB-3 green card backlog currently exceeds 50 years, meaning Indian employees on H-1B will remain visa-dependent for their entire career at the company unless an alternative path is pursued. HR must track H-1B status expiry dates rigorously and file extensions well in advance.

items.text: H-1B lottery selection rate is ~25-35%; Indian nationals are the largest applicant group. File in March registration window; consider cap-exempt employers (universities, research nonprofits) as an alternative.

India EB-2/EB-3 green card backlog is currently 50+ years — Indian employees will remain H-1B dependent for the foreseeable future. HR must track H-1B validity and file extensions (up to 6-year initial cap, extendable with I-140 approval).
Premium processing for H-1B I-129 is $2,805 (as of 2024) and guarantees USCIS review within 15 business days — strongly recommended to meet business start dates.

Indian employees have no US credit history; this can hinder apartment rental, car leasing, and credit card applications. HR should provide a landlord letter and consider a corporate lease for the first 6-12 months.
US health insurance must be in place from day one — there is no public safety net. Gaps in coverage for pre-existing conditions can create significant out-of-pocket costs.

H-1B transfers between employers: if employee changes jobs, new employer must file an H-1B transfer petition BEFORE the employee starts working. Portability provisions (AC21) apply only after 180 days of approved I-140.

rows.title: Determine visa pathway: H-1B, L-1, or O-1
rows.description: Assess whether the employee qualifies for L-1A/L-1B (intracompany, no lottery), O-1 (extraordinary ability), or must enter the H-1B lottery. Engage immigration counsel immediately. For H-1B lottery, registration opens in March each year.

rows.title: Engage US immigration attorney
rows.description: Retain qualified US immigration counsel experienced with Indian national cases and H-1B cap filings. Provide attorney with employee passport, degrees, experience letters, and offer letter.

rows.title: Register for H-1B lottery (March window)
rows.description: Submit H-1B electronic registration via USCIS myUSCIS portal during the March 1-18 registration window. Pay $215 registration fee per beneficiary. USCIS notifies selected registrants by March 31. If selected, proceed to full petition filing by June 30.

rows.title: File LCA with Department of Labor
rows.description: After lottery selection, file the Labor Condition Application (LCA) on the FLAG system. DOL certifies within 7 business days. The LCA must be certified before filing the I-129 petition. Post notice of LCA at worksite for 10 business days.

rows.title: File USCIS I-129 petition with premium processing
rows.description: File Form I-129 (H-1B petition) with supporting evidence (LCA, degree credentials, specialty occupation support). Add Form I-907 and $2,805 premium processing fee to guarantee 15-business-day adjudication. Track receipt notice (I-797C).

rows.title: Employee schedules H-1B visa interview at US Embassy/Consulate India
rows.description: Upon I-797 approval, employee schedules visa appointment at the nearest US Consulate (Chennai, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata). Interview wait times in India can be 6-12+ months — schedule immediately upon receipt of I-797 approval notice.

rows.title: Complete DS-160 visa application and pay MRV fee
rows.description: Employee completes the DS-160 online nonimmigrant visa application and pays the MRV fee ($205 for H-1B). Upload photo and print DS-160 confirmation barcode page for the interview.

rows.title: Attend US visa interview and obtain stamp
rows.description: Employee attends consular interview with passport, I-797, DS-160 confirmation, MRV fee receipt, offer letter, and supporting documents. Visa is typically affixed within 3-5 business days if approved (CEAC status: Issued).

rows.title: Pre-departure tax briefing: India exit and US entry tax obligations
rows.description: Engage a cross-border tax adviser to cover: India exit (residency cessation), US Substantial Presence Test, India-US tax treaty (Article 21 for students; Article 16 for income), FBAR obligations (foreign bank accounts), and employer tax equalisation policy.

rows.title: Apply for Social Security Number (SSN) upon arrival
rows.description: Employee visits Social Security Administration office (no appointment needed) with passport, visa, I-94 record (verify at i94.cbp.dhs.gov), and offer letter. SSN mailed within 2-4 weeks. Required for payroll, bank accounts, and driving licence.

rows.title: Complete I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification
rows.description: US law requires Form I-9 to be completed within 3 business days of employment start. Employee presents List A documents (passport + I-94 + visa) or List B+C combination. HR retains I-9 for the duration of employment plus 3 years.

rows.title: Enrol in employer health insurance plan
rows.description: Employee must enrol in group health insurance within 30 days of hire date. Review medical, dental, vision options. Note that US insurance is employer-specific; there is no public universal coverage. Ensure pre-existing conditions are disclosed if required.

rows.title: Open US bank account
rows.description: Open a US checking account (Chase, Bank of America, or credit union). Requires SSN, passport, visa, and proof of address. Some banks allow opening with ITIN or passport only. Consider international transfer accounts (Wise, Remitly) for sending money to India during transition.

rows.title: Enrol in 401(k) retirement savings plan
rows.description: Enrol in employer 401(k) within the election window (30-90 days from hire). Contribute enough to capture any employer match. Note that 401(k) funds are US-based; consider cross-border retirement planning with Indian EPFO/NPS accounts.

rows.title: Begin building US credit history
rows.description: Apply for a secured credit card (Capital One Secured, Discover Secured) or an immigrant-friendly card (Nova Credit, which translates Indian CIBIL scores) to start building a US credit profile. Good credit needed for apartment leases and future car loans.

rows.title: Obtain state driving licence
rows.description: Indian driving licence is not directly valid in most US states; employee must obtain a state driving licence promptly. Bring SSN, passport, visa, I-94, and proof of residence to the DMV. Most states require a written test and vision test; some require a road test.

rows.title: Initiate green card (EB-2/EB-3) PERM process
rows.description: For Indian nationals, start PERM labor certification as early as possible given the extreme per-country backlog. HR and immigration counsel should file PERM within the first year of H-1B employment to maximise priority date. An approved I-140 also enables H-1B extensions beyond the 6-year cap.

rows.title: Arrange housing and corporate support letter
rows.description: HR should provide a corporate housing letter to assist the employee in securing an apartment, as Indian nationals have no US credit history. Consider corporate lease or furnished short-term housing for the first 60-90 days. Most landlords require credit check, 3 months deposit, or employer guarantee.

rows.title: H-1B registration submitted (March)
rows.description: Electronic H-1B registration submitted via USCIS myUSCIS portal during the March 1-18 window. Confirmation number retained. Lottery selection notification expected by March 31.

rows.title: H-1B lottery selected — petition preparation begins
rows.description: USCIS notifies employer of lottery selection. Full petition package preparation begins immediately. LCA filing on FLAG system initiated in parallel.

rows.title: USCIS I-129 petition approved (I-797 issued)
rows.description: USCIS issues I-797 approval notice for H-1B petition. Employee can now schedule visa stamp appointment at US Consulate in India. Premium processing approval typically within 15 business days of filing.

rows.title: US visa stamp obtained at Indian consulate
rows.description: Employee has H-1B visa stamp in passport from US Consulate. Employee is authorised to travel to the USA and begin employment on or after the H-1B start date (October 1 for cap-subject).

rows.title: Employee arrives in the USA and I-94 confirmed
rows.description: Employee crosses the US border; I-94 record created. Employee verifies I-94 at i94.cbp.dhs.gov within 48 hours. I-9 completed with HR on or before Day 3 of employment.

rows.title: SSN received and payroll/benefits active
rows.description: Social Security Number card received. Payroll updated, 401(k) enrollment initiated, bank account opened. Employee is financially operational in the US.

rows.title: PERM green card process initiated
rows.description: Given the India per-country backlog, PERM labor certification process initiated within first 6 months of employment to establish earliest possible priority date. Immigration counsel managing timeline.

rows.title: Any Country to USA
rows.description: Moving to the United States requires a valid work visa sponsored by your employer — the specific visa type depends on your nationality, job role, and company structure. You will need a Social Security Number for almost every administrative task after arrival, and there is no universal public healthcare, so employer-provided insurance is essential from day one. The US tax system taxes on worldwide income and has both federal and state layers, so engaging a cross-border tax adviser before departure is strongly recommended.

extras.hr_summary: HR must evaluate the appropriate visa category early — H-1B (lottery-based), L-1 (intracompany transfer), O-1 (extraordinary ability), TN (Canada/Mexico), or E-3 (Australia) — and engage immigration counsel at least 6-12 months before the target start date. Benefits enrolment, payroll setup, I-9 compliance, and state-specific employment law all require careful pre-arrival planning. HR must maintain a visa expiry tracker to avoid unlawful employment situations.

items.text: H-1B lottery (April 1 filing, October 1 start) has a ~25-35% selection rate — employers must have a contingency plan (L-1, O-1, TN, E-3) ready before committing to a start date.
There is no universal US health insurance — employer coverage must begin on or before day one. Gaps in coverage expose the employee to catastrophic out-of-pocket costs.
I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification must be completed within 3 business days of the first day of work. Non-compliance carries civil and criminal penalties for the employer.
US Substantial Presence Test triggers full tax residency after 183 qualifying days — employees may owe US income tax and be required to report global assets (FBAR, FATCA) within the first year.
State income tax varies significantly: California taxes up to 13.3%, while Texas and Florida have no state income tax. Work location determines state withholding obligation.

rows.title: Determine applicable visa category
rows.description: Select the appropriate visa: H-1B (specialty occupation, lottery), L-1A/B (intracompany manager/specialist), O-1 (extraordinary ability), TN (Canadian/Mexican nationals under USMCA), E-3 (Australian specialty workers), or E-2 (treaty investor). Nationality and employer structure determine eligibility.

rows.title: Engage US immigration attorney
rows.description: Retain a licensed US immigration attorney to manage the visa petition process, USCIS filing, consular processing, and ongoing compliance. Provide attorney with employee passport, educational credentials, CV, and job offer letter.

rows.title: File visa petition with USCIS or arrange TN/E-3 at port of entry
rows.description: For H-1B/L-1/O-1: file Form I-129 with USCIS (LCA required for H-1B). For TN (Canada): can be processed at the border with offer letter and credentials. For E-3 (Australia): apply at US consulate. Premium processing available for most petition-based visas.

rows.title: Employee applies for US visa stamp at US Embassy/Consulate
rows.description: Once USCIS petition is approved (for petition-based visas), employee schedules and attends a consular interview at the nearest US Embassy or Consulate. Completes DS-160, pays MRV fee, and attends interview. TN and E-3 may be processed at the port of entry or consulate.

rows.title: Conduct pre-departure tax briefing
rows.description: Engage cross-border tax adviser to assess: home country exit tax obligations, US Substantial Presence Test, applicable tax treaty benefits, FBAR and FATCA disclosure requirements, and employer tax equalisation policy.

rows.title: Set up US payroll and tax withholding
rows.description: Configure employee in US payroll with federal withholding (W-4), Social Security tax, Medicare tax, and applicable state/local taxes. Confirm state of work and state of residence for withholding purposes, as they may differ.

rows.title: Complete I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification
rows.description: On or before Day 3 of employment, complete Form I-9. Employee presents List A (passport + I-94 + visa) or List B + C documents. HR retains original I-9 and must update Section 3 upon visa renewal. Non-compliance is a federal violation.

rows.title: Verify I-94 arrival record
rows.description: Employee should verify the automatically generated I-94 record at i94.cbp.dhs.gov within 48 hours of arrival. Check that the visa class, authorised stay period, and name are accurate. Errors must be corrected at the nearest CBP Deferred Inspection site.

rows.title: Apply for Social Security Number (SSN)
rows.description: Visit the local Social Security Administration office with passport, visa, I-94, and employer letter. SSN takes 2-4 weeks to arrive by mail. Without SSN, payroll, banking, and state ID applications are blocked.

rows.title: Enrol in employer health insurance
rows.description: Enrol in the employer group health plan within 30 days of hire. Select medical, dental, and vision coverage tiers. Ensure dependants are added if applicable. There is no public safety net for working-age adults on non-immigrant visas.

rows.title: Open a US bank account
rows.description: Open a US checking account at a major bank. Requires SSN (or ITIN), passport, visa, and proof of address. International employees with no US credit history may need to demonstrate income or use an expat-friendly bank (HSBC, Citibank global transfer).

rows.title: Enrol in 401(k) retirement savings plan
rows.description: Enrol in the employer 401(k) plan within the allowable window (typically 30-90 days from hire). Contribute enough to maximise employer matching. The 2024 employee contribution limit is $23,000 ($30,500 if age 50+).

rows.title: Obtain state driver's licence
rows.description: Most states recognise foreign driving licences for 3-6 months. Employee must visit the DMV to convert to a state licence using passport, visa, SSN, and proof of residence. Some states require written and/or road tests.

rows.title: Arrange housing and relocation support
rows.description: HR or relocation provider should assist with temporary furnished housing for the first 30-60 days. International employees typically lack US credit history, so a corporate guarantee letter or employer lease is recommended for the first rental.

rows.title: Set up visa expiry tracking and renewal schedule
rows.description: HR should record the employee's visa validity, I-94 expiry, and authorised stay period in a compliance tracker. Set renewal reminders at -6 months before expiry. H-1B extensions must be filed before the employee's current status expires.

rows.title: File first US federal and state tax returns
rows.description: Employee must file Form 1040 (or 1040NR if non-resident for tax purposes) by April 15 of the following year. First-year filers may have a dual-status filing obligation. Coordinate with tax adviser on treaty elections and foreign tax credits.

rows.title: Ship household goods — customs clearance
rows.description: Engage an international moving company. Household goods owned for 12+ months are duty-free. Customs clearance at US ports typically takes 3-7 business days. Restricted items include certain foods, plants, and firearms. Obtain CBP Form 3299 (Declaration for Free Entry).

rows.title: Notify home country authorities of departure
rows.description: Deregister from home country social security, tax authority, and municipal registry as applicable. Obtain social security certificate of coverage if a bilateral Social Security Agreement exists between the US and the home country (covers ~30 countries) to avoid dual contributions.

rows.title: Visa pathway confirmed and attorney retained
rows.description: Visa category determined by immigration counsel. Attorney engaged. Contingency pathway (e.g., L-1 if H-1B lottery fails) documented. Employee briefed on timeline and requirements.

rows.title: Visa petition filed / consular appointment scheduled
rows.description: For petition-based visas: I-129 filed with USCIS. For TN/E-3: consular appointment or border crossing preparation complete. All supporting documents assembled and reviewed by counsel.

rows.title: US visa stamp in passport
rows.description: Employee holds valid US work visa stamp and is cleared to travel. Visa validity dates verified. Employer has copy of I-797 and visa page for records.

rows.title: Employee arrives in the USA
rows.description: Employee crosses US border; I-94 created. I-9 completed within 3 business days. Temporary housing confirmed. First day of employment begins per work authorisation date.

rows.title: SSN received — admin unblocked
rows.description: Social Security Number card received. Payroll, banking, driving licence, and credit applications can all proceed. Benefits enrollment confirmed complete.

rows.title: Fully settled — housing, bank, insurance, licence in place
rows.description: Employee has permanent housing, active US bank account, employer health insurance, 401(k) enrollment, and a state driving licence. Tax adviser engaged for first-year filing.

rows.title: Any Country to France
rows.description: Moving to France requires a long-stay visa (VLS-TS) obtained from a French consulate in your home country before departure — you cannot enter France on a tourist visa and convert to a work visa after arrival. Within three months of arriving, you must validate your visa with the French immigration authority (OFII) and may need to attend a mandatory integration appointment. France has an outstanding public healthcare system (Sécurité Sociale) that activates automatically once your employer registers you for payroll, but there is a short gap at the start that supplemental insurance (mutuelle) covers.

extras.hr_summary: HR must initiate the French work permit or Talent Passport application well before the employee's start date, as processing by French immigration authorities (DGEF/Préfecture) typically takes 2-4 months. EU/EEA nationals require no work permit but should register at the local Préfecture within three months. Employers must declare the hire to URSSAF and set up French payroll contributions (employer charges of ~42-45% on gross salary). The French 35-hour work week, mandatory profit-sharing (intéressement/participation for companies over 50), and mandatory 25 days of paid leave are non-negotiable legal minima.

items.text: Non-EU nationals cannot enter France on a tourist visa and switch to a work permit — the long-stay visa (VLS-TS) must be issued by the French consulate in the home country before departure. Violations result in deportation and re-entry bans.
OFII validation of the VLS-TS is mandatory within 3 months of arrival. Failure to validate renders the visa invalid and the employee's stay unlawful.

French employer social charges are approximately 42-45% on top of gross salary — budget for this in the total cost of the assignment, as it significantly exceeds employer costs in many source countries.

The Talent Passport (Passeport Talent) is the preferred long-term permit for senior professionals (salary > 1.5x SMIC average), researchers, and investors — it grants a 4-year multi-entry permit and extends to family members.
French administrative processes (Préfecture appointments, OFII) are often slow and require in-person appointments — build 2-4 weeks buffer into all administrative timelines.

rows.title: Determine visa and permit category
rows.description: Assess the appropriate French permit: VLS-TS Salarié (salaried worker), Talent Passport (Passeport Talent) for senior professionals earning >1.5x average salary, Talent Passport Researcher, or EU Blue Card. EU/EEA/Swiss nationals have automatic right to work — no permit needed but registration recommended.

rows.title: Obtain employer immigration authorisation (autorisation de travail)
rows.description: For non-EU nationals, the French employer must obtain prior work authorisation from the DREETS (Direction régionale de l'économie). This takes 4-8 weeks. Required before the employee applies for the VLS-TS. Employer must provide a signed contract, proof of adequate salary, and job advertisement evidence.

rows.title: Employee applies for long-stay visa (VLS-TS) at French consulate
rows.description: Employee applies at the French consulate in their home country with the employer's autorisation de travail, signed employment contract, proof of accommodation in France, civil status documents, and photos. Processing takes 2-6 weeks. The VLS-TS is valid for the duration of the work permit (1-4 years).

rows.title: Register with OFII within 3 months of arrival
rows.description: Upon arrival in France, the employee must validate their VLS-TS with OFII (Office Français de l'Immigration et de l'Intégration) online at ofii.fr within 3 months. An OFII stamp in the passport makes the visa act as a temporary residence permit. OFII may require a medical visit and language test.

rows.title: Apply for titre de séjour (residence permit) at Préfecture
rows.description: After OFII validation, for stays longer than 1 year, apply for a multi-year titre de séjour at the local Préfecture (or via the ANEF online portal at administration-etrangers-en-france.interieur.gouv.fr). Book appointment early as slots are limited. Bring all immigration and employment documents.

rows.title: Register employee with URSSAF — French social security
rows.description: Employer must declare the new hire via the DPAE (Déclaration Préalable à l'Embauche) on net-entreprises.fr at least 8 days before the start date. This automatically registers the employee with the French social security system (Sécurité Sociale) and allocates an INSEE/NIR number.

rows.title: Obtain French INSEE social security number
rows.description: The INSEE number (numéro de sécurité sociale) is assigned automatically after URSSAF registration via payroll. A provisional number is issued first; the definitive number takes 3-6 months and is needed for healthcare reimbursements and Carte Vitale application.

rows.title: Apply for Carte Vitale (health insurance card)
rows.description: Apply for the Carte Vitale at the local CPAM (Caisse Primaire d'Assurance Maladie) or via ameli.fr with the definitive INSEE number, proof of identity, and proof of residence. The Carte Vitale enables automatic healthcare reimbursements at pharmacies and doctors. Takes 4-8 weeks to arrive.

rows.title: Enrol in employer supplemental health insurance (mutuelle)
rows.description: French law requires all employers to provide a complementary health insurance (mutuelle) covering at least 50% of the premium. Employee must be enrolled from the first day of employment. The mutuelle covers the gap between Sécurité Sociale reimbursement and actual healthcare costs.

rows.title: Open a French bank account
rows.description: Open a bank account with a major French bank (BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole) or an expat-friendly option (Compte Nickel, N26, Revolut). Requires passport, proof of address, and visa. Some banks require a French tax number. Needed for payroll receipt and direct debits.

rows.title: Register with the French tax authority (impots.gouv.fr)
rows.description: Employee must declare their arrival and register for French income tax (impôt sur le revenu). France operates a self-declaration system (déclaration annuelle) with the deadline in May. Employer deducts monthly withholding at source (prélèvement à la source) from salary.

rows.title: Arrange accommodation and domiciliation
rows.description: Secure a French address before arrival — required for visa and OFII registration. HR or relocation provider should arrange temporary furnished housing (logement meublé) for the first 30-60 days. French landlords typically require 3 months' rent deposit and a guarantor (garant).

rows.title: Register children in French schools
rows.description: Contact the local mairie to obtain a school allocation certificate (certificat d'inscription scolaire). French public education is free and mandatory from age 3. For international schools (École Active Bilingue, Lycée International), apply 3-6 months before the start date as places are limited.

rows.title: Convert or validate driving licence
rows.description: EU driving licences are valid in France without conversion. Non-EU licences: some countries have bilateral exchange agreements with France (check service-public.fr for the list). If no agreement, must pass French driving test within 1 year. Apply for exchange at local Préfecture.

rows.title: Apply for CAF housing assistance (if eligible)
rows.description: Low-to-mid income employees renting in France may be eligible for housing benefit (APL/ALS) from the CAF (Caisse d'Allocations Familiales). Apply online at caf.fr after obtaining French address and INSEE number. Expats on work permits are generally eligible after 3 months residence.

rows.title: Deregister and close home-country administrative obligations
rows.description: Notify home country tax authority, social security, and municipal registry of departure. Request a social security certificate of coverage if the home country has a bilateral social security agreement with France to avoid dual contributions.

rows.title: Ship household goods — French customs
rows.description: Household goods imported for personal use are exempt from French customs duty (franchise de droits) if the employee has resided abroad for at least 12 months and is transferring habitual residence to France. Submit customs form CERFA 10070 to French customs (douanes.gouv.fr).

rows.title: Work authorisation (autorisation de travail) granted by DREETS
rows.description: French employer receives confirmation that the work authorisation has been granted by the regional labour authority. Employee can now apply for the VLS-TS long-stay visa at the French consulate.

rows.title: VLS-TS visa issued — employee cleared to travel
rows.description: French consulate issues the long-stay visa (VLS-TS) in the employee's passport. Employee is authorised to travel to France and begin employment. Visa validity dates checked and OFII validation reminder set.

rows.title: Employee arrives in France and DPAE filed
rows.description: Employee arrives in France. Employer has filed the DPAE with URSSAF before day one. Employment contract signed. Mutuelle (supplemental insurance) activated from day one.

rows.title: OFII visa validation completed
rows.description: Employee has completed OFII online validation and received OFII stamp in passport. Residence status is lawful. INSEE provisional social security number received.

rows.title: French bank account open and payroll active
rows.description: Bank account opened and linked to payroll. Employee receiving salary in France. Tax withholding at source (prélèvement à la source) active.

rows.title: Carte Vitale received — healthcare fully active
rows.description: Definitive INSEE number received and Carte Vitale issued. Employee can now receive automatic reimbursements for healthcare costs through Sécurité Sociale and supplemental mutuelle.

rows.title: Multi-year titre de séjour obtained
rows.description: Préfecture or ANEF portal has issued the multi-year residence permit (titre de séjour). Employee is fully documented for a multi-year stay in France.

rows.title: USA to France
rows.description: As an American relocating to France, you will need a long-stay visa (VLS-TS) from the French consulate before departure — the most common category for company-sponsored employees is the Talent Passport (Passeport Talent), which is well-suited for senior professionals. France has an exceptional public healthcare system that covers you automatically once you begin employment. However, as a US citizen, you will remain subject to US worldwide income tax reporting and must file US tax returns every year regardless of where you live, making cross-border tax planning essential.

extras.hr_summary: HR must apply for the French work authorisation (autorisation de travail) at least 14-18 weeks before the move, as the DREETS processing time combined with the French consulate visa appointment can take 3-4 months. For senior hires, the Talent Passport offers a streamlined 4-year permit that is significantly more efficient than the standard salarié permit. HR must also manage the payroll transition, as French employer social charges (42-45%) represent a significant cost uplift over the US, and the mandatory 35-hour week, 25 days of paid leave, and profit-sharing obligations must be built into the employment contract.

items.text: US citizens must file US federal tax returns and FBAR (FinCEN 114) every year regardless of French residence — failure to comply with FATCA and FBAR carries severe penalties ($10,000+ per violation). Engage a US-France dual-tax specialist before departure.

The French VLS-TS must be obtained at the French consulate in the USA before departure — Americans cannot convert a tourist entry to a work permit while inside France. Most French consulates in the US require an in-person appointment (New York, Los Angeles, Washington DC).
OFII validation of the VLS-TS must be completed within 3 months of first arrival in France — this step is mandatory and missing the deadline invalidates the visa.

French employment law is significantly more protective of employees than US at-will employment: minimum notice periods, mandatory severance, works council consultation for restructuring, and strict probation (période d'essai) rules all apply from day one.

US-sourced retirement funds (401k, IRA) are generally not taxable in France under the France-US tax treaty (Article 18) while in France, but this must be confirmed with a tax adviser — PFIC rules and French reporting obligations for US accounts (impôts Form 3916) still apply.

French social charges (cotisations sociales) of approximately 22-25% of gross salary are deducted from the employee's pay — take-home pay will appear significantly lower than a comparable US gross salary.

rows.title: Determine French visa and permit category
rows.description: For most US professionals, the Talent Passport (Passeport Talent — Salarié qualifié) is recommended: requires salary >1.5x average French wage (approximately €43,000/year in 2024) and grants a 4-year permit. Standard VLS-TS Salarié is the alternative. Engage a French immigration adviser to confirm.

rows.title: Obtain French work authorisation (autorisation de travail) from DREETS
rows.description: Employer submits work authorisation request to the DREETS (regional labour authority) via the employer portal. Processing takes 4-8 weeks. Must demonstrate that the role could not be filled by an EU/EEA candidate (labour market test). Talent Passport route is exempt from the labour market test.

rows.title: Employee schedules and attends French consulate appointment (USA)
rows.description: Employee applies for VLS-TS / Talent Passport visa at the French consulate in their US city (New York, Washington DC, Los Angeles, Houston, Miami, Chicago). Appointment booking via france-visas.gouv.fr. Bring: passport, work authorisation approval, signed contract, proof of accommodation, civil status documents.

rows.title: Engage US-France cross-border tax specialist
rows.description: As a US citizen, the employee must file US taxes for life regardless of country of residence. Engage a CPA or tax adviser specialising in US expats before departure. Assess: Foreign Earned Income Exclusion (FEIE, Form 2555, up to $126,500 in 2024), Foreign Tax Credit (Form 1116), FBAR/FATCA obligations, French pension reporting.

rows.title: Review US bank and investment account reporting obligations
rows.description: Identify all US financial accounts. US citizens with foreign financial accounts exceeding $10,000 at any point in the year must file FBAR (FinCEN 114) by April 15. French bank accounts and investment accounts must also be reported on IRS Form 8938 (FATCA) if thresholds are met. Set up annual reporting reminders.

rows.title: File DPAE with URSSAF before first day of employment
rows.description: Employer must file the Déclaration Préalable à l'Embauche (DPAE) on net-entreprises.fr at least 8 days before the employee's first day. This registers the employee with French social security (Sécurité Sociale) and triggers INSEE number assignment.

rows.title: Validate VLS-TS with OFII within 3 months of arrival
rows.description: Employee registers VLS-TS validation online at ofii.fr within 3 months of arriving in France. OFII may schedule a medical appointment and an integration interview. Upon completion, the passport receives an OFII stamp that acts as a temporary titre de séjour.

rows.title: Open a French bank account
rows.description: Open an account with a French bank (BNP Paribas, Crédit Agricole, Société Générale) or expat-friendly digital bank (N26, Revolut, Wise). Bring passport, visa, and proof of French address. Some US citizens face difficulty with French banks due to FATCA compliance costs — Compte Nickel and online banks tend to be more accommodating.

rows.title: Enrol in employer mutuelle (supplemental health insurance)
rows.description: French law mandates employer-provided complemental health insurance (mutuelle) for all employees. Enrolment is automatic from day one. The mutuelle covers the portion of healthcare costs not reimbursed by Sécurité Sociale (typically 20-40% depending on service).

rows.title: Apply for Carte Vitale (French health insurance card)
rows.description: Apply at local CPAM or via ameli.fr once the definitive INSEE number is received (3-6 months after payroll registration). The Carte Vitale enables automatic electronic reimbursements for all covered healthcare costs. Until it arrives, keep paper reimbursement request forms (feuille de soins).

rows.title: Register for French income tax at impots.gouv.fr
rows.description: Create a personal tax account on impots.gouv.fr and declare French residence. France applies monthly withholding at source (prélèvement à la source) on salary. Employee must file annual déclaration de revenus by May of the following year. First-year filers may receive a provisional rate from the employer.

rows.title: Convert US driving licence to French licence (if required)
rows.description: The USA does not have a bilateral driving licence exchange agreement at the federal level with France; however, several US states (New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Michigan, South Carolina) have individual agreements. If the employee's state is not listed, they must pass the French driving theory test (code de la route) within 12 months. Check the current list at service-public.fr.

rows.title: Arrange French accommodation and tenant's insurance
rows.description: Secure a furnished apartment (meublé) for the first 30-60 days. French landlords require: last 3 payslips (or employer letter), proof of identity, bank account (RIB), and a guarantor (garant). Home contents insurance (assurance habitation) is mandatory by law for all French tenants.

rows.title: Apply for multi-year titre de séjour (residence permit)
rows.description: For stays longer than the initial VLS-TS validity, apply for a multi-year titre de séjour at the Préfecture or via the ANEF online portal within the 2 months before the VLS-TS expires. Talent Passport holders can apply directly for a 4-year card.

rows.title: Review US 401(k) and IRA management during French residence
rows.description: US pension accounts (401k, IRA, Roth IRA) remain US-held assets while the employee is in France. Under the France-US tax treaty (Article 18), distributions from US qualified plans are generally taxable only in the US. However, French tax authorities may require reporting via Form 3916. Coordinate with tax adviser on optimal contribution strategy.

rows.title: Enrol in French professional training account (CPF)
rows.description: French employees automatically accumulate training credits in their Compte Personnel de Formation (CPF) — approximately €500/year (up to €5,000 lifetime cap). Employee can access CPF at moncompteformation.gouv.fr to fund professional development courses recognised in France.

rows.title: Notify US authorities of foreign residence (FBAR/FATCA setup)
rows.description: Establish annual FBAR filing (FinCEN 114, due April 15) and FATCA reporting (IRS Form 8938) calendar reminders. Notify existing US financial institutions of new French address — some US brokerages restrict accounts for residents of certain countries. Review state-level tax obligations: some states (California, New York) continue to tax former residents who maintain certain connections.

rows.title: Work authorisation (autorisation de travail) received from DREETS
rows.description: French employer has received the approved work authorisation from the DREETS regional labour authority. Employee can now proceed to apply for the VLS-TS or Talent Passport at the French consulate in the USA.

rows.title: French long-stay visa (VLS-TS / Talent Passport) issued
rows.description: French consulate has affixed the VLS-TS or Talent Passport visa in the employee's US passport. Employee is cleared to travel to France. Visa validity dates and conditions verified by HR and immigration counsel.

rows.title: Employee arrives in France — DPAE filed and employment begins
rows.description: Employee arrives in France. DPAE confirmed filed with URSSAF. First day of employment on or after visa validity start. Mutuelle enrolment active. French payroll initiated.

rows.title: OFII validation complete
rows.description: VLS-TS validated online with OFII. OFII stamp in passport. Provisional INSEE social security number assigned. Employee's residence status is lawful.

rows.title: French bank account open and tax registration complete
rows.description: French bank account open and linked to payroll. Employee registered on impots.gouv.fr. Prélèvement à la source (monthly tax withholding) active. FBAR/FATCA reminder calendar established.

rows.title: Carte Vitale received — French healthcare fully operational
rows.description: Definitive INSEE number confirmed; Carte Vitale received. Employee can now access the full French healthcare system with automatic reimbursements via Sécurité Sociale and mutuelle.

rows.title: First US and French tax returns filed
rows.description: Employee has filed: US Form 1040 with Form 2555 (FEIE) or Form 1116 (FTC), FBAR (FinCEN 114), and French déclaration de revenus. Tax adviser has reviewed treaty positions and no double taxation liability remains outstanding.

rows.title: Any Country to Singapore
rows.description: Singapore is one of the world's most efficient places to relocate for work: the Employment Pass (EP) application is fully online and typically approved within 3-8 weeks. Once you arrive, you will receive your NRIC (identity card) after 60 days of continuous employment, and you will need to create a SingPass account to access all government digital services. Singapore has no capital gains tax and income tax rates are relatively low (maximum 24%), making it a highly attractive financial destination for international professionals.

extras.hr_summary: HR must apply for the Employment Pass via the MOM myMOM Portal well in advance, as the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) requires the role to be advertised on the MyCareersFuture.sg portal for at least 14 days before EP applications can be submitted for most roles. The minimum qualifying salary for EP is S$5,000 for most sectors (S$5,500 for financial services), with higher thresholds for older applicants under the COMPASS points framework introduced in 2023. Employers are legally responsible for the employee's conduct and repatriation costs if the EP is revoked.

items.text: Fair Consideration Framework (FCF): the role must be advertised on MyCareersFuture.sg for at least 14 calendar days before filing the EP application. Failure to do so will cause the EP application to be rejected. Certain roles (salary >S$22,500/month) are exempt.

COMPASS (Complementarity Assessment Framework) points system for EP: applicants must score ≥40 points across salary, qualifications, diversity, and support for local employment. Score below 40 = automatic rejection. Use MOM's online COMPASS calculator before applying.

CPF (Central Provident Fund) contributions are NOT required for EP holders — only for Singapore citizens and Permanent Residents. However, if the employee later converts to PR status, CPF obligations begin immediately and retroactive contributions are not allowed.

EP holders must not begin work in Singapore before the EP is approved and the pass card is physically issued or In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter is held. Working without a valid EP is a criminal offence under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act.

Tax residency: employees present in Singapore for ≥183 days in a tax year are taxed as residents (progressive rates 0-24%). Those present <183 days are taxed at a flat 15% or the resident rate, whichever is higher. The Singapore tax year is January-December.

rows.title: Conduct COMPASS pre-assessment for Employment Pass
rows.description: Use the MOM COMPASS self-assessment calculator at mom.gov.sg to confirm the candidate scores ≥40 points before investing in the EP application. Key criteria: salary benchmarking vs. local peers (C1), qualifications (C2), diversity (C3), support for local employment (C4), and strategic economic priorities (C5, bonus). Adjust salary or role if needed to meet the threshold.

rows.title: Advertise role on MyCareersFuture.sg for 14 days (FCF requirement)
rows.description: Post the job on MyCareersFuture.sg for a minimum of 14 calendar days. The posting must describe the role, salary range, and qualifications. Document the application outcomes to demonstrate fair consideration of Singaporean candidates. Retain records for at least 2 years. Roles paying >S$22,500/month are exempt.

rows.title: Apply for Employment Pass via myMOM Portal
rows.description: Submit the EP application via the MOM myMOM Portal (ep.mom.gov.sg). Required documents: employee's passport, educational qualifications, employment contract, and employer ACRA registration. Processing time: 3-8 weeks for standard applications. An In-Principle Approval (IPA) letter is issued first.

rows.title: Receive EP In-Principle Approval (IPA) and arrange travel
rows.description: MOM issues the IPA letter when the EP is approved in principle. The IPA allows the employee to enter Singapore to collect the EP card. The IPA is valid for 6 months. Employee can travel to Singapore using the IPA letter as a single-entry permission if no Singapore visa is required from their nationality.

rows.title: Complete EP formalities at MOM services centre
rows.description: Upon arrival in Singapore, employee must visit a MOM Services Centre to have biometrics taken and collect the EP card. Bring IPA letter, passport, and medical insurance proof. EP card typically issued within 4-7 business days of the biometrics appointment.

rows.title: Set up SingPass digital identity
rows.description: SingPass is Singapore's national digital identity platform required for all government services. Employee registers at singpass.gov.sg using their FIN (Foreign Identification Number) from the EP card. SingPass is needed for IRAS tax filing, CPF (if applicable), MOM services, and bank account opening with some banks.

rows.title: Obtain NRIC after 60 days of continuous employment
rows.description: After 60 consecutive days of employment in Singapore, EP holders (long-term pass holders) can apply for an NRIC (National Registration Identity Card) at an ICA Service Centre. The NRIC is the primary national ID document in Singapore and is required for many local services.

rows.title: Open a Singapore bank account
rows.description: Open a bank account with DBS, OCBC, or UOB — the three major local banks. Most branches require an in-person visit with EP card, passport, and proof of residential address. Digital banks (Revolut SG, GXS Bank) may offer simpler online onboarding for EP holders. Needed for payroll receipt.

rows.title: Arrange mandatory health insurance as per MOM requirements
rows.description: Employers must provide medical insurance of at least S$15,000 per year for EP holders as a condition of the EP. Enrol the employee in the company group health plan or arrange individual coverage from day one. Keep proof of insurance available as MOM may request it.

rows.title: Register for IRAS tax as a Singapore resident
rows.description: Register on myTax Portal (mytax.iras.gov.sg) using SingPass. Singapore's tax year is January-December; the filing deadline is April 15 for electronic filing. Employer files IR8A (employee income statement) annually by March 1. First-year employees present <183 days are taxed at 15% or resident rate, whichever is higher.

rows.title: Arrange accommodation — HDB or private housing
rows.description: EP holders can rent HDB flats (public housing) or private condominiums/landed property. HDB rentals require EP with at least 6 months remaining validity. Typical rental deposits: 1 month (HDB) to 2 months (private) plus 1 month advance. HR or relocation provider should source temporary housing for the first 30 days.

rows.title: Register children in Singapore schools
rows.description: Apply for school placement via the Ministry of Education (moe.gov.sg) for Singapore citizens and PRs, or via the International School Admission process for EP holders. International schools are expensive (S$20,000-S$40,000/year) and typically have waiting lists — apply 3-6 months in advance. HR relocation package may include school fees.

rows.title: Apply for Dependent Pass (DP) or Long Term Visit Pass (LTVP) for family
rows.description: EP holders earning ≥S$6,000/month can bring a legally married spouse and unmarried children under 21 on a Dependent Pass. Apply via the myMOM Portal simultaneously with the EP. LTVP (for common-law partners, stepchildren, elderly parents) requires additional documentation.

rows.title: Understand CPF obligations and future PR conversion pathway
rows.description: EP holders are not required to contribute to CPF. However, if the employee wishes to apply for Singapore Permanent Residence (PR) after 2+ years, CPF contributions will begin retroactively from the PR approval date. Brief the employee on the PR application process and timeline expectations.

rows.title: Convert foreign driving licence to Singapore licence
rows.description: Most foreign driving licences can be converted to a Singapore Class 3/3A licence at a driving centre (BBDC, SSDC, CDC) if the home country licence is in English or accompanied by an official translation. No driving test required for most OECD country licences. EP card required for the application.

rows.title: Set up EP renewal tracker
rows.description: EP is typically issued for 2 years initially (1 year for first-time applicants in some cases). HR must track EP expiry dates and submit renewal applications at least 6 months before expiry. Renewals are subject to COMPASS re-assessment at the time of renewal.

rows.title: Deregister from home country administrative systems
rows.description: Notify home country tax authority and social security of departure and Singapore residence. Check whether a bilateral social security agreement exists between Singapore and the home country (agreements with Japan, India, Germany, Netherlands, and others). Obtain certificate of coverage if applicable.

rows.title: COMPASS pre-assessment passed and FCF advertising started
rows.description: Candidate confirmed to score ≥40 COMPASS points. Job posting live on MyCareersFuture.sg. 14-day FCF advertising window running. Earliest EP application date confirmed.

rows.title: EP application submitted to MOM
rows.description: Employment Pass application submitted via the myMOM Portal with all supporting documents. Application reference number recorded. Processing timeline: 3-8 weeks.

rows.title: EP In-Principle Approval (IPA) received
rows.description: MOM has issued the IPA letter. Employee is approved to enter Singapore and complete EP issuance. IPA valid for 6 months. Travel to Singapore arranged. Dependent Pass IPA received simultaneously if applicable.

rows.title: Employee arrives in Singapore and EP card issued
rows.description: Employee arrives in Singapore, visits MOM services centre for biometrics. EP card issued within 4-7 business days. Employee can legally commence work. Mandatory health insurance confirmed active.

rows.title: SingPass activated and bank account open
rows.description: SingPass account activated with FIN from EP card. Singapore bank account open and payroll received. Employee is administratively functional in Singapore.

rows.title: NRIC issued after 60 days
rows.description: Employee has collected NRIC from ICA after 60 consecutive days of employment. NRIC is the primary ID for Singapore. Driving licence conversion application submitted.

rows.title: Fully settled — housing, banking, insurance, NRIC in place
rows.description: Employee has permanent housing secured, Singapore bank account active, mandatory health insurance in place, NRIC received, and SingPass fully activated. EP renewal date tracked by HR.

rows.title: India to Singapore
rows.description: The India-to-Singapore corridor is one of Asia's busiest and most competitive professional migration routes. Singapore's Employment Pass (EP) is the primary pathway for Indian professionals, with a minimum qualifying salary of S$5,000 per month and a COMPASS points assessment that considers diversity metrics — meaning that employers with a high proportion of Indian nationals on their payroll may face additional scrutiny. Singapore has no capital gains tax, a relatively low maximum income tax rate of 24%, and excellent infrastructure, making it a highly desirable destination. Building local administrative foundations (SingPass, bank account, NRIC) should be prioritised in the first two weeks.

extras.hr_summary: HR must be particularly alert to the COMPASS C3 (diversity) criterion when hiring Indian nationals, as teams that are already concentrated in a single nationality may score lower and face EP rejection. The Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) advertising requirement is strictly enforced for this corridor. Indian professionals are one of the largest EP holder groups in Singapore, which has prompted MOM to apply heightened scrutiny to applications from companies with high Indian EP concentrations. HR must also note that S Pass (mid-skilled) has strict quota limits (10-15% of total workforce) and is not appropriate for most professional hires.

items.text: COMPASS C3 diversity criterion penalises employers where the candidate's nationality is already over-represented — companies with a high concentration of Indian EP holders score lower on diversity and may face automatic rejection at <40 points. Review the workforce diversity score before applying.

FCF 14-day advertising on MyCareersFuture.sg is mandatory before EP application and is strictly enforced by MOM — document all Singaporean applicants considered and reasons for non-selection. MOM audits employers for FCF compliance.

Indian nationals holding S-Pass (not EP) are subject to S Pass quota limits (10% of local workforce for services sectors, 15% for manufacturing). Exceeding the quota triggers automatic rejection. Verify quota headroom before offering an S Pass role.

Indian employees transferring money back to India should use regulated channels (bank transfers, MAS-licensed remittance operators) — Singapore has no exchange controls but Indian FEMA (Foreign Exchange Management Act) regulations impose reporting obligations on Indian residents earning abroad.

India-Singapore DTAA (Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement): Singapore-sourced income is generally not taxable in India if the employee is non-resident in India for tax purposes (spends <182 days in India in the fiscal year). Confirm non-residency status before the first Singapore tax filing.

HDB rental for Indian EP holders: some HDB estates have Non-Citizen (NC) subletting quotas — if the quota for the block is full, the landlord cannot legally rent to an EP holder. Verify NC quota availability via HDB's website before signing a tenancy agreement.

rows.title: Run COMPASS assessment and check workforce diversity score
rows.description: Before initiating the EP process, run the MOM COMPASS calculator at mom.gov.sg/eservices/compass. Pay particular attention to the C3 (diversity) criterion — if the hiring company's workforce already has a high proportion of Indian nationals, the candidate may not pass the ≥40 point threshold. Explore salary uplift or other COMPASS strategies if score is borderline.

rows.title: Advertise role on MyCareersFuture.sg for 14 days (FCF)
rows.description: Post the open role on MyCareersFuture.sg for at least 14 calendar days. Document every Singaporean/PR applicant considered and provide specific reasons for non-selection (experience gap, qualifications, etc.). MOM can and does audit FCF compliance. Retain all documentation for 2 years. Roles paying >S$22,500/month are FCF-exempt.

rows.title: Confirm Indian educational credentials for EP application
rows.description: Indian university degrees must be verifiable — MOM accepts credentials from recognised institutions. Degrees from Tier 1 Indian universities (IITs, IIMs, NITs, leading private universities) attract higher COMPASS C2 score. Ensure degree certificates and transcripts are original or notarised copies. If credentials are from an unrecognised institution, COMPASS points will not be awarded for C2.

rows.title: Submit EP application via myMOM Portal
rows.description: File the EP application via ep.mom.gov.sg. Required: employee's Indian passport (valid ≥6 months beyond intended stay), degree certificates, employment contract at the qualifying salary (≥S$5,000, S$5,500 for financial sector), and employer ACRA registration. Standard processing: 3-8 weeks. Apply for Dependent Pass simultaneously if applicable (EP holder must earn ≥S$6,000).

rows.title: Receive EP In-Principle Approval (IPA) and complete Indian pre-departure steps
rows.description: Once IPA is received, arrange travel to Singapore. Indian nationals do not require a tourist visa for Singapore (up to 30 days). Notify Indian income tax authority (e-filing portal) of change of residence status. Check NPS/EPFO account status — EPFO funds can be withdrawn upon emigration after satisfying conditions.

rows.title: Complete EP issuance at MOM Services Centre upon arrival
rows.description: Employee visits an MOM Services Centre within the first week of arrival to submit biometrics and collect the EP card. Bring IPA letter, Indian passport, and proof of Singapore residential address. EP card issued within 4-7 business days. Do not commence work until EP card is in hand or IPA authorises commencement.

rows.title: Register for SingPass using FIN from EP card
rows.description: Create a SingPass account at singpass.gov.sg using the FIN (Foreign Identification Number) printed on the EP card. SingPass is the gateway to all Singapore government digital services: IRAS tax filing, MOM services, CPF (if/when applicable), and health records. Activate SingPass Face Verification for full service access.

rows.title: Open Singapore bank account
rows.description: Open a Singapore bank account at DBS, OCBC, or UOB. Most Indian employees open a DBS account (strong India diaspora services, POSB digital banking). Bring EP card, Indian passport, and proof of Singapore address. Digital onboarding available for DBS via MyInfo (SingPass linked). Essential for salary receipt and bill payments.

rows.title: Establish low-cost India remittance channel
rows.description: Set up a regulated remittance channel for sending money to India (DBS Remit, OCBC Global Transfers, Wise, or MAS-licensed remittance operators such as Western Union or InstaReM). Compare rates — Wise is typically competitive. Indian FEMA reporting: amounts remitted are not capped, but Indian recipients with NRE/NRO accounts must comply with RBI rules.

rows.title: Confirm non-resident status with Indian tax authority
rows.description: An Indian who stays outside India for ≥182 days in a financial year (April-March) becomes a Non-Resident Indian (NRI). NRIs are taxed in India only on India-sourced income. Update residential status on the Indian e-filing portal (incometax.gov.in) to NRI. Notify Indian banks to convert accounts to NRE (tax-free repatriation) or NRO (for India-sourced income) status.

rows.title: Register for Singapore IRAS income tax
rows.description: Register on myTax Portal using SingPass. Singapore's filing deadline is April 15 for e-filing. Employer submits IR8A by March 1. Indian nationals in Singapore for their first year should calculate Singapore tax residency (≥183 days = resident rates, 0-24%). The India-Singapore DTAA may reduce withholding on certain Singapore-sourced income if it is also remitted to India.

rows.title: Enrol in employer mandatory health insurance
rows.description: Employers must provide a minimum S$15,000/year medical insurance for all EP holders as an MOM licensing condition. Enrol the employee in the company group health plan from day one. Confirm that the plan covers hospitalisation — Singapore's private hospital costs are high (S$1,000-S$5,000/night for a private room).

rows.title: Secure Singapore accommodation — verify HDB NC quota
rows.description: If renting an HDB flat, verify the Non-Citizen (NC) subletting quota for the block and unit at hdb.gov.sg before signing. If the NC quota is full, the landlord cannot legally sublet to an EP holder. Private condominiums have no such restriction. Typical rental: S$2,500-S$4,000/month for an HDB 3-room flat; S$3,500-S$7,000 for a private 1BR condo.

rows.title: Obtain NRIC after 60 days of continuous employment
rows.description: After 60 consecutive days of employment in Singapore, visit an ICA Service Centre with EP card and passport to apply for the NRIC. The NRIC is Singapore's primary identity document and is required for local contracts, rental agreements, and some bank services.

rows.title: Apply for Dependent Pass for family members
rows.description: EP holders earning ≥S$6,000/month can sponsor a spouse and unmarried children under 21 on a Dependent Pass (DP). Apply via myMOM Portal simultaneously with the EP. DP holders can apply for a Letter of Consent (LOC) to work in Singapore without needing a separate EP. Parents and in-laws can apply for a Long Term Visit Pass (LTVP) with additional documentation.

rows.title: Convert Indian driving licence to Singapore licence
rows.description: Indian driving licences can be converted to a Singapore driving licence at a Singapore driving centre (BBDC, SSDC, or CDC) without taking a full driving test, subject to passing a Basic Theory Test (BTT). Visit the Driving Centres with Indian driving licence, EP card, and passport. Fee approximately S$50-S$100.

rows.title: Review Indian PF/EPFO and NPS accounts
rows.description: Indian employees emigrating permanently can withdraw EPFO (Employee Provident Fund) balances after 2 months of unemployment (for emigration purposes). NPS (National Pension System) accounts continue to earn returns and can be maintained as NRI. Nominate beneficiaries and update contact details for both accounts.

rows.title: Track EP renewal — COMPASS will re-apply at renewal
rows.description: EP renewal applications are subject to the full COMPASS assessment at the time of renewal, based on updated salary and workforce diversity data. HR must track EP expiry 6 months in advance and reassess COMPASS score before filing the renewal. Salary increments between initial EP and renewal improve the C1 score.

rows.title: COMPASS score confirmed ≥40 and FCF advertising started
rows.description: COMPASS pre-assessment confirms candidate will meet the 40-point threshold. MyCareersFuture.sg job posting live. 14-day FCF advertising window underway. Diversity risk flagged and documented if applicable.

rows.title: EP application submitted to MOM
rows.description: Employment Pass application submitted via myMOM Portal with all Indian credential documents, employment contract, and ACRA employer details. Dependent Pass applications filed simultaneously. Processing time 3-8 weeks.

rows.title: IPA received — Singapore travel arranged
rows.description: MOM has issued the In-Principle Approval. Indian employees do not need a separate entry visa for Singapore. Flight and temporary accommodation booked. Indian NRI status, EPFO, and bank conversion steps initiated.

rows.title: Employee arrives in Singapore and EP card issued
rows.description: Employee arrives in Singapore, completes MOM biometrics, EP card issued within 7 business days. Mandatory health insurance active. First day of legal employment confirmed.

rows.title: SingPass active, bank account open, payroll live
rows.description: SingPass registered with FIN from EP card. Singapore bank account (DBS/OCBC/UOB) open. First salary received in Singapore. India remittance channel established. Indian bank accounts converted to NRE/NRO.

rows.title: Indian NRI tax status confirmed and India IRAS filing set up
rows.description: Indian e-filing portal updated to NRI status. India-Singapore DTAA position documented by tax adviser. Singapore IRAS account set up on myTax Portal. NRIC application submitted.

rows.title: Fully settled — NRIC, driving licence, school enrolment complete
rows.description: NRIC received, Singapore driving licence obtained, children enrolled in school, permanent accommodation secured. EP renewal date tracked by HR with COMPASS re-assessment schedule in place.

rows.description: Register the address at the local Bürgeramt within 14 days of moving in — this triggers issuance of the tax ID.

rows.title: Enrol children in school or Kita
