rows.description: A general relocation path to Germany covering both EU and non-EU employees. EU citizens move freely; non-EU citizens need a visa and residence permit. Universal non-obvious steps are the 14-day Anmeldung deadline, mandatory health insurance, and obtaining the tax ID before the first payroll run.

rows.title: Determine immigration route
rows.description: Establish whether the employee needs a visa/permit (non-EU) or moves under free movement (EU) and finalise the contract.

rows.title: Complete immigration paperwork
rows.description: Non-EU employees apply for the visa; EU employees confirm ID and right to work.

rows.description: Secure accommodation with landlord confirmation and select German health insurance.

rows.title: Arrival in Germany
rows.description: Employee arrives and begins the settling-in administrative sequence.

rows.title: Anmeldung within 14 days
rows.description: Register the address at the Bürgeramt within 14 days; non-EU employees also book the residence-permit appointment.

rows.title: Tax ID, bank account & payroll live
rows.description: Receive the tax ID, open a bank account, and confirm payroll and social security registration.

rows.title: Finalise settling-in
rows.description: Complete dependents, schooling, utilities, and confirm compliance obligations are closed.

rows.title: Determine visa vs free-movement route
rows.description: Classify the employee as EU (free movement) or non-EU (visa/permit required) and plan lead times accordingly.

rows.title: Apply for entry visa (non-EU employees)

rows.description: Arrange accommodation and obtain the landlord confirmation required for the Anmeldung.

rows.title: Register address (Anmeldung) at the Bürgeramt
rows.description: Register within 14 days of moving in; this legal obligation triggers the tax ID and is needed for any permit.

rows.title: Apply for residence permit (non-EU employees)
rows.description: Non-EU employees convert their entry visa to a residence permit/EU Blue Card at the Ausländerbehörde.

rows.title: Enrol in German health insurance

rows.title: Complete employer payroll registration
rows.description: Register the employee in German payroll with tax ID, tax class, and social security data.
rows.source_name: Make it in Germany (German Federal Government)

rows.title: Obtain social security number
rows.description: The social security number is issued via the pension insurer once employment and health insurance are registered.

rows.title: Open a German bank account (Girokonto)
rows.description: Open a current account for salary; most banks require the Anmeldung confirmation and valid ID.
rows.source_name: Make it in Germany (German Federal Government)

rows.title: Assess social security coordination
rows.description: Determine whether A1/certificate of coverage applies for EU postings or bilateral totalization for non-EU origins.
rows.source_name: DVKA (German Liaison Agency for Health Insurance Abroad)

rows.title: Arrange dependent immigration and cover
rows.description: Arrange family reunion visas (non-EU) or free-movement registration (EU) and dependent health insurance.

rows.title: Register for broadcasting fee (Rundfunkbeitrag)
rows.description: Register the household for the mandatory broadcasting licence fee after the Anmeldung.

rows.title: Enrol children in school or Kita

rows.title: Set up utilities and internet
rows.description: Arrange electricity, heating, and internet contracts for the new residence.

rows.title: Obtain Meldebescheinigung and retain records
rows.description: Obtain the registration certificate and keep records for administrative and future permanent-residence purposes.

rows.title: Receive residence card (Zairyu card) on arrival
rows.description: Foreign nationals with a mid/long-term status of residence are issued a residence card (Zairyu card) at the airport on entry; carry it at all times.

rows.title: Register residence at municipal office (jumin toroku)
rows.description: Register your address at the local city/ward office within 14 days of moving in to obtain a certificate of residence (juminhyo).
rows.source_name: Ministry of Justice (MOJ) / Immigration Services Agency

rows.title: Obtain My Number (Individual Number)
rows.description: After residence registration, a My Number notification is sent to your registered address; it is required for employment, tax, and social insurance.
rows.source_name: My Number Card (Digital Agency, Government of Japan)

rows.title: Apply for My Number Card
rows.description: Apply for the physical My Number Card, which serves as official photo ID and enables online administrative services.
rows.source_name: My Number Card (Digital Agency, Government of Japan)

rows.title: Enrol in Employees' Health Insurance / National Health Insurance
rows.description: Company employees enrol in employees' health insurance (Shakai Hoken) via the employer; others enrol in National Health Insurance at the municipal office.
rows.source_name: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)

rows.title: Enrol in pension (Employees' Pension / National Pension)
rows.description: Employees are enrolled in the Employees' Pension Insurance via their employer; residents not covered enrol in the National Pension.

rows.title: Open a Japanese bank account
rows.description: Open a bank account for salary; most banks require the residence card, My Number, and often a residence period of 6 months (some allow earlier with employer letter).
rows.source_name: Japan Post Bank / financial regulator guidance
rows.review_reason: bank-specific requirements vary; verify at corridor sign-off

rows.title: Obtain a personal seal (hanko/inkan) and register it
rows.description: A personal seal is commonly required for contracts and some bank/administrative processes; register it at the municipal office if an official seal (jitsuin) is needed.

rows.title: Set up a mobile phone contract
rows.description: A local mobile number is often required for banking and services; carriers require the residence card and often a Japanese bank account or credit card.
rows.source_name: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC)

rows.title: Register for resident tax (juminzei) awareness
rows.description: Resident tax is levied based on the previous year's income and prior-year residence; understand first-year exemptions and payment timing.

rows.title: Understand income tax withholding (gensen choshu)
rows.description: Employers withhold income tax at source and perform a year-end adjustment (nenmatsu chosei); confirm this with HR.

rows.title: Enrol children in local school
rows.description: Foreign children can attend Japanese public schools; apply through the municipal board of education, or arrange international school placement.

rows.title: Register change of address on residence card
rows.description: Report any change of residence to the municipal office within 14 days so it is recorded on the residence card.

rows.title: Obtain re-entry permit awareness for travel
rows.description: Mid/long-term residents can use special re-entry permission for trips under 1 year; understand the rules before leaving Japan.

rows.title: Notify of employment change to Immigration
rows.description: Workers with work-based status must notify the Immigration Services Agency within 14 days of changes to their employer/contract.

rows.title: Register for long-term care insurance (age 40+)
rows.description: Residents aged 40 and over pay long-term care insurance (kaigo hoken) alongside health insurance premiums.
rows.source_name: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)

rows.title: Exchange foreign driving licence (gaimen kirikae)
rows.description: Convert a foreign driving licence to a Japanese licence via the prefectural licence centre; some countries require a knowledge/skills test.

rows.title: Register with home-country embassy (optional)
rows.description: Register with your home-country embassy or consulate in Japan for consular support and voting where applicable.

rows.title: Determine status of residence & apply for COE
rows.description: Confirm the correct work status of residence and file the Certificate of Eligibility application in Japan.

rows.title: COE issued & visa applied at embassy
rows.description: Once the COE is issued, the employee applies for the visa at the Japanese embassy/consulate in their country.

rows.title: Housing & pre-departure arranged

rows.title: My Number, bank & payroll live

rows.title: Finalise settling-in

rows.title: Determine correct status of residence
rows.description: Identify the appropriate work status of residence (e.g. Engineer/Specialist in Humanities/International Services, Intra-company Transferee).

rows.title: File Certificate of Eligibility (COE) application
rows.description: The employer (or agent) files the COE application at the regional immigration bureau; this is a prerequisite to the visa.

rows.title: Apply for work visa at Japanese embassy
rows.description: Once the COE is issued, the employee applies for the visa at the Japanese embassy/consulate in their home country.

rows.title: Prepare employment contract and supporting documents
rows.description: Provide the employment contract, company documents, and evidence of qualifications required for the COE and visa.

rows.title: Secure accommodation in Japan
rows.description: Arrange housing; rentals often require a guarantor or guarantor company and initial key-money/deposit payments.

rows.title: Receive residence card on arrival
rows.description: Collect the residence card (Zairyu card) at the designated port of entry and carry it at all times.

rows.title: Register residence at municipal office within 14 days
rows.description: Register the address at the city/ward office within 14 days of moving in to obtain the juminhyo.

rows.title: Enrol in pension insurance
rows.description: Enrol in Employees' Pension Insurance via the employer; understand totalization agreements to avoid double contributions.

rows.title: Complete employer payroll and withholding setup

rows.title: Open a Japanese bank account
rows.description: Open a bank account for salary; requirements include the residence card and My Number, with some banks requiring 6 months' residence.

rows.title: Understand resident tax (juminzei) timing
rows.description: Resident tax is based on prior-year income and residence as of 1 January; first-year arrivals are often exempt.

rows.title: Arrange dependent (Dependent) visas

rows.title: Enrol children in school

rows.title: Set up mobile phone and utilities

rows.title: Notify Immigration of any employment changes
rows.description: Workers must notify the Immigration Services Agency within 14 days of changes to employer or contract.
